articles.title: Altman Describes Three Endgames for AI, Including One Where a Single Firm ‘Melts Everyone Else’s GPUs’
articles.text:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman last week told employees about three proposals the industry has discussed for how to safely develop AI, a stark framing that comes just as the Trump administration sets up its first system for policing “superintelligence” developers like OpenAI.
One path involved developing an international organization, similar to the International Atomic Energy Agency, that would enforce safety standards, a scenario Altman appeared to support, said two people with knowledge of the comments. Another option would involve merging all of the AI labs into a single body to develop new AI safely.

articles.title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22507v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks. To comprehensively measure collaboration, REALCLI builds a five-dimensional framework, operationalized into 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates. REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI-EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI-COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information, corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions. Evaluations reveal profound capability gaps in frontier agents: the best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and when evaluated by the joint collaboration score ($J_{\mathrm{collab}}$), the peak performance reaches merely 37.6%. These results show that task effectiveness diverges sharply from collaboration quality, with models consistently struggling in steerability, trust calibration, and safety boundary management. REALCLI provides a rigorous, reproducible foundation for measuring and advancing collaborative CLI agents.

articles.title: 王志宇：拓竹卷C，轻量智造为何押注小B丨未来创新50人
articles.text:
三一、华为、创想、安克履历加持，王志宇二次创业绕开C端。
作者丨姚单
编辑丨董子博
七月，雷峰网·鲸犀来到了轻量智造位于深圳西丽的新办公室。60 多个工位坐得满满当当，物业那层空着的三四百平方米，也被这家公司临时占了过来。而这间办公室，他们今年 4 月才从龙华观澜搬来。办公区这边坐不下人，产线那一头却已经独自撑起一栋楼。今年 7 月，公司已有 50 台设备发货、200 台在产线爬坡，制造由欣旺达负责，日产能 400 台。为了配合生产，欣旺达甚至专门为它腾出了一栋新楼。在 3D 打印赛道，这样的扩张节奏并不常见。轻量智造成立于 2025 年 4 月，一年多时间，团队从零长到 60 余人，连续完成多轮融资——海欣资本、南山战新投、南山资本、卓源亚洲、朗翰创投先后入局。相比纯消费投资逻辑，这批资方更熟悉制造业，也更容易看到轻量智造这条路线背后的想象空间。创始人王志宇，先后任职于三一重工、华为、创想三维、安克。王志宇是机械设计制造专业出身，先在三一重工，后来又去了华为做软件研发；2019 年，他创业做过手持喷墨打印笔——这段经历，后来也支撑了安克全彩 3D 打印的路线验证。2021 年他来到安克，正式开始负责 3D 打印机，用 12 个月做完了 AnkerMake M5，众筹比拓竹早两个月上线，880 万美元的成绩也比拓竹高出不少。当年，M5 全年营收约 6000 万；第二年，这个数字就冲到了 1.2 个亿；第三年时，营收则逼近两亿人民币。这些经历给他攒下了三样东西：手机大厂的软硬件与供应链功底，喷墨打印的技术积累，以及对 C 端市场的判断。2025 年入局 3D 打印，一些人认为轻量智造是一头扎进了红海市场。但对于王志宇来说，他想服务的不是“发烧友”，而是一个一个的“农场”。这里说的“农场”，指的是提供 3D 打印服务的商家。他们通常规模不小，对打印机成本、效率、损耗等指标也更加敏感。王志宇观察，在 500 亿人民币的 3D 打印消费市场里，打印“农场”的占比几乎达到了 20%，有 100 亿人民币的空间。普通老百姓的家用打印机，更多只是“玩具”，大家更关注打印机的“玩具属性”；而轻量智造却更关注“工具属性”，聚焦在把工具做好，让打印机替代一部分传统的制造业，解决真正的问题。同样是打印，场景不同，批量需求就不同。在王志宇看来，拓竹要做拓圈、做小白用户，这是好事——全世界都知道 3D 打印机好玩。但真要批量制造，逻辑就完全是另一回事。这也划定了轻量智造的位置：阶段性不做 ToC，主攻小 B。本质上，过去 20-30 万元设备才能做到的事情，轻量智造想用 ToC 机器的成本来完成。“（我们的）打印效率比拓竹快 4 倍，换颜色比快造 U1 快 5 倍。”王志宇说道。不过，速度快只是第一步。多头同时打印，能否兼顾精度与稳定性？几千元的设备，真能承担起批量制造的任务吗？以下是与轻量智造创始人王志宇的对话，雷峰网·鲸犀在不变原意的基础上做了编辑和调整。01
归来仍是“少年”
雷峰网·鲸犀：毕业后，你去了三一重工，在里面做了什么？王志宇：就做软件。我大学学的是机械，不过在学校时也和同学一起参加过计算机大赛。后来我在三一重工做软件，差不多做了三年。当时我所在的部门叫智能研究院，主要做工程机械的远程遥控。2006 年就做这类产品，其实很早——那时候还没有物联网概念。互联网还没跑起来，就搞物联网，是比较超前的。IoT 这个概念其实是到 2015 年之后才讲得比较多。
雷峰网·鲸犀：后来就去了武汉？王志宇：没错，当时好多三一前同事都去了武汉华为，我就跟他们一起去了。我在那里待了差不多两年。我在华为就做手机。2009 年，智能手机还没有真正普及，但是安卓这个概念已经在少数手机公司里面有了。我算是最早一批做安卓手机的人。我在华为的时候，也是最肯拼的那拨人：一个任务干一遍干不好，那就干两遍；两遍干不好，那就干三遍。老板就认为我可以创造一些价值，所以他会给我更多机会。在中国，任何一个老板只要看到有个人非常拼，他都会多给点机会。
雷峰网·鲸犀：但之后你很快做了一个手持喷墨笔——怎么想到跨界创业的？王志宇：最开始我们是做一个外包项目：有个电商公司老板说，你帮我做个定制项目，我付 30 万开发费。我们给他做这个项目，做得比较成功。这个老板就说要不这样——我们合伙开一家，你们负责研发，我负责亚马逊的销售。2019 年，我跟两个华为同事正式出来创业，做打印机——不是 3D 打印机，而是平面喷墨打印机。我们做过一个像马克笔这么小的打印机，里面是一个喷头，可以喷墨，这样喷着扫过去，就能打出打印机那样的字。特别小，是一种便携的打印机。我们创业一年左右，那个产品总共卖了差不多 2000 多万人民币，一共做了两代产品；当时也做了一个众筹，没什么经验，只众筹了 10 多万美金。
雷峰网·鲸犀：当时想过对外融资吗？王志宇：当时也没有去走这条路，刚好 2020 年疫情来了，也没有那么多时间和机会去想。但说实话，2000 万营收对于一个科技公司，如果你真的想要招人，其实是不可持续的——算下来毛利可能就几百万，一年下来几百万，一个月就只有几十万的开销。
雷峰网·鲸犀：第一段创业踩过哪些坑？王志宇：我本来是工程师出身，第一次创业发现工程师的经验不够用——创业你首先要看懂市场、看懂用户，这些都是我当时比较欠缺的。所以我后来创业一段时间，感觉也没那么顺利，反而觉得加入一家公司重新管研发好像也还不错。带着这样一个想法，我决定倒回去再做研发，结果阴差阳错进了一个非常好的赛道。那时候创想三维在行业里发展特别好、大规模扩招，我是在那个时候加入创想三维。我在创想三维待的时间不长，但正是通过创想三维，我才进入 3D 打印这个行业。
雷峰网·鲸犀：后来在什么契机下加入安克？王志宇：我有一个华为前同事，以前是酷派的，他认识安克现任副总裁 Frank（酷派前高管）。2021 年，我第一次跟 Frank 见面，就拿了我以前创业做的喷墨打印原型机给他看。当时我提了一些想法：要不我们把彩色加上去，做全彩的 3D 打印机。后来，我又通过 Frank 结识了阳萌。和阳萌聊过之后，我觉得这是一个不错的机会。当时安克计划成立一家新公司做 3D 打印机，于是我便从创想三维离职，加入安克，从 2021 年一直干到 2024 年。
雷峰网·鲸犀：安克的体系，你觉得哪一点是最核心、影响你最深的？王志宇：如果今天让我总结安克这段经历，我会觉得安克这本“书”，真正读得深的人少之又少，而我算是读得相当深的一个。为什么呢？第一，我进去之前的知识体系和安克反差特别大。我一直做技术，从来没接触过市场、营销，也没接触过品牌逻辑，所以刚进去时感受到非常多反差。我当时刚进去，就说要搞懂安克这家公司，你得先搞懂安克老板；要搞懂老板，就得知道他从哪里来——他是从谷歌回来的。于是我去找了一本叫《谷歌方法论》的书——还真有这本书，网上也有很多视频和有声书。我确实认真看了，还反复听了很多遍。沿着谷歌方法论这些书看下去，我们发现，它们总结的大部分方法论都有一种“我要为这个社会做贡献”的底色，里面多次讲到“美国梦”。谷歌的价值观，某种意义上就是把美国文化做到极致：假设我是一个工程师，我会帮助公司创造尽可能大的价值，也会分享给周围的同事；如果有一天我真的被淘汰了，我也应该向你学习。它非常讲结果、讲奉献、非常大度，而这种大度里，实际上带一点点宗教色彩。
雷峰网·鲸犀：影响在什么地方？王志宇：我经常跟别人讲：我借助安克这扇窗，真正看懂了海外的事。我们现在再去跟海外的人交流，会理解他们为什么要这么干；而且我们也能够揣测到他们的一些价值观和判断，做出更多符合他们价值观的产品。
雷峰网·鲸犀：出来之后为什么还继续做 3D 打印？王志宇：我们现在就基本上不再走消费者路线了。以前，我也想过去走拓竹那条路，但纯消费级里面卷成一团麻，竞争异常激烈、收益十分有限，更多的是巨头之间不计成本的拼杀，价格和各方面都是白热化的竞争。于是我们就转变了赛道。我们正式转变方向之前，见了上百个投资人。现在，我们主要是针对小 B、SMB 这样的群体，不再做纯消费级的家用市场，就算要做也是偏专业级，甚至偏制造。02
为什么盯上小 B，而不是继续卷 ToC？
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们那款产品什么时候众筹结束？众筹成绩怎么样？王志宇：10 月 15 日众筹结束，众筹了 300 多万美金，在 3D 打印历史众筹中排名第十——除了那些 UV 和光固化的项目，我们现在是 Kickstarter 上面第十名。300 万美金对大公司来说不算什么，但是对初创公司来说还是比较不错的。我们还拿了线下 300 万美金的订单，签下了一个欧洲客户。
雷峰网·鲸犀：没想过往 500 万美金冲吗？王志宇：现在广告费很高。而且我们发现，众筹不是唯一的一条路。我们要小批量交付，先看看效果，然后再迭代一点、再交付，这样才比较好。
雷峰网·鲸犀：主要是哪些用户？王志宇：DIY 创客还是大头。小 B 也有一部分，但是小 B 的人群不是特别大。
雷峰网·鲸犀：既然定位小 B，为什么预售阶段个人用户反而可能更多？王志宇：定位是一方面，买我们预售产品的用户可能不完全一样。如果他是一个小作坊，他可能会先买一台试试，不会一下子买很多。但是如果是个人，这个群体基数本来就比较大，所以刚开始个人会占多数。而如果机器卖出去了，小作坊可能会复购，但是个人可能购买一次就不会再买了。
雷峰网·鲸犀：所以，你们后续还是希望更多进入小作坊？王志宇：对。但不管是个人还是小 B，我们都会积极去做。
雷峰网·鲸犀：小作坊肯定购买的欲望更强。王志宇：这小作坊其实相对谨慎一点，因为他们购买产品回去要用很长时间，决策不会像个人用户那么冲动。个人用户是喜欢就立马买，反正就是玩嘛。
雷峰网·鲸犀：LightMake L4 的定价比一些同类产品高，是否会限制用户规模？王志宇：没关系，我们先服务好一部分高端群体，未来再考虑拓展用户。
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们和以小白 C 端用户为主的拓竹，走的是完全不同的路线。你们怎么看待这两条路线的竞争关系？未来会不会出现互相抢市场的情况？王志宇：举一个真实的例子，大家比较容易对标。你看打印机行业，惠普和理光。惠普家喻户晓，打印机大家都卖，家用机很便宜，几百到一两千都有。理光则专注商用，办公室复印机、复印店、印刷厂的大设备，很多都用理光的喷头。惠普 2025 年打印业务全年营收 1196 亿人民币，理光去年营收 787 亿。两者的区别在于使用场景：家用打印机一次打几张到几十张，速度慢；而理光的复印机一分钟能打几十张，适合批量需求，比如几十人开会、每人 10 页文件，一次就要几百张。打印店更是天天大量打印。比如毕业论文 200 张，用家用打印机要等一天，商用机就快得多。这就是场景和批量需求的不同。这是场景不同。拓竹要做拓圈、做小白用户，这是好事，全世界都知道 3D 打印机好玩。但真要批量制造，场景就不一样了。有人说我在南极最牛，在北极也最牛——其实并不见得。每家公司有各自的定位，不排除有人既想做消费级又想做工业级，那是公司自己的问题，要他们自己去定位。我们不用担心惠普抢理光的生意，因为这两类人群完全不同，诉求和生态也完全不同。从娱乐角度，买玩具是兴趣驱动；但印刷厂要的是赚钱，好不好玩不重要，赚钱才是本质。两类用户出发点不同，选择产品的标准、概念、诉求完全不同。做 256 头的机器给家用不现实，但对工厂来说，原来要很大厂房，现在一台机器就能搞定。
雷峰网·鲸犀：中小企业很适合买这款 3D 打印机回来做模型、打样或小批量生产。王志宇：是的，我们专门针对大规模批量制造，一台机器能顶别人一个厂房。03
直线电机，凭什么做到 4 倍效率？
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们的竞争优势在哪里？王志宇：效率比拓竹快 4 倍，比快造 U1 换颜色快 5 倍。
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们会现场或直播展示吗？王志宇：有。我们 9 月 5 号参加德国的展会，有在现场直播，也邀请了很多网红到现场看机器。
雷峰网·鲸犀：发售前，这款产品迭代了多少次？王志宇：软件迭代了几百次。
雷峰网·鲸犀：主要迭代什么环节？王志宇：现在大家最担心的是，打印速度快，能不能打得好。我们是先保证打得好，再打得快。简单来讲，拓竹的 H2C 虽然搭载了 7 个喷嘴，但只能轮流作业。快造的四喷头方案也是一样，换头才能继续打印。而我们的四喷头打印方案，支持四头同时工作，不用等待切换打印头。
雷峰网·鲸犀：这听起来还挺强的。稳定性如何呢？王志宇：稳定性比拓竹的高一两个数量级，精度高 100 倍。
雷峰网·鲸犀：怎么做到啊？王志宇：拓竹、快造用的电机，都是比较有性价比的步进电机。我们用的电机是工业级的直线电机，过往主要用在半导体领域，精度都是微米级。因为直线电机的精度和可靠性高，整个设备体系的精度和可靠性也随之提升了。打得又快又稳。
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们采用工业级的直线电机方案，有受到什么启发？王志宇：从需求出发，大部分人觉得 3D 打印机速度慢，打印一个模型要等几个小时。打照片一分钟搞定，打印模型至少几小时，这种需求没被满足，离用户预期还很远。3D 打印要进入家庭和大众消费，还有很长的路要走，速度可能需要提升几千倍。
雷峰网·鲸犀：除了电机方案，你们前期在产品方向上尝试过其他方案吗？王志宇：换头、换热端以及热端升降等方案，我们都有调研过。我们之所以选择直线电机方案，更多是觉得它是最优解，为什么呢？首先我们的四喷头打印机不用换头，省时间，永远是最优解。第二，你购买的一台打印机，标称能打印最大幅面，但实际打印未必每次都用到最大，空间浪费比例很高。从节约空间的角度出发，多头同时打印才是真正的节约空间。
雷峰网·鲸犀：市面上有做双头打印的，也有不少做四头打印的，你们规划的上限是多少？王志宇：四头打印是起点，下一代是 16 头，再往下一代是 64 头，再往下是 256 头。
雷峰网·鲸犀：现在是什么进度？王志宇：16 头和 64 头已经规划好了，只是机器还没做出来。
雷峰网·鲸犀：四头打印已经被验证了，16 头、64 头的可行性来自于哪里？王志宇：我们的 16 头机器和 4 头机器的大小是一样的，只是打印头的尺寸变小了。以后我把喷头的尺寸做得更小，64 喷头跟 16 喷头的机器还是一样大小，喷头尺寸会再缩小一半。
雷峰网·鲸犀：这个想法是什么时候开始萌生的？在第一代产品做到哪个节点的时候？王志宇：我们在做第一代产品就想过，我们要走制造的路径，我们要把制造的效率提升几百倍，而不是几倍。
雷峰网·鲸犀：刚刚你说你们前面已经调研了很多其他的方案，最终才选了四喷头的方案。相比快造、闪铸的四喷头打印机，肉眼看上去，你们这款产品的架构挺不一样的，这个出发点又是怎么考虑的？王志宇：我们有两个横梁，每个横梁上面有两个头。目前很少有公司会在一个横梁上做两个头，因为皮带驱动不稳定，一个头已经有重量，两个头更重，需要更大的电机推力，而常规步进电机的推力和皮带伸缩性不够，很难实现一个横梁装两个头，更别说四个或 16 个。我们采用直线电机，横梁推力达到 110 N，是常规步进电机的很多倍。有这个金刚钻，才敢揽这个瓷器活。
雷峰网·鲸犀：对比拓竹或者其他产品，你们的四个喷头有什么优势？王志宇：第一，你摆四台机器要留间距，浪费空间，而我一台机器只比单台大一点，却能顶四台，节约 75% 的空间。第二，时间上，你打一个模型，我能打四个，同样节约 75% 的时间。第三，材料和人工方面，开机率更高，材料成本节约一半，人工也节约一半。第四，管理上，原来一个人管四台，现在管一台；如果原来是 400 台，现在只需 100 台，管理大大简化。以后如果有 16 头的机器，别人需要 1600 台，我这里只需要很少的台数。我们的这个逻辑遥遥领先。04
从打印机到耗材机，轻量智造到底想做多大的生意？
雷峰网·鲸犀：有说法称小 B 用户买了咱们的产品，ROI 提升 10 倍以上。这是怎么计算出来的？王志宇：精益制造里有个概念叫人机料法——人力成本、机器设备效率、材料、管理方法。这几件事都搞好了，效率就会不断循环提升。从人的维度看，我们的机器能做到模型打印完自动取出来，别人不用开晚班，很多农场现在都要开晚班去拿模型。
雷峰网·鲸犀：就是不用人力再干预了。王志宇：对。我可以让它节约一半的人力，不用开晚班，这是第一个维度。第二，我的机器产能是拓竹的 4 倍。打常规单色或幻彩模型，包括龙蛋，拓竹设备打一个，我同时打 4 个，因为 4 个喷头可以同时工作。4 倍产能，节约一半人工。材料维度，我们可以提供比拓竹或同类公司低一半的耗材成本。
雷峰网·鲸犀：耗材的成本降低是因为什么？王志宇：很多人问是不是把毛利降低一点？我想说我们的毛利不会降低，可能还要提升，但会把用户售价降低一半。逻辑是：现在的耗材——不管是拓竹还是其他 3D 打印公司——都是把美国 PLA 颗粒买回来，拉成线再卖到用户，成本从 3 美金一公斤变成 15 美金一公斤。这完全是多余的，买过来又拉回去。我们提供了一个桌面化解决方案，替代生产线大设备，用户可以在美国的农场或家里直接买 3 美金的颗粒，自己拉成线，花 6-7 美金就能在家生产耗材了。
雷峰网·鲸犀：这个方案，相当于耗材直接在美国本土化。王志宇：第一叫减少中间环节，没有机会赚差价。第二，拉过来拉过去，浪费很多物流成本。
雷峰网·鲸犀：这个工具是你们自研？定价是多少？王志宇：我们自己研发的。这个机器定价 1000+ 美金。它一天可以生产 30 公斤耗材，每公斤节约 7 美金，一天能省下 200 多美金，一周就能回本。
雷峰网·鲸犀：一周就能回本。有其他同行在做这个事情吗？王志宇：目前没有人做这个事。而且我们这个工具会颠覆整个耗材的行业逻辑。
雷峰网·鲸犀：影响这么大吗？王志宇：那卖卷料的就卖不下去了。所以我们以后可能光是耗材机这个设备，都有可能做到比拓竹更大的规模。
雷峰网·鲸犀：创想三维做了一款 3D 耗材回收机。王志宇：他们确实也做了这样的一个产品。但是我们的侧重点不一样。创想三维那款侧重的是废料的回收，它是把用过的废料碾碎，混色，再掺点新料，做批量生产。我们做的是新料的生产，可不支持废料回收。
雷峰网·鲸犀：但使用这个是有门槛的，不是所有人都需要这个耗材机。王志宇：如果年用几百卷，就可以考虑；如果只用两卷，就没必要。我们是为相对资深的用户设计产品，针对 Pro C 和 SMB 这类有经验的专业客户——他们用量大，三五台机器不停运转，省起来就很划算。
雷峰网·鲸犀：除了核心的产品，还有两个针对不同细分场景的产品。除了这个，另外一个是啥？王志宇：另外一款是自动取模型的，也是一个配件，定价几百美金。
雷峰网·鲸犀：这个工具好，我之前打印过一个模型，取模型的时候就被割伤了。王志宇：所有取过模型的人都流过血，我也流过。虽然是塑料的，但是一样会让你获得“血的教训”。取模型还是不方便，远没到安全迅速、打印完直接拿了就用的地步，3D 打印机离那一天还很远。
雷峰网·鲸犀：你们对发货有做预期吗？王志宇：我们今年 11 月份就会发货。7 月份，我们已经有 50 台打印机发货了，还有 200 台在产线，相当于我们已经有 250 台机器。
雷峰网·鲸犀：产能怎么做到的？王志宇：我们的制造是在一家特别大的公司，叫欣旺达。所以制造管够，一天 400 台。
雷峰网·鲸犀：背后有高人牵线吗？王志宇：确实有高人牵线，是我以前在华为的朋友介绍的。欣旺达有个 3C 事业部，现在做扫地机、泳池机器人。他们跟我讲了投资元鼎的故事：当时元鼎还很小，他们投了几百万，帮他们做制造、做改进，一直迭代——现在元鼎已经是泳池机器人 TOP1。他们有这种超前培养、和公司一起成长的意识。我们聊后一拍即合，相互认可，所以他们也愿意进入这个赛道。他们为我们单开了一栋楼，因为一条产线摆不下。
雷峰网·鲸犀：跟他们合作，他们有什么硬性的门槛吗？王志宇：他们不是什么都做，也会看领域。我们行业目前处于快速增长期，算是红利期，这可能是他们愿意进入的一个重要原因。
雷峰网·鲸犀：会不会有其他家也在跟进方案呢？王志宇：有些人会跟进类似方案，比如也用直线电机，但没人像我们这样用于制造、农场。我们了解到，有些公司的直线电机产品还是针对消费级、个人场景。大家场景不同，就像同一口锅，可以炒青菜也可以炒荤菜，关键看老板想往哪个方向走。
雷峰网·鲸犀：有哪些在做类似的？王志宇：以前富志做过一款用雅科贝思直线电机的 3D 打印机，卖二三十万一台。这属于大机器。
雷峰网·鲸犀：咱们在 3D 生成这一块有布局吗？王志宇：短期内，我们不会自己做这类基础性投入。我们还没到这个阶段，会选择外部合作，借助别人已有的 AI 能力来赋能。但如果农场、小作坊或用户对某些模型很感兴趣，我们也会收集一些有意思的模型供大家选择，这个成本不高。我们会选择畅销、热门的模型，不会做那种几百万个没人要的。
雷峰网·鲸犀：设想一下，你们的社区或平台建设逻辑是怎样的？王志宇：我们的用户主要是工程师、设计师，设计能力较强，属于资深人群。我们做的是 Pro C 类产品，更多是提供参考或便利，他们本身就有很强的设计能力。所以我们不会做小白类内容，人群不同，诉求不同，平台建设逻辑也不一样。我们更倾向于用 AI 来做设计，而不是等别人做好设计再来选择。目前 3D 生成有两个方向：一是用 AI 控制传统设计软件，让设计师更高效、更快完成工作；二是不需要设计师，输入一句话或拍张照就能生成设计，属于傻瓜式。我们更倾向第一种，帮助设计师提高效率，比如原来花一天，现在可能半小时就够了。
雷峰网·鲸犀：你怎么看 3D 打印在欧美制造业中的机会？王志宇：结合现在中美博弈的背景，美国现在大举推行"美国制造"这个概念，动不动就给补贴，只要你搬回一个供应链，美国就给你补多少钱。我们会更多地通过 3D 打印去帮助美国把制造做得更好。我觉得在未来欧美的主力制造领域，3D 打印有非常大的发展空间，远不只是一个玩具市场。我们公司取的名字叫轻量智造，没有取什么"什么三维"——轻量智造的解读就是：一整套的轻量化制造解决方案。它不局限在 3D 打印这个点，而是怎么样把这种大设备、大制造变成一个小制造，让它回归到原产地、回归到用户那里去：在欧洲、在美国、在各种小镇上面，我就能自己给自己造东西，我不需要依赖一个远在太平洋彼岸的大工厂。我们是在给未来制造递铲子的人。

articles.title: Thunder-DeID+: Boundary-Aware Korean De-identification from Court Judgments to Broader Sensitive Documents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22733v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: This study examines the transferability of a de-identification model developed for Korean court judgments to a broader range of sensitive documents, focusing on boundary precision, label granularity, and recall. The agglutinative structure of Korean causes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers to frequently merge Personally Identifiable Information (PII) with adjacent particles, which complicates accurate span recovery. Furthermore, current PII taxonomies lack sufficient granularity for legal texts. To address these issues, this study introduces Thunder-DeID+, which integrates a refined three-tier PII taxonomy with a boundary-aware tokenizer. The tokenizer enhances a pretrained BPE vocabulary by incorporating N-gram and boundary-scoring components to better align token and PII span boundaries. The proposed approach is evaluated using a tokenizer-independent word-segment-level protocol. On full-length judgments, the tokenizer consistently improves W. Strict Typed F1-score from 0.76-0.77 to 0.87-0.88 across four model sizes (150M, 395M, 750M, and 1B), mainly by increasing precision rather than model scale. With fine-tuning on 1,000 broader sensitive documents, the judgment-trained model further achieves 0.93 W. Strict Typed F1-score, indicating effective transfer beyond court judgments.

articles.title: 约20%的Anthropic股份，将用于公益！
articles.text:
智东西（公众号：zhidxcom）
编译 |  黄菲
编辑 |  江宇
智东西10月19日消息，今日，美国AI独角兽Anthropic宣布，其将拿出其5%的股份设立公益基金Anthropic公共利益基金（Anthropic Public Benefit Fund）。该基金旨在应对AI发展对就业市场带来的冲击，并为公益事业提供更多资金支持。
对此，特斯拉首席执行官、SpaceXSI创始人兼首席执行官埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）在X上评论称：“我建议直接把这些股份分给公众。”
▲Anthropic以及马斯克的评论，图源：X
目前，这项计划仍需获得股东的批准。未来，随着该公司估值上升，基金持有的股份比例还可能进一步提高。
Anthropic称，设立该基金在进一步推进该公司的公益事业的同时，也计划将公益投入拓展至现有的AI安全研究和生物医学研究之外。
7月22日，该公司就已承诺投入2亿美元（约合人民币13.5亿元），用于研究和应对AI对就业市场带来的冲击，包括岗位流失、劳动者收入保障以及如何让劳动者分享AI发展带来的经济收益等问题。
▲Anthropic发文投入Anthropic公共利益基金，图源：Anthropic官网
一、Anthropic加大公益投入，股权捐赠承诺持续加码
据Anthropic官网公告，新设立的Anthropic公共利益基金将采用由Anthropic全资持有的有限责任公司（LLC）形式。
按照计划，在获得股东批准后，Anthropic将向基金划拨该公司5%的股份。此后，该公司估值每较尚未公布的基准值增长50%，董事会便可酌情再向基金增加相当于该公司2%的股份。
为了让基金能够更灵活地开展公益活动，Anthropic选择将其设立为有限责任公司，而非依据美国《国内税收法》第501(c)(3)条设立免税慈善组织。因此，基金既可以向传统非营利组织提供大额捐款，也可以直接向特定群体提供资金支持。
Anthropic称，其此前已有多项与公益使命相关的工作，如向非营利组织和科研机构提供Claude服务折扣。这些工作在具有公益价值的同时，也可能为该公司带来商业价值。
现有相关公益项目仍主要由该公司内部推进，而新设立的基金将用于支持更多不同形式的项目。
在资金用途方面，Anthropic明确称，基金持有的公司股份不会用于美国境内外的游说活动或政治捐赠。
对于基金的具体治理机制、组织架构，以及未来增加持股比例所依据的估值门槛，Anthropic称将在未来几个月会进一步公布。
此次设立基金并非Anthropic首次作出公益承诺。Anthropic官网称，该公司创立时，包括达里奥·阿莫迪（Dario Amodei）、丹妮拉·阿莫迪（Daniela Amodei）等在内的联合创始人已承诺捐出其个人持股的80%作为人类公益基金，用于支持公益事业建设。
此外，Anthropic还设有员工股权捐赠配比计划，允许员工承诺捐赠部分股权，再由该公司提供相应配比支持。目前约有一半员工参与该计划。
此前创始人的股权捐赠承诺、员工股权捐赠计划与此次新增的5%股份承诺合并计算，Anthropic称，约20%的公司股份将用于公益目的。
关于此次划拨股份对应的具体金额Anthropic尚未公布。
二、Anthropic关注AI就业冲击，基金探索援助新方式
Anthropic此次设立公益基金，旨在探索更多方法应对AI发展带来的社会问题，其中一项重点是应对AI可能给就业市场带来的冲击。
Anthropic认为，考虑到AI的发展速度，其未来需要采取力度更大的应对措施，而新基金能够为这些尝试提供更灵活的资金支持。
随着企业加大对AI的投入，全球多家公司已削减数以千计的岗位，其中不少科技企业将裁员归因于AI技术带来的效率提升。
国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃（Kristalina Georgieva）此前也曾谈及AI对就业的影响。她于10月12日称，AI可能改变约40%的工作岗位，在发达国家中，这一比例可能达到60%。
▲国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃在小组讨论中发言，图源：新加坡总统府（The Istana）官网
此次设立公益基金，也与Anthropic对AI潜在风险的长期关注相呼应。
据路透社9月29日报道，Anthropic在为首次公开募股（IPO）准备的文件中，用约80页篇幅讨论风险因素，并提到先进AI可能对人类构成灾难性甚至生存层面的风险。
对于基金未来如何分配资金，Anthropic尚未公布具体项目清单。
Anthropic称，将在未来几个月进一步披露基金的治理与组织架构，并发布公益报告，介绍该公司在实现自身使命方面取得的进展。
结语：公益基金能否托住AI时代的打工人，Anthropic仍在探索
AI带来的就业冲击，不仅体现在部分岗位被替代，还可能导致劳动者收入下降、职业技能过时，以及重新就业难度上升等问题。
Anthropic此次设立公益基金，为应对这些问题提供了新的资金渠道。如果未来基金能够帮助劳动者分享AI带来的经济收益，或能在一定程度上缓解技术变革带来的就业压力。
对普通劳动者而言，关键在于这些资金能否转化为实际保障，帮助他们在岗位被AI改变甚至取代后，获得重新就业的机会，并分享技术进步带来的收益。
Anthropic的公益承诺最终能在多大程度上缓解AI带来的就业冲击，取决于资金的具体用途，以及能否转化为切实的就业支持。

articles.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
articles.text:
“I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration.
Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.
After a summer filled with revelations that swarms of agents built by top firms like OpenAI and Anthropic have been breaking their containment and causing havoc on the public internet—often while those companies weren’t aware of what their agents were up to—the AI industry is desperate to get a better handle on the technology it has built.
That’s one reason the blog post landed with such force. “I think this may be remembered as a major moment in scientific history,” one AI researcher posted on X: “I feel like my understanding of what a neural net is has been catapulted into the future by five years or something.” Another called it “the most important AI paper of the year.”
Not everyone is convinced, however. What Cammarata has shared is little more than a hunch, says Chris Potts at Stanford University, who leads a team that is trying to understand how LLMs work. “As far as I can tell, nothing about this blog post makes the problems any easier,” he says. “It would not have occurred to me to say this at all, but very prominent people on social media seem to believe that it is an all-encompassing breakthrough.”
I talked to Cammarata the day after his post blew up. He says he was surprised by the response: “I didn’t expect people to update [their beliefs about AI] quite as much as they did.”
“I just really enjoy looking at neural networks,” he says. “Honestly, I really like doing this stuff. And after looking a lot, I have a hopeful story.”
Knotted networks
It has long been accepted that the mechanisms inside neural networks, the software that underpins most AI models, are very hard—perhaps impossible—to unpick fully. That’s because when the networks are trained, they appear to take on weird, tangled structures that make no sense to a human. Researchers like to say today’s AI is grown like a garden, not built like a bridge.
Cammarata has done more than most to establish that view. He previously worked at OpenAI, where he helped pioneer techniques that allowed researchers to peer inside models, including tools that can probe individual neurons to see what they represent. It’s a little like how neuroscientists use MRI to study brains. (MIT Technology Review chose this approach, known as mechanistic interpretability, as one of its 10 hottest technologies of 2025.)
Back in 2020, Cammarata and his colleagues were studying a small image-recognition model called Inception v1. When they looked at its neurons, it seemed to be using them to capture multiple things at once. For example, they found that one neuron responded to both images of cars and images of cats.
The researchers concluded that the model was getting at least some of its neurons to multitask, perhaps so that it could fit in more data. Looking at other models appeared to back this up. The phenomenon became known as superposition: Models folded unrelated concepts into single neurons. The upshot was clear: When you looked inside a model, what you saw was a vast, tangled knot.
Most mechanistic interpretability research has therefore focused on ways to untangle that knot. But despite a few breakthroughs, progress has been slow. Today’s models, such as the latest LLMs, are so large and complex that researchers can make sense of only tiny pieces at a time. Some leading figures in the field doubt if it will ever be possible to understand an LLM in fine-grained detail.
Cammarata was one of them. “I was very pessimistic,” he says. But then he took the trouble to really look.
Nothing but neurons
At Goodfire, Cammarata spends nearly all of his time peering inside neural networks. He has built new tools and deploys teams of AI agents to help him make sense of what he sees. “I spent like, I don’t know, 10 hours a day, seven days a week, for most of the last year just looking at neurons,” he says.
What he claims to have realized is that there is a kind of logic to neural networks after all, even if they seem to make no sense at first. “We were looking at it wrong,” he says. “I just think you want to try slightly harder; you don’t want to give up too quickly.”
Cammarata almost makes it sound like a conversion of faith. Those early experiments with models such as Inception v1, which suggested that neural networks were tangled up, fostered a kind of confirmation bias. When researchers looked at a new model, they expected to be flummoxed, he says. “Every time I couldn’t understand something, I was like, ‘Wow, this untangling process is even more important than I thought, because I can’t make any progress without it.’”
But the more Cammarata looked at neurons, he says, the more things started to fall into place. “Not all of them are flawless, but I expected nothing to be legible, or very little to be legible,” he says. “And actually, I was able to, like, map out whole circuitry.”
Back to cars and cats
Cammarata took his new approach—and his new agents—and went back to Inception v1. “I’d studied that for probably thousands of hours,” he says. But with fresh eyes, Cammarata found things that he now thinks they got wrong the first time around. Take the car-and-cat neuron. Rather than asking why multiple unrelated things were packed into a single neuron, he now tried to figure out what those things might have in common.
It hit him: It was a V shape. “I was looking at the same images; there was no technical change,” he says. “But I now believed that neural networks defined patterns, and so I looked at it differently. It probably took me five seconds.”
It turns out that the image-recognition model was packing cars and cats into the same place because pictures of both those things often feature a prominent shape that looks like a V: the face of a cat; the front of a car seen from the side.
Cammarata ran a few experiments to check what other things the neuron responded to and found they included the corner of a pool table, the pointed nose of a Japanese high-speed train, and a fire boat shooting water into the air from its deck. He also checked what turned the neuron off and found that it included images with a round O shape, a kind of anti-V.
The model had stored cats and cars in the same place because at some level they look the same, says Cammarata. “And I was like, ‘Whoa, okay, I think I might just be misunderstanding neural networks in general.’”
Cammarata is not saying that he yet fully gets how LLMs (or any models) work. He is saying that he no longer thinks full understanding is impossible. “I previously thought there would be some really hard problems to solve,” he says.
“I now feel like if I had 100,000 years to go look through a frontier language model just one circuit at a time, there’s, like, a pretty good shot I would come up with a good understanding.”
He adds: “And if that’s true, things are really good, because you’re about to get insanely smart agents at a ridiculous scale. And what would have taken me, you know, 100,000 years, we will be able to do much faster. Automated scientists are getting really good.”
Boundless optimism
Built by Google in 2014, Inception v1 is a far simpler model than anything at the cutting edge today. Cammarata and his colleagues have started looking at modern LLMs and plan to publish the technical results of that work soon. A lot of researchers are looking forward to seeing those details. “I appreciate that he looked at thousands of examples, but even a large number here is not a substitute for rigorous evaluation,” says Stanford University’s Potts.
In the meantime, some are pushing back hard on the hype. Jacob Hilton at the Alignment Research Center, a nonprofit research lab based in Berkeley, who has collaborated with Cammarata in the past, doesn’t think his claims are as important as people are making out.
In a series of posts on X, Hilton notes that researchers understand less than 0.01% of the inner workings of top-tier LLMs. “I always appreciate Nick [Cammarata]’s boundless optimism when we hang out, but unfortunately this is giving the public an unrealistic picture of the state of the field,” he wrote. “For a full understanding, we need to go beyond neurons, and explain how they connect together to form circuits. How is this going? If we are aiming for a full understanding, things are not looking good!”
Neel Nanda at Google DeepMind, who helped pioneer mechanistic interpretability alongside Cammarata, is also skeptical. “This is interesting work, but I don’t think it’s a significant update to the big picture of interpretability,” he wrote on X.
Nanda agrees that understanding what individual neurons do could help researchers figure out why specific models misbehave. But like Hilton, he notes that neurons are just one piece of a far larger puzzle. “I do not agree with some people’s grander inferences like that this is substantial progress towards ambitious reverse engineering [or] solving interpretability,” he wrote.
Cammarata admits that a lot of people have taken what he said too far: “It’s not infinitely good news; it’s not everything solved,” he says. “There’s a bunch of open questions around, like how much the combinations of neurons matter versus just one at a time.”
Cammarata says his blog post landed at a time when people are looking for hope. In particular, he thinks the AI safety community—the researchers and policymakers most worried that powerful models will bring huge risks—needs a lifeline right now. They think that things are looking bad and that even if things do turn out okay, it will be because we got lucky, not because we fixed anything, he says: “I don’t really hear a lot of optimism.”
That’s why Cammarata thinks what he has to say matters. The job of figuring out how this technology works, and thus how to control it, has barely begun. But at least it’s not a nonstarter. “I think our job is to sort of try to think like the neural network,” he says. “My guess is that things will turn out pretty well, because it was in some sense designed to be read.”

articles.title: 荣耀WIN耳机官宣：40ms超低延迟、55dB深度降噪
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，荣耀正式官宣全新WIN耳机，定位电竞向真无线耳机，主打游戏低延迟和强降噪能力，将会在10月21日荣耀WIN 电竞宇宙嘉年华活动正式发布。
游戏性能是这款耳机的一大亮点，开启游戏模式后可以做到40ms超低延迟。玩射击手游的时候，脚步声、枪声可以做到音画同步，玩家可以根据声音提前判断对手位置，抢占对战先机。
降噪给到55dB深度降噪，通勤坐地铁、身处嘈杂室内，耳机可以压制大部分环境噪音。
打游戏的时候隔绝外界干扰，让玩家可以专心团战；日常上下班，也能安安静静听歌追剧，不用被周边杂音打扰。
发声硬件配备12.4毫米镀钛振膜单元，音质方面通过LHDC5.0以及Hi-Res金标双认证。
不光打游戏音效到位，日常听歌的解析力也有保障，兼顾游戏和音乐两种使用场景，不用准备两副耳机来回切换。
通话配置也没有缩水，搭载三麦AI通话降噪算法，遇到刮风环境也能压制风噪。不管是游戏开黑语音，还是户外打电话，对方都可以听清人声，杂音不会干扰沟通。
这款耳机瞄准多场景使用，手游电竞上分、通勤赶路、休闲听歌都可以覆盖。从官宣信息来看，没有公布完整续航、售价，更多细节会留到10月21日发布活动揭晓。
荣耀WIN耳机想要把游戏延迟、降噪、Hi?Res音质全部兼顾，后续正式开售之后，会成为中端电竞耳机里有力的竞争者。

articles.title: Achieving near-zero-downtime scaling in Elastic Expert Parallelism
articles.text:
Achieving near-zero-downtime scaling in Elastic Expert Parallelism | vLLM Blog
MenuSearch DocsDocumentationBlogEventsOffice HoursContactCommunityGitHub

Blog
Achieving near-zero-downtime scaling in Elastic Expert Parallelism
October 19, 202612 min read
Itay Alroy (NVIDIA)
#large-scale-serving#elastic-ep#expert-parallelism#moe#nixl#cuda-graphs
Overlapping topology preparation with serving
Expand EP communication in place
Preserve CUDA graphs on existing workers
Prepare joining workers independently
Performance on DeepSeek V4 Pro
Scale-up and scale-down timings
Maintaining the SLO while adding GPUs
Try Elastic EP
What comes next
Restore warm workers with Dynamo Snapshot
Achieve state-of-the-art EP communication with NIXL EP
Connect Elastic EP to Dynamo and llm-d orchestration
Acknowledgements
Table of Contents
Traditionally, changing the number of GPUs in a vLLM service required adding or removing entire model replicas or restarting the engine with a different GPU count. As models grow larger, each replica needs more GPUs, so scaling by replica adds or removes GPUs in increasingly large increments. Restarting vLLM to scale DeepSeek V4 Pro from 16 to 20 GB200 GPUs stopped serving for 197 seconds (see the performance section for details), leaving those expensive GPUs allocated without generating tokens.
In our first Elastic EP post, we showed how vLLM could add or remove GPUs from a running DEP deployment (data-parallel attention with expert-parallel MoE) without restarting it. While we avoided a restart, serving still stopped throughout reconfiguration as we initialized new workers, prepared the expanded communication groups, loaded model weights, and repeated kernel warmup and CUDA graph capture. In our DeepSeek V4 Pro benchmark, this pause lasted 100 seconds when scaling from 16 to 20 GPUs and 56 seconds when scaling back to 16 GPUs (full details in the performance section).
In this post, we describe how asynchronous preparation and NIXL EP enabled Elastic EP reconfiguration with near-zero downtime. In the same benchmark, we reduced downtime to 0.82 seconds when scaling from 16 to 20 GPUs and 1.96 seconds when scaling back to 16 GPUs, allowing us to scale up and down with almost no impact on serving performance.
Overlapping topology preparation with serving
We reorganized vLLM's reconfiguration flow into two phases: background preparation and a short commit. Existing workers use separate background threads to prepare and warm up target communication, transfer model weights, and synchronize execution-related information (such as autotuning results) with joining workers, while continuing to serve requests with their current communication groups and CUDA graphs. In parallel, joining workers initialize, receive model weights, and prepare their communication and GPU execution. During the commit phase, vLLM briefly pauses its schedulers, activates the prepared topology, and resumes serving. These changes were introduced in asynchronous preparation and prepare/commit optimizations.
Preparation covers four main tasks:
Initialize joining workers. Start their processes and allocate storage for the model and execution.
Prepare communication. Set up the target communication groups and expand the EP communicator.
Transfer model weights. Transfer the required weights from existing workers to joining workers over NVLink or RDMA.
Prepare execution. Complete the required compilation, kernel warmup, tuning setup, and CUDA graph construction on joining workers.
After the commit phase, asynchronous Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB) allows new workers to begin handling attention while existing workers handle expert computation. EPLB then redistributes experts across the expanded group in the background.
The main challenge is preparing communication and GPU execution without involving or disrupting the workers that are serving requests.
Expand EP communication in place
Before NIXL EP, the EP communication backends available in vLLM used fixed membership: each instance was created for a specific set of ranks. Adding or removing ranks requires a new instance. Even when that instance can be created in the background, two problems remain.
First, the old and new instances need separate communication buffers and other resources, including memory registrations, IPC handles, and RDMA Queue Pairs (QPs). Keeping both instances alive increases communication memory usage and requires repeating setup rather than reusing existing resources.
Second, switching EP communicators changes the buffers and communication state used by the EP communication kernels. This invalidates previously captured CUDA graphs, which must be recaptured before serving can resume. That requires repeating warmup and graph construction for many batch shapes across all retained workers. In our DeepSeek V4 Pro benchmark, even with asynchronous preparation, performing warmup and graph recapture during the commit phase resulted in serving pauses of 58 seconds during scale-up and 44 seconds during scale-down.
To solve these problems, we designed NIXL EP, an EP communication library tailor-made for Elastic EP. It adds or removes ranks in place, reusing the same NIXL agent, buffers, and connections. New peers can be connected while existing workers continue serving, and only joining peers need new connections and registrations. NIXL EP also keeps captured EP dispatch and combine entries valid across reconfiguration, allowing retained workers to reuse their existing CUDA graphs.
During preparation, vLLM's background thread connects joining peers without activating them. The commit phase then activates the prepared peers without replacing the communicator.
The same NIXL EP communicator progresses from the current active group to connected inactive joining peers, then activates the target group at commit.
Figure 1. Connecting and activating new EP peers. Green ranks are active; gray ranks are connected but masked. During the commit phase, new peers are activated without replacing the agent or buffers.
vLLM still creates new DP coordination groups and EPLB groups for the target topology, but their communication runs outside the captured model forward pass, so switching to them does not invalidate CUDA graphs.
Preserve CUDA graphs on existing workers
A CUDA graph records GPU operations so that vLLM can replay a forward pass without repeatedly launching each operation from the CPU. A captured kernel node includes its launch configuration and argument values, including pointers to input and output tensors. Memory contents can change between replays, but the recorded pointers must remain valid. These requirements are part of the CUDA graph execution contract.
vLLM captures separate graphs for different batch shapes and execution modes and runs warmup forward passes before each capture.
Preserving captured CUDA graphs requires more than keeping the communicator object alive. NIXL EP also keeps kernel launch configurations, graph-visible communication arguments, and input and output tensor addresses stable across reconfiguration. Its kernels read active group membership from device state that can be updated in place.
We also changed vLLM to keep the captured arguments, launch configurations, and input and output tensor addresses of the surrounding compute kernels stable across reconfiguration:
We reuse retained workers' fused-MoE execution objects instead of rebuilding them for a different active EP size.
We keep the addresses and layouts of graph-visible workspaces and dispatch outputs stable across reconfiguration so that captured expert kernels can continue using them. Dispatch outputs also serve as inputs to expert computation. If their addresses or layouts changed with EP size, captured expert kernels would still use the old pointers and offsets.
We preserve the backing storage of expert-routing tensors and update mappings in place. This allows EPLB to change the mapping contents without moving the tensors used by captured kernels.
Together, these changes allow retained workers to reuse their existing CUDA graphs after both scale-up and scale-down.
Prepare joining workers independently
Existing workers have graphs to preserve. Joining workers have none.
Joining workers normally prepare by running model forward passes with EP dispatch and combine, as well as exchanging batch information with other workers. These steps require other workers to participate, but existing workers are already serving real requests on the current topology.
NIXL EP lets each joining worker temporarily mask every remote EP peer during warmup and graph preparation. Only that worker's local rank is active for EP communication. We also modified vLLM so that these preparation passes do not wait for DP batch information from other workers. This lets joining workers run their dummy batches and capture CUDA graphs without requiring existing workers to participate.
Existing workers serve with their current peers active and joining peers masked. Each joining worker keeps only itself active for local warmup and graph capture, masking all remote peers, including other joining workers.
Figure 2. Green ranks are active for EP communication; gray ranks are masked. Existing workers serve together while each joining worker masks all remote EP peers for preparation.
After capture, NIXL EP can reactivate peers without invalidating the graphs. Joining workers reuse their locally captured graphs when they begin serving as part of the expanded group.
Performance on DeepSeek V4 Pro
All experiments in this section used DeepSeek V4 Pro on GB200 GPUs, with TP=1 and DP/EP sizes of 16 and 20. Model weights were pre-downloaded in safetensors format on shared Lustre storage and loaded using the default --load-format auto. Measurements used warm kernel-compilation caches (Triton, TileLang, and FlashInfer).
Scale-up and scale-down timings
The table shows which stages run while serving is paused and which run in the background while existing workers continue serving.
StageA: BlockingB: Async preparationC: Async preparation + graph reuseInitialize joining workersServing pausedBackgroundBackgroundPrepare target communicationServing pausedBackgroundBackgroundTransfer model weightsServing pausedBackgroundBackgroundWarmup and graph capture on joining workersServing pausedServing pausedBackgroundWarmup and graph capture on existing workersServing pausedServing pausedNot needed (existing graphs stay valid)Activate the target topologyServing pausedServing pausedServing paused
Configuration C is supported only by NIXL EP.
Downtime: the observed serving interruption, when in-flight requests stop progressing and new requests are not admitted.
Total time: the duration of the full scaling operation, including preparation.
The two durations are measured separately.
MetricA: BlockingB: Async preparationC: Async preparation + graph reuse16 to 20 GPUs: downtime99.62 s58.04 s0.82 s20 to 16 GPUs: downtime56.25 s44.07 s1.96 s16 to 20 GPUs: total time99.72 s97.27 s92.34 s20 to 16 GPUs: total time56.21 s51.46 s9.32 s
All configurations passed numerical correctness checks, including checks on every joining worker.
Maintaining the SLO while adding GPUs
We served DeepSeek V4 Pro on 16 GPUs, then gradually increased the incoming request rate from about 8 to 16 requests per second. We replayed the same 11,391-request scenario against three deployments: one stayed at 16 GPUs, one restarted with 20 GPUs, and one scaled to 20 GPUs using Elastic EP with NIXL EP. The service-level objective (SLO) was a rolling p95 time to first token below 5 seconds.
Elastic EP stays below the SLO throughout the scenario. During preparation, its serving performance matches the static 16-GPU deployment. After scaling, it matches the recovered 20-GPU deployment's performance.
Figure 3. End-to-end serving under rising request load. Curves show 30-second rolling p95 outcomes, with failed requests assigned a 30-second penalty rather than a measured TTFT.
Elastic EP completed all 11,391 requests and stayed below the SLO throughout the scenario.
During preparation, Elastic EP matched the static 16-GPU deployment's serving performance, with no visible degradation from background preparation.
After scaling, Elastic EP matched the recovered 20-GPU deployment's performance, with no visible post-scale degradation.
Try Elastic EP
Background preparation, CUDA graph reuse, and independent graph capture on joining workers are all available today in the latest vLLM and NIXL releases. Install them with pip and start using Elastic EP.
For a complete usage example, see the cuda_graphs_heavy_nixl_ep case in vLLM's Elastic EP test. The example includes the server configuration and scaling API calls. It scales from two GPUs to four and back while sending requests, checking serving during preparation and model accuracy around each resize.
What comes next
Restore warm workers with Dynamo Snapshot
We have effectively solved the long serving interruption. The next challenge is getting new capacity ready sooner. We plan to integrate Dynamo Snapshot so joining workers can restore initialized process and CUDA state instead of repeating compilation, kernel warmup, graph construction, and other startup work.
Communication for the target topology must be prepared separately because it is not restored from the snapshot. Restoring large model weights from checkpoint storage can dominate restore time, so we plan to keep Elastic EP's GPU-to-GPU weight transfer from existing workers instead.
Achieve state-of-the-art EP communication with NIXL EP
We aim for state-of-the-art dispatch and combine performance with NIXL EP while maintaining full support for Elastic EP and fault tolerance. An upcoming NIXL EP performance update is the next step toward that goal (see the NIXL EP roadmap RFC).
Connect Elastic EP to Dynamo and llm-d orchestration
With the engine-level capability in place, the next step is to use Elastic EP from orchestrator autoscalers. Work toward this integration is already underway across the vLLM, Dynamo, and llm-d communities.
These efforts include vLLM's external-load-balancer work and Dynamo's Elastic EP proposal.
If you run inference at scale, we encourage you to try Elastic EP and share your workloads and operational requirements. If you build inference infrastructure, we welcome contributions to vLLM Elastic EP and NIXL EP. Let's get Elastic EP running in production.

articles.title: Mitigating Demographic Disparities in Explanation-Human Alignment via Rationale Regularization
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22586v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups. Using the HateXplain dataset, we introduce Plausibility-EFG, a metric that measures the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups by comparing model-generated token attributions with human-annotated rationales. We evaluate BERT, RoBERTa, and ADV-RoBERTa, an adversarially trained model, using Integrated Gradients and SHAP. Our results show that ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups. These improvements are observed with both attribution methods and remain consistent across training, validation, and test splits. We also show that reducing prediction-level bias alone does not eliminate disparities in explanations, suggesting that predictive fairness and explanation fairness are related but distinct objectives. Finally, our fairness-performance analysis shows that stronger adversarial regularization can further reduce Plausibility-EFG, although it may cause a small decrease in macro-F1. Overall, this work presents explanation fairness as an important objective in hate speech moderation and introduces Fair-REF, a framework designed to reduce disparities in model explanations across demographic groups.

articles.title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22686v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Agents operating over long horizons need an effective memory that allows them to reuse their experience throughout long interactions. If the entire history of an interaction is retained, it becomes difficult to find the relevant experience, while compressing it into summaries may result in the loss of visual and spatial details that are required later on. We present \textbf{MFM}, a multimodal filesystem memory architecture that keeps complementary types of agent memory. \textbf{Episodic memory} stores the observations, actions, and outcomes, and \textbf{spatial memory} associates experiences with locations. \textbf{Semantic and procedural memory} build up general knowledge and reusable methods of acting, and \textbf{working memory} holds the current plans. MFM makes use of searchable textual records to connect these different representations to the underlying multimodal episodes. The agents are able to find previous experiences by means of contextual cues and to examine the original observations in order to recover details that are missing from their textual descriptions. Through consolidation, the agents convert experience into higher-level knowledge and procedures while still keeping references to the original episodes. In the case of long-horizon Minecraft and computer-use tasks, MFM leads to improved performance with three base models. With GPT-6-Astra, MFM completes \emph{Mine Diamond from Scratch} and reaches 16 out of 24 milestones on the \emph{Ender Dragon} task, as against 12.7 for the best baseline. On CUABench-KiCad it attains a mean reward of 0.440, as compared to 0.400 for the best baseline and 0.267 in the case of no persistent memory.

articles.title: From Parallels to Divergence: Language Models' Learning of Action Nominal Constructions
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22468v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Action nominal constructions (ANCs) express events in nominal form, with their argument marking following patterns found in clauses or ordinary noun phrases. In this paper, we investigate how different grammatical configurations affect language models' learning of ANCs and related constructions, and how these learning preferences compare with typological distributions in natural languages. We use a grammar-engineered method for synthetic corpus construction that combines shared semantic input from natural corpora with computational grammars. We construct 96 target languages varying in clause word order, noun-phrase word order, alignment, complement system, and ANC strategy. For each language, we train GPT-2-small models from scratch and evaluate them using targeted minimal pairs covering 34 grammatical phenomena. The results show typological parallels in basic clause configurations but divergences in complement systems and ANC strategies, with models also learning combinations rare or unattested in natural languages. This partial alignment suggests that natural language distributions may reflect both general learning pressures and functional demands not fully captured by model learning experiments.

articles.title: Developer’s guide to implementing MCP apps in Gemini
articles.text:
Enterprise assistants still respond mostly in text. However, that can break down for visual, multi-step work, where every adjustment costs another slow chat turn.
MCP Apps (SEP-1865) solves this. This open Model Context Protocol (MCP) extension pairs a tool with a live UI. In Gemini Enterprise, that UI renders directly in the chat flow inside a sandboxed iframe, and can expand to fullscreen or a side panel. Edits run locally while the workspace and assistant stay synchronized.
You also avoid rebuilding core foundations: Gemini provides workforce sign-in, governed data access, and the Default Assistant, while you host your MCP server on a private Cloud Run service.
Why we need MCP Apps
Enterprise assistants have evolved through three generations:
Generation 1 (Text chatbots): Returns static markdown with no interactive controls.
Generation 2 (Standard MCP tools): Invokes live APIs, but outputs static text. Every change requires another model turn.
Generation 3 (Interactive MCP Apps): Pairs each tool with a live workspace. Adjustments happen in the widget without a model turn, while the assistant stays in sync.
Building MCP Apps in Gemini delivers six benefits:
Responsive user experience: Single-click actions execute directly in the panel without round-tripping through the chat.
Purpose-built workflows: Deliver visual redaction views for legal review, 3D viewers for CAD, or sensitivity models for finance.
Enterprise security: Workforce OAuth sign-in, private Cloud Run ingress, and a sandboxed iframe protect every layer.
Human-in-the-loop governance: Experts inspect and approve high-stakes actions before execution.
Open standard: Portable across compatible hosts, with automatic text fallback.
Broad connectivity: Connect to BigQuery, Agent Platform, Cloud Storage, or internal ERP and CRM systems.
High-level architecture
Three decoupled tiers work together:
Client browser: Shows the chat alongside the MCP App widget in the side panel.
Gemini Enterprise: The default assistant calls tools, the AppBridge proxy relays widget messages, and the connector manages OAuth.
Google Cloud (your project): You deploy and host the MCP server on Cloud Run, which exposes one JSON-RPC endpoint (/mcp), runs background jobs, and serves the single-file HTML widget.
Each tier talks only to its neighbor, letting Gemini Enterprise enforce security and routing.
Authentication with two independent layers
Each user signs in through OAuth 2.0. On every call, Gemini Enterprise sends its service agent token alongside the user's OAuth token:
Layer 1 (Cloud Run IAM): Enforced at Google's edge, this answers "which service may call?" Public access is disabled; unauthorized callers receive HTTP 403.
Layer 2 (In-App OAuth): Enforced inside the application, this answers "which user is calling?" Failed verification returns HTTP 401, prompting the user to sign in again.
Cloud Run IAM cannot distinguish end users, so both layers are required. Outbound calls use a least-privilege service account.
Build, deploy on Google Cloud, and register in Gemini Enterprise
First, build your custom MCP server (exposing POST /mcp and a bundled ui:// HTML widget) using the MCP Apps SDK, or use Google Antigravity  to scaffold and deploy your MCP App with this starter prompt:
Build an MCP App for Gemini Enterprise using the create-mcp-app skill (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/tree/main/plugins/mcp-apps/skills/create-mcp-app).
Workflow: [describe your input data, side-panel UI controls, and approval or export actions].
Generate a single-file HTML widget, a Streamable HTTP backend (POST /mcp) with <2s async tool responses and get_app_state polling, and Cloud Run deployment commands (--no-allow-unauthenticated, --no-cpu-throttling, --min-instances=1).
Once your MCP server code is ready, deploy it to Cloud Run and connect it to Gemini Enterprise:
Step 1: Enable APIs for Cloud Run, Discovery Engine, Agent Platform, and Organization Policy.
Step 2: Deploy your MCP server container to Cloud Run from source (gcloud run deploy <service> --source .) with --no-allow-unauthenticated, --no-cpu-throttling so background work does not freeze between polls, and --min-instances=1.
Step 3: Grant the invoker role (roles/run.invoker) to your Discovery Engine service agent (Layer 1).
Step 4: Create an OAuth 2.0 Web Client with redirect URI https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect(Layer 2).
Step 5: Override the discoveryengine.managed.disableCustomMcpServerConnector constraint and complete the Before you begin prerequisites (roles/discoveryengine.editor for the admin, allowedEgressFqdns for your server and OAuth hosts, and custom_mcpin allowedDataSources if enforced). Then, in the Google Cloud Console under Gemini Enterprise > Data stores > Create data store, select Custom MCP Server and register the connector:
Configuration field
Value
MCP Server URL
https://<your-cloud-run-service>.run.app/mcp
Authorization URL
https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth
Token URL
https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
Client ID and Secret
Your Web OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Secret
Scopes
openid email profile
Enable PKCE Support
Checked (recommended)
Use HTTP Basic Auth
Unchecked (avoids invalid_client errors)
Step 6: Enable actions on your data store. Gemini Enterprise imports your MCP server's tools as actions and disables them by default. In the Cloud Console, open Gemini Enterprise > Data stores > [Your MCP Data Store] > Actions, click Reload custom actions (which calls tools/list on your server), select your model-visible tools, and click Enable actions.
Step 7: Connect the data store to your app. Open Gemini Enterprise > Apps > [Your App] > Connected data stores > Add existing data stores, and select your MCP data store. Connecting it as a data store gives the built-in Default Assistant access to your MCP tools and UI widget directly in main chat ( do not use "Add Agent,"  which is for external sub-agents rather than MCP data stores).
Build your own
An MCP App pairs backend tools with a live workspace in Gemini Enterprise. You do not build a chat frontend or identity pipeline; you deploy one Cloud Run container and attach it as a Data Store, making Gemini Enterprise where enterprise work gets done.
Try Gemini here
Co-build with Google Antigravity here
Build on Google Cloud: MCP Apps Specification (SEP-1865), Cloud Run, and Google Cloud AI.

articles.title: Git 被换掉，LLM 被替代：AI 编码开始反噬传统工具链？
articles.text:
Anthropic 代码量暴涨，GitHub 密钥扫描又慢又贵，两家被迫改造系统。
作者丨郑佳美
编辑丨岑   峰
Git 已经支撑软件开发二十多年，Anthropic 却决定把它换掉。为了让 Claude 持续生成的代码顺利进入开发流程，7 名工程师花了 5 个月，开发出版本控制系统 Scion，并将核心代码仓库迁移过去。今年 5 月，Anthropic 每天平均合并约 2500 项代码变更，到 9 月已超过 3 万项，仅 CI 系统每天就要执行约 2500 万次代码检出。写代码的速度上来了，准备仓库、同步对象和查询历史却越来越费机器。几乎同一时期，GitHub 用微调后的 ModernBERT 替换密钥扫描中的通用 LLM 判断。哥伦比亚大学与 Google DeepMind 等机构则通过 BTTF，把芯片仿真波形转换成 SQLite，让 Agent 使用 SQL 排查异常。Scion 默认在线，BTTF 将波形变成查询接口，GitHub 把高频判断交给分类器。围绕人类开发节奏设计的系统，开始承受 Agent 带来的另一种负载。
01
Git 的离线能力，为什么成了负担
Git 的分布式设计让工程师克隆仓库后，即使断网也能提交、合并、查看历史。但 Anthropic 大量读取代码的任务是始终联网的 CI 作业和 Agent 沙箱，运行几分钟便销毁，可能只需要几个文件、一份 diff，或确认两个提交的祖先关系。为了这些操作准备本地仓库，重复成本越来越高。Anthropic 主分支历史接近 100 GB，压缩工作副本超过 25 GB。若每天 2500 万次检出分别获取完整副本，理论流量会超过 600 PB。公司虽用浅克隆、稀疏检出、快照和数百台 Git 镜像，但镜像仍要同步、快照会过期，历史查询还需补齐对象。仓库越活跃，维护成本越高。Scion 将客户端缩成轻量入口。提交创建、合并、变基与历史查询放到中心服务，本地仅监测文件变化、维护少量缓存，需要工作目录时按需展开。CI 若只想计算 diff，可以直接调用 API，无须完整检出。这牺牲了离线自治，却减少重复初始化。提交格式也变了。Git commit 指向描述仓库状态的目录树，Scion 的 changeset 则以预写日志条目记录相对首个父提交修改过的文件，通过内容寻址指针引用数据。创建 changeset 无须生成 Git packfile，也不用立即移动共享分支，只有 main 等引用更新时，系统才对 Spanner 中的单行记录执行 compare-and-swap。Agent 可以并发生成变更，竞争集中到分支引用移动时。但历史查询仍有难题：增量记录无法直接回答某行是谁改的、文件经历过什么。Scion 为 blame、路径历史与提交图跳表维护 derived data，按父提交关系预计算，或等查询发生后再生成。写入与历史分析可以独立扩展。雷峰网检出时，scn 客户端从目标目录树开始，只请求缺失的 tree 和 blob。请求依次经过节点上的 scion-daemon、区域 scion-cache，再由 scion-server 回源到 Spanner 或对象存储。对象写入后不可变，缓存能够跨任务复用，减少协商、压缩及反复传输。Anthropic 称缓存命中率超过 99%，并限制故障时的回源流量。迁移后，Scion 相较旧 Git 镜像体系的 CPU 和内存需求约缩小 200 倍，检出从分钟级降至秒级，CI 释放约 25% 的 CPU 容量。200 倍说的是基础设施资源占用，并非 Git 操作整体提速。Anthropic 还同步建设 Antique 代码评审、源码搜索、IAM 和批量合并工具，以适配新协议。在线服务的维护也成了新成本。
02
让数据库读波形，Agent 才能追查故障
芯片验证面对的是另一种障碍。RTL 仿真产生的 VCD、FSDB 波形记录大量信号随时间变化的状态，复杂设计的转储可能达到数十 GB，甚至 TB 级。雷峰网工程师可以在波形查看器里沿时间轴寻找异常，Agent 若把原始波形转换成文本，上下文很快便被时间戳、信号名和重复跳变占满。追查其他信号，还可能重复读取文件。另外，人类习惯用眼睛在图表里“大海捞针”，但 Agent 再大的上下文也装不下几十 GB 的物理文件。因此，将这些“死文件”转化为可被 SQL 精准调用的“活接口”，是给 AI 喂数据的最优解。BTTF 把数据访问交给 SQLite。signal_metadata 保存信号名称、类型和层级等静态信息，signal_changes 记录信号 ID、时间戳和变化后的值，两表通过 ID 关联。查询某条信号在指定时刻的状态，SQL 找到该时刻之前最近的变化记录，要检查一段时间内的翻转，则按时间窗过滤与聚合。两次跳变之间状态不变，不能把没有新记录误当作未知。模型只需处理问题与少量返回事件。比如某段握手协议超时，Agent 可以先检索请求与响应信号的变化，再缩小到异常区间，检查时序关系。数据库负责检索，模型决定下一步查什么。查询需对齐信号 ID、时间单位与 RTL 版本。但把波形搬进数据库，并不会自动消除压力。高频时钟产生密集记录，逐行 INSERT 又有事务成本。BTTF 在摄取时建立波形标识到数据库 ID 的映射，统计信号跳变，结合时钟过滤、无跳变信号裁剪和批量插入。未裁剪数据库占用 1420 MB，查询约耗时 410.5 毫秒，过滤时钟和无跳变信号后，规模降到 395 MB，耗时降至 94.8 毫秒。若继续删除跳变率低于平均水平的信号，数据库能缩至 185 MB，但活动覆盖率只剩 64.23%。罕见故障可能恰好出现在几乎不翻转的控制信号上。数据在导入阶段被删除，后面的 Agent 就无法恢复证据。裁剪要服从断言与调试需求。有了 SQL 接口，BTTF 再安排不同 Agent 分工：Orchestration Agent 拆解任务，Analysis Agent 生成查询，Verification Agent 检查断言并关联 RTL 源码，Evaluation Agent 核查时间范围、字段关系与结果完整性。例如 ASSERT_KNOWN 发现信号出现 X/Z 未知状态，系统先锁定违规时刻，再向前检查相关操作数的状态，逐步定位可能的模块。SQL 出错还可以修正后继续。研究团队在 4.2 GB 波形、18450 个信号和 150 条专家标注查询的实验中，取得 95.33% 的执行准确率。Multi-Agent 质量评分比单 Agent 提高 17.3%，平均延迟也增至约 1.96 倍，静态 SVA 检查准确率为 84.62%。方案可支持后仿真分析，但持续摄取与复杂归因仍需验证。
03
为什么密钥扫描换回了分类器
高熵字符串可能是真实凭据，也可能是测试数据、占位符或校验和。正则表达式能快速找到可疑格式，却不擅长判断代码上下文，通用 LLM 可以帮助区分，但候选越多，推理费用和延迟便不断累积。对于需要在代码提交被接受前给出结果的 Push Protection，这种等待会直接影响开发体验。GitHub 保留正则作为候选入口，将后续判断交给微调后的 ModernBERT。它读取候选字符串、密钥类型、变量名、文件路径和附近代码，输出风险分类得分，再由阈值决定是否告警。编码器经过前向计算就能返回类别，不需要像生成式 LLM 那样逐 token 输出解释，适合批量处理同类请求。难点在于 hard negatives：字符串很像密钥，却是无害示例。GitHub 将产品反馈及人工标注、真实仓库中的高召回候选、专门合成的困难负样本组合起来，并按仓库、候选值和关联关系划分训练与评估集，减少相似数据带来的评估偏差。否则模型可能记住文件名，却难以辨认陌生项目中的凭据。部署时，模型导出为 ONNX 并进行 8 位量化，以降低推理资源开销。阈值还需要结合 Precision、Recall 与线上流量校准：太宽松会带来误报，过于严格则可能放过真实密钥。出现新密钥格式时，还需更新训练集和规则。相较旧 LLM 管线，新方案的离线 Precision 提高 13%，Recall 提高 19%。线上 A/B 实验显示，Post-push 扫描执行时间中位数下降 86%，模型服务成本下降超过 98%，按仓库所有者加权的告警接受指标提高 11.5%。这里 98% 指模型服务费用，并非整套安全系统的总成本。分类器也只能判断正则找到的候选，前置规则的覆盖范围仍限制漏报表现。规则发现线索，分类器完成判断，开放式分析仍可交给通用 LLM，避免每次固定判断承担生成式推理成本。
04
接下来可能轮到 CI
GitHub 缩短了安全扫描的反馈时间，代码接下来仍要经过构建、测试和部署。Anthropic 在解决源码检出问题后，也遇到了新的麻烦：一轮测试尚未结束，主分支可能又合入数百甚至数千项修改。继续依赖全局锁会让变更不断积压，放开并发又会带来新的风险，即便某次测试已经通过，它对应的代码状态也可能与准备部署的版本出现差异。这意味着 CI 接下来要处理的，是验证结果如何在高频变更中保持有效。构建缓存需要识别源码与依赖关系的变化，测试记录必须关联具体提交和构建产物，系统还要判断哪些结果能够复用、哪些修改会使此前的验证失效。对于依赖关系复杂的 Monorepo，仅仅增加测试机器，很难解决并发修改带来的版本一致性问题。Anthropic 已经开始强化合并后测试与部署前验证。对普通团队而言，先完善依赖分析、增量测试和构建缓存，比直接重建版本控制系统更现实。随着 Agent 持续提高代码产出，软件工程的瓶颈还会沿着交付链路向后移动。代码进入主分支的速度可以越来越快，但构建、测试与部署之间必须保留可靠的验证关系。未来可能会有越来越多的例子说明，AI 写代码的狂飙突进，最终倒逼着整条软件工程流水线被迫“重做一遍”。工程基础设施的价值，也将更多体现在能否让高速变化的代码持续获得可信的交付依据。参考链接：https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control

articles.title: Amazon opens its AWS Trainium AI chips to every PyTorch developer, no rewrite needed
articles.text:
Amazon's TorchNeuron runs PyTorch on AWS Trainium chips
News
Innovation at Amazon
Amazon opens its AWS Trainium AI chips to every PyTorch developer, no rewrite needed
TorchNeuron lets developers run their existing AI code on AWS Trainium chips with virtually no changes, reducing the friction to adopting new hardware.
Share
Written by Isaac Schultz
4 min read
Key takeaways
Amazon's TorchNeuron runs existing PyTorch code on Trainium with no rewrite.
TorchNeuron will be open-sourced at the PyTorch Conference on October 20.
Startups and enterprises in robotics, video, world models, self-driving cars, speech, drug discovery, LLMs, and finance are already building on it.
Today, 85% of AI researchers and developers write their code in PyTorch. Until now, the hardware that code could run on was far more limited than the code itself, and expanding to new chips meant rewriting and revalidating work that took months to perfect.
Amazon is now closing that gap. With TorchNeuron, the PyTorch code developers already write runs natively on Amazon's AWS Trainium chips, with a single configuration change and no rewrite. TorchNeuron will be released under an open-source license at the PyTorch Conference North America on October 20.
Inside the AWS lab that makes everything you do online feel effortless
In a nondescript building in Cupertino, California, a team of engineers is quietly designing the networking technology that keeps the modern world connected—one wavelength of light at a time.
What does “no code change” actually mean?
Think of your AI code as a car you've spent years fine-tuning. The engine, the suspension—every part working together. A new, more affordable engine comes along with serious horsepower, but installing it would mean tearing down the car and rebuilding it piece by piece. TorchNeuron lets you swap in the new engine without taking the car apart.
In a side-by-side demonstration, Amazon engineers ran the same AI training script on a conventional chip and on Trainium. The only difference was a setting that told the code which chip to use. Results showed that the AI model learned the same things at the same rate.
For developers, this is significant. PyTorch already has a built-in way for new hardware to register itself. TorchNeuron plugs into that standard mechanism, meaning the tools developers already use to test, debug, and scale their AI models all work on Trainium without modification.
How Amazon became one of the world’s top chip companies in a decade
Amazon’s custom silicon business exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate—here’s what that means for customers and the future of AI.
Why TorchNeuron matters for developers and for the industry
The real cost of AI goes beyond the price of a chip. For many companies, especially startups, the most expensive line item is engineering time. Every week a developer spends adapting software for new hardware is a week not spent improving the product. For small teams with limited resources, that trade-off can contribute to whether a company succeeds or fails.
And it’s not just startups. For large enterprises running massive AI fleets, the ability to use the same hardware for both training and inference is a game changer. During off-peak hours, capacity that served inference workloads can shift seamlessly to training jobs, getting more value from the same hardware instead of leaving specialized hardware idle.
By reducing the friction of adopting new hardware, TorchNeuron introduces something the AI industry has largely lacked: meaningful choice. When developers can move between chips without penalty, chipmakers have to earn developers' business, and developers benefit from lower costs and faster iteration.
From voice AI to drug discovery: who's already building on TorchNeuron
TorchNeuron's early adopters span a wide range of AI applications. From real-time voice to molecular design, they share a common thread: they moved to Trainium without rewriting their code.
Cartesia is building intelligence that learns from and interacts with the world the way humans do, starting with conversation. With PyTorch native support on Trainium, Cartesia ran its standard inference pipeline with minimal changes to its PyTorch code. The applications extend into healthcare, too. The Lieber Institute for Brain Development, the largest research institute dedicated to developing new medical interventions for major neuropsychiatric conditions like schizophrenia, uses biological, chemical, and language AI models across drug target and drug discovery. Molecular dynamics simulations are powerful but extremely computationally expensive, and an emerging generation of AI tools offers the potential to accelerate or replace them. TorchNeuron allows the Lieber Institute to explore these strategies on Trainium, from initial model exploration through optimizing performance for bottlenecks.
AWS launches Amazon Bio Discovery to accelerate AI-powered research in life sciences
A new agentic AI application aims to speed up drug development, helping bring new medical treatments to patients faster.
Opening up the chips ecosystem
Amazon's approach extends beyond its own hardware. The company is contributing changes upstream to PyTorch itself, working with the PyTorch community to remove code that ties the framework to specific chips. The goal is to make PyTorch more hardware-agnostic for the entire developer community, not just Trainium users.
To maintain quality, Amazon tests TorchNeuron against hundreds of thousands of AI models on every build, so issues are caught before any customer workload runs.
Hugging Face has enabled native Trainium support directly in its popular AI development tools, allowing developers to work on Trainium natively without requiring any Amazon-specific code.
TorchNeuron integrates with TorchTitan, PyTorch's native distributed training framework, giving developers a standard path for scaling model training across Trainium instances using Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP)—the same tools and patterns they use on any other PyTorch device.
For developers who want to go deeper, TorchNeuron offers tools for scaling training across multiple chips and writing custom low-level code for maximum performance. Amazon has also made a major open-source contribution to vLLM, a popular open-source tool for speeding up inference, and open-sourced its complete set of performance kernels, giving developers a starting point when building their own.
What's next
TorchNeuron supports Trainium2 and Trainium3. It will be released as open-source under the Apache 2.0 license at PyTorch Conference North America on October 20.
TorchNeuron is the latest chapter in Amazon’s decade-long investment in custom silicon. Since acquiring chip design company Annapurna Labs in 2015, Amazon has built four chip families from the ground up, each designed for a specific cloud workload. With TorchNeuron, the company is now making that hardware accessible to any developer who writes in PyTorch.
Learn more about TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium and why AI startups are choosing AWS Trainium to train world models.

# Computer Science > Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing

# Title:Understanding KV Residency in Production-Scale Agentic LLM Workloads

Authors: ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  L12: 
View a PDF of the paper titled Understanding KV Residency in Production-Scale Agentic LLM Workloads, by Mayank Arya and 6 other authors

 L16: > Abstract:Agentic large language model (LLM) applications turn one user request into a sequence of model and tool calls over a growing context. Retaining this context's key-value (KV) state in GPU memory lets later calls reuse it instead of recomputing it, but at fleet scale this needs substantial memory. We characterize four production Microsoft M365 workload traces (Deep Research, Enterprise Assistant, Coding Agent and Enterprise Chat) spanning more than 121 million model calls.
In Deep Research, the application issues 89% of model calls and the median context grows from about 10K to 68K tokens by the 30th call. About 80% of context tokens are served from the prefix cache. With the public Llama-2-70B KV layout standing in for confidential models, one 99th-percentile Deep Research session exceeds the 80 GB HBM of an NVIDIA H100, and holding all live sessions at their peak needs an estimated 501.8 TB of HBM, although inference occupies only 5.6% of that retention time.
Trace-driven replay shows that a one-hour idle cap cuts this ceiling by 3.6x while raising the share of calls that recompute context only from 4.07% to 4.53%. Under tighter budgets, eviction alone is insufficient: at one tenth of the busiest hour's demand, LRU eviction makes 63% of Deep Research calls recompute and clairvoyant furthest-next-use 31%, whereas multi-resolution retention (MRR), which demotes the LRU session's KV state to int4, lowers this to 13.6%.
Placement imposes a separate limit: when the next call reaches a different deployment, cached-context reuse drops from 89% to 29%, and treating KV state as deployment-local raises the recompute floor under unlimited memory from 5.4% to 20.2%. These findings motivate retention that changes the representation of KV state, together with deployment-aware routing or migration. We plan to release AgenticTraceSim, a parametric trace generator, and a residency replay framework.

articles.title: Muse Wonder 建模大翻车，亚历山大·王辩护遭马斯克无情补刀
articles.text:
官方承认 3D 短板，跨模型测试 Harness 不同。
作者丨郑佳美
编辑丨岑   峰
Meta 刚发布的 Muse Wonder，没想到因为一盏熔岩灯，在开发者社区引发了一场关于 AI 模型跑分的争论。10 月 12 日，Meta 推出 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full，主打 Coding Agent、工具调用和长任务执行能力。官方公布的成绩相当亮眼，Wonder Full 在 SWE-Marathon 上拿到 57.5 分，DeepSWE 1.1 达到 79.0 分，已经能够与同期的前沿模型展开竞争。然而，开发者社区 BridgeMind 随后安排了一项 3D 编程测试，要求 Muse Wonder 制作一盏具有透明玻璃外壳、动态熔岩和光照效果的熔岩灯。结果模型只生成了一个红色圆柱体。BridgeMind 随即质疑 Muse Wonder 存在严重的 Benchmaxxing，也就是针对 Benchmark 进行大量优化，成绩看着漂亮，碰上陌生任务却露了怯。连马斯克也忍不住下场，在相关帖子下意味深长地回了一句 Hmm。短短一个词，虽然没有明确表态，却让这场围绕 Meta 新模型的刷分争议又添了几分戏剧性。Meta 首席 AI 官 Alexandr Wang 很快回应，团队确实没有针对 3D 演示游戏进行显式训练，事后看来或许应该补充相关训练，但他仍然希望开发者实际体验 Muse Wonder 的 Coding 能力。雷峰网这场争论有一个重要前提：熔岩灯测试针对的是普通版 Muse Wonder，而 Meta 公布的部分突出成绩来自 Wonder Full，两者存在能力差异。同时，Meta 官方 Model Card 已经明确承认，视觉与空间推理，尤其是 3D 任务，属于 Muse Wonder 的已知短板。但高分模型在陌生任务中遭遇如此明显的失败，依然让人好奇：当前大模型的训练方法究竟在强化哪些能力，Agent Benchmark 又能在多大程度上反映模型的实际水平？
01
奖励机制，
决定模型擅长解决什么问题
Muse Wonder 的表现，与当前大模型越来越依赖 Post-training 提升任务能力的技术路线有关。在 Pre-training 阶段，模型通过大规模数据学习语言、代码、空间关系和其他通用知识。进入 Post-training 后，训练会进一步塑造模型的行为策略，尤其是通过强化学习，让它在特定任务环境中形成更稳定的执行能力。Coding Agent 很适合这类训练。例如，给模型一个存在 Bug 的代码仓库，要求它定位问题、修改文件并运行测试。整个过程可以通过编译结果、单元测试和功能检查获得相对明确的反馈。强化学习系统据此判断哪些操作有效，持续强化能够提高任务成功率的行为。训练规模扩大后，模型逐渐学会一套复杂的软件工程策略，包括如何缩小搜索范围、选择工具、处理报错，以及在多轮修改中维护任务状态。Meta 在官方技术文章中提到，Muse Wonder 接受了多样化长任务训练，并引入 Active Focus，使模型能够在遭遇阻碍后尝试其他方案、恢复执行并继续推进任务。但这类训练依赖一个关键条件：环境必须能够向模型提供有用的反馈。熔岩灯恰好打破了传统 Coding Agent 熟悉的反馈方式。雷峰网从程序实现来看，熔岩灯涉及三维几何、透明材质、光照计算和动态形变。如果使用 Three.js，模型需要构造玻璃灯罩，为内部熔岩生成不规则的几何形态，再通过时间变量或噪声函数驱动形状变化。这些代码即使能够正常执行，画面仍然可能完全错误。例如，透明材质的参数配置不当，玻璃就可能变成不透明的实体，熔岩形状缺少连续变化机制，内部效果就可能退化为静态色块。编译器和单元测试很难直接判断这些视觉问题。这意味着，Agent 还需要具备一套视觉反馈机制，通过渲染截图、识别画面偏差，再把视觉问题转换成代码修改。单纯增加工具调用次数或延长推理时间，并不能替代这一环节。Muse Wonder 生成红色圆柱体的具体原因，仍然需要完整执行轨迹才能确定。可能是模型没有建立正确的空间结构，也可能是图形工具使用不当，或者生成错误后缺少有效的视觉检查。Alexandr Wang 承认没有针对 3D 演示进行显式训练，至少说明这一任务没有获得与重点 Coding 场景相同的训练投入。
02
Agent 的高分，
已包含型之外的系统能力
Muse Wonder 的争议还有一层容易被忽略的问题：今天的 Agent Benchmark，已经无法简单理解为给语言模型出题。以 SWE-Marathon 为例，它考察的是持续性软件工程任务。模型需要在代码仓库中执行多个操作，读取文件、调用终端、修改代码，并通过测试验证结果。这类任务的完成率，除了依赖底层模型，还会受到 Harness 的直接影响。Harness 是围绕模型构建的执行框架，负责组织工具接口、管理上下文、保存任务状态，以及处理执行过程中的异常。例如，一个 Agent 正在修复复杂的软件问题，连续运行测试后产生了数千行终端日志。如果系统将全部日志直接追加到上下文中，模型可能逐渐失去对原始需求和关键错误的把握。设计更完善的 Harness 可以自动提取重要报错、压缩无效信息，并维护当前修改进度。当任务执行时间延长，这种上下文管理能力会直接影响系统能否持续工作。错误恢复机制同样如此。假设 Agent 已经修改了多个文件，却在后续测试中发现早期修改存在问题。如果执行系统能够保留检查点、定位引入错误的步骤，并局部回滚，就有机会避免重新执行整条任务链。此外，推理预算也会影响成绩。允许 Agent 使用更多 Token、执行更多工具调用，或者尝试多个候选方案，相当于增加了搜索空间和纠错机会，代价则是更高的运行成本。Meta 官方 Model Card 对此有明确说明。在 SWE-Marathon 评测中，GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.1 分别使用 Codex 与 Claude Code 执行系统，因此这一项目并非统一 Harness 条件下的受控比较。Muse Wonder Full 的 57.5 分还使用了 xhigh 推理档位。这些配置差异不会自动使成绩失效，却会影响成绩的解释方式。如果要比较基础模型的推理与规划能力，就需要尽可能统一工具环境、Harness 和推理预算。但如果比较的是能够投入生产的 Coding Agent 产品，完整执行系统的表现本身就具有工程价值。对于实际开发者而言，Agent 能否稳定处理长任务，往往比单轮生成代码的质量更有意义。问题在于，当各种系统配置被压缩成排行榜上的一个分数时，外部很难判断成绩增长究竟来自模型推理能力、执行框架优化，还是更充足的计算资源。这要求 Agent 评测提供更详细的执行信息，包括任务完成率、Token 消耗、工具调用次数、运行时间以及失败恢复情况，否则相近的 Benchmark 成绩，可能对应完全不同的工程体验。
03
Meta 自己也在研究 Benchmaxxin
有意思的是，Muse Wonder 官方技术文章专门设置了 Capabilities That Generalize 章节，讨论的恰好是 Benchmaxxing 背后的问题。Meta 指出，两个模型即使在常见 Benchmark 中取得相似成绩，处理陌生任务的能力仍然可能存在较大差距。为研究这一现象，团队将测试任务划分为两类：一类是 Post-training 重点优化的 In-distribution 任务，另一类是没有进行针对性优化的 Out-of-distribution 任务。研究人员进一步比较 Muse Spark 1.3 与 Muse Wonder Full，在不同推理预算下的表现变化。按照 Meta 公布的实验结果，Wonder Full 在陌生任务上的表现，相比前代模型对应的能力变化趋势有所提升。Meta 认为，这与更强的基础模型有关，基础能力的改善使 Post-training 收益能够更有效地迁移到其他任务。但这里存在一个评测设计问题：陌生任务究竟陌生到什么程度？对于长期训练代码修复的 Agent，换一个未曾接触过的代码仓库，仍然属于相近的软件工程任务。如果进一步更换编程框架、引入陌生 API，模型就需要重新理解工具环境。而制作 3D 熔岩灯，除了软件开发，还引入了空间建模、材质渲染和视觉质量判断。它对能力组合提出了更大的变化。因此，分布外泛化不能只用一个综合平均分来描述。不同任务之间的距离、需要补充的知识，以及评价结果的方法，均会影响模型表现。判断模型是否存在严重的 Benchmark 过拟合，也需要系统性实验。单个熔岩灯失败只能说明模型没有完成当前任务，无法直接证明它针对公开题库进行了过度优化。更合理的方法，是在相同执行条件下逐步改变任务分布。例如，先测试模型能否修复陌生仓库中的 Bug，再要求它使用未见过的 API 构建程序，随后加入缺少明确测试脚本的视觉开发任务。这样既可以观察模型在软件工程内部的能力迁移，也能检查它跨越任务类型时出现的性能变化。评测还可以进一步改变环境约束，例如临时替换工具接口、引入新的错误信息，或者要求 Agent 自行设计验证程序。这些设置能够检验模型面对陌生条件时，是否具备阅读文档、建立方案、验证假设和修正错误的能力。 对于熔岩灯这样的任务，除了检查最终画面，还应该记录模型是否主动使用截图工具、能否识别材质与几何错误，以及在获得反馈后是否能够作出有效修改。相比单纯统计成功率，这类执行轨迹更有助于判断 Agent 的能力缺口，也能够区分知识不足、工具错误和反馈机制失效等不同原因。随着公开 Benchmark 越来越成熟，模型研发会持续利用已知任务结构改进训练方法。动态任务、隐藏测试以及更完整的执行过程评估，将成为补充固定排行榜的重要手段。
04
高分之外，还需要看清能力边界
Muse Wonder 的熔岩灯失败，无法抹去它在软件工程任务上的进步，也不足以证明 Meta 存在严重刷分行为。但开发者确实需要重新理解今天的 Agent 成绩。当 Post-training、工具系统和推理预算共同参与能力提升，排行榜上的高分，反映的是一套特定条件下的任务完成表现。它对模型选型具有参考意义，但使用场景越复杂，单一分数能够提供的信息就越有限。未来的 Agent 研发仍然会继续强化 Coding、工具调用和长任务执行，但当模型逐渐能够承担独立的软件工程工作时，它需要处理的问题会不断超出既有训练任务的范围。届时，能否识别陌生环境中的问题、自行建立有效的验证方法，并通过反馈持续修正执行策略，将直接影响 Agent 可以承担多大范围的实际工作。一盏熔岩灯没有给出 Muse Wonder 的完整能力答案，却提供了一个具体的提醒：模型在熟悉任务中取得的成绩，与它在未知环境中能够独立完成的工作，仍然需要分别检验。

articles.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22594v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, and collaboration does not consistently protect against it. Existing defenses help only partly: they miss injections that look like ordinary clinical text. Yet when asked to check the injected text against the patient's findings, a model that followed the injection usually rejects it. We therefore propose a training-free defense that verifies the clinical judgments behind the system's decision. Following clinical practice, it separates the patient's findings from clinical judgments, such as diagnoses, recommendations and instructions, and checks each judgment against the findings alone, so the decision rests only on supported judgments. Our defense outperforms all baselines on every benchmark, lowering attack success on MedQA to 4-7% while maintaining accuracy on cases without an attack, and remains effective with a medical model and against defense-aware and adaptive attacks.

articles.title: 光量子计算，距离真正的产业化还有多远？
articles.text:
导语：产业化落地，光量子计算的新考场
记者：郭思
编辑：包永刚
摩尔定律走到红利尽头，AI、新药研发、新材料探索对算力的需求还在不断扩张。依靠持续堆 GPU 提升算力的老路越来越不划算，存算一体、Chiplet、光互连等技术竞相寻找算力增量，量子计算因此被寄予厚望，光量子路线更是长期收到行业关注与讨论。它在实验室创下震撼的量子优越性记录，其工程化进展与产业化时间表也始终是业界关注的焦点。
光量子计算，会成为下一代算力的破局钥匙，还是一场尚待产业化验证的技术革命？
2026 年 10 月 14 日深圳湾芯展，图灵量子创始人、上海交大无锡光子芯片研究院院长金贤敏带领团队在同一天三项动作接连落地，光子芯片产业合作签约、先进智算联盟扩容，以及粤港澳大湾区量超智融合算力中心共建签约。
这一连串产业布局，提供了一个跳出纸面参数的视角：量子计算的对手，早已不只是物理，芯片工程、产业链生态、商业落地的大考，已然开场。
量子计算的对手，早就不只是物理指标
量子计算走入大众视野，并非最近一两年才发生的新事。伴随摩尔定律见顶，算力供需矛盾日益凸显，量子计算的价值被重新放到聚光灯下。
数耀量生 CTO 邱迪生，曾对传统深度学习与量子计算的求解逻辑做出形象对比：深度学习常用的随机梯度下降，相当于在局部点位附近小范围试探，摸索迭代前进方向，属于局部搜索，很容易出现震荡徘徊；而量子计算能够一次性扫描完整的解空间地形，直接定位最优解，他将这种核心差异概括为 “量子全局最优性”。
图灵量子首席科学家金贤敏则认为，量子计算之所以能够获得长期关注，并不源于某一项单点应用，它是继牛顿力学体系之后，可以系统性赋能整个科学发展的底层基础方向。
早在上世纪四五十年代，晶体管、激光器、核能等成果，就已经完成了第一波量子技术的产业化应用；而当下，人类对量子体系、物质微观体系的操控能力实现跃升，叠加 AI 算力需求爆发，才推动量子计算走到产业发展的关键窗口。
行业经久不衰的疑问依旧存在：超导、离子阱、光量子、中性原子，多条量子技术路线同台竞技，谁能走到商业化的终点？
纵观当前行业进展，在众多技术路径里，公开实验中同时达成 “可制造、可扩展、已演示量子优越性” 三大条件的，主要集中在光量子与超导两大路线。
超导路线起步较早。2025年，中国科学技术大学团队构建的105比特超导量子计算原型机“祖冲之三号”，在量子随机线路采样任务上比当时最快超算快15个数量级，刷新了超导体系量子计算优越性纪录。
相比之下，离子阱路线门保真度最高、相干时间长，但系统扩展慢，目前处于高精度模拟和原理演示阶段；中性原子路线阵列规模扩展潜力大，但门保真度和速度仍在追赶，工程化成熟度较低。
光量子路线则在特定问题上展现出更强的算力优势。2026年，“九章四号”可编程光量子原型机首次操纵和探测3050个光子，在高斯玻色采样任务上比全球最快超算快10⁵⁴倍，建立了国际最强的量子计算优越性。
更重要的是，光量子路线正从“实验室装置”走向“可制造平台”。PsiQuantum发布的Omega光子芯片组，由格罗方德45纳米产线批量制造，单量子比特态制备与测量保真度达99.98%，芯片间互联保真度99.72%，并计划在澳大利亚和美国建设数据中心级量子计算中心。那么图灵量子TuringQ Gen3则将技术重点放在大规模片上集成、空时复用扩展以及量子算力与经典计算体系的融合上。
环境稳定成落地最为关键的突破点
量子计算并不缺“性能故事”。各家机器在特定任务上早已展示量子优越性，超导路线也在不断刷新比特数纪录。但产业客户真正关心的不是实验室峰值，而是机器能不能稳定跑在客户现场。
这也是为什么行业正在从比拼物理比特转向交付逻辑比特。中金公司在2026年的分析中指出，量子计算仍处于从含噪声中等规模量子时代向容错量子计算演进的早期阶段，物理比特数量、门保真度、纠错阈值和系统稳定性仍是关键不确定性。
各技术路线尚未突破规模化与容错两大核心瓶颈，量子软件、算法和工程化能力也仍需补课。换句话说，量子计算要真正进入产业，必须完成从能演示到能稳定运行的跨越。
而在这场光电交替里，图灵量子握着的牌格外引人注目。
“我们的机器对环境没有要求。”金贤敏说。从第二代 TuringQ Gen2开始，图灵量子的光量子计算机都是采用标准 IDC 机柜形态，可在室温运行。对产业客户来说，不必为它单独建特殊的底纹运行环境，可以像一台服务器那样进现有的数据中心。
2026 年 9 月图灵量子推出第三代大规模芯片级可扩展光量子计算机TuringQ Gen3。相比前两代产品，TuringQ Gen3实现了全芯片化架构，基于高速可编程薄膜铌酸锂光量子芯片，走空时复用架构。其中高斯玻色采样计算单元叫"致远3号"。官方口径是单芯片万光子级、百万模式数，在设定的损耗边界内实现芯片级量子优越性。
至于如何做到，就涉及到了另一个在光量子芯片中的关键概念——光损耗。与电子芯片制造看中制程不同，在光量子芯片里，损耗是一个非常重要的指标，过高的损耗率，不只是“信号变弱”，而是可能直接让光子丢失、干涉失效，进而导致计算出错。芯片规模越大、光路越长，光子经过的器件越多，损耗就会层层叠加，所以把整条链路的损耗压低，是光量子芯片能否走向大规模化的关键。
为了做到这一点，团队把薄膜铌酸锂光量子芯片的光子线路传输损耗降到 0.03 dB/cm，关键单器件插入损耗低于 0.1 dB，光纤—芯片单端耦合损耗达到 0.9 dB/facet，晶圆级量子光源光谱纯度超过 99%。这意味着，光子从产生、在芯片内传输、经过器件到进出芯片的每一步损耗都被大幅压低，信号也足够纯净，从而为更大规模、更稳定的光量子计算打下了基础。
而数字的背后，则是一条真正跑起来的工程闭环。在金贤敏牵头推动下，上海交大无锡光子芯片研究院建成了国内首条光子芯片中试线，形成了“设计—制造—测试—反馈—再迭代”的晶圆级工艺闭环，芯片迭代周期已缩短到 2 至 3 周。也就是说，它不只是在实验室里搭出一台样机，而是在尝试用半导体工程的方法持续降低损耗、提升一致性、扩大规模。
而金贤敏的产业化底气，并不仅仅来自于这些书面参数，而是逐渐清晰的商业化路径。金贤敏将光量子计算比作一把“锤子”，产业化的关键在于找到能够真正发挥其优势的“钉子”。目前，图灵量子正围绕整机交付、算力服务和量子智算中心建设探索多元化商业模式，从提供光量子计算设备，到开放量子算力服务，再到推动量子算力与现有智算基础设施融合，逐步打通从技术研发到产业应用的商业闭环，并已在生物医药、金融等领域开展应用合作。
这或许是判断一条光量子路线更为诚实的标准：不是论文发了多少、演示跑得多快，而是有没有人在它上面持续付费。
一台机器进不了产业，所以得先修路
回看湾芯展期间的三项产业动作，一个值得深究的问题摆在面前：一家量子计算公司，为什么要同时介入上游材料、下游软件工具、行业联盟标准，还要投入算力中心建设。
答案其实很简单，金贤敏表述，即便做出可用的量子硬件，也不等于完成产业化。量子算力要产生商业价值，要能被调度平台识别，能够面向行业用户开放调用，单靠硬件单点突破无法跑通完整闭环，整套上下游配套体系必须同步跟上。
在光子芯片的产业协作上，天通股份输出材料，Luceda 提供设计软件工具，上海交大无锡光子芯片研究院负责制造落地，设备、材料、软件、应用几方经过长时间磋商达成合作，目标就是协同完善光子芯片上下游生态。
而先进智算联盟 FAIC 的推进，则是产业层面的协同探索。这个联盟最早在2022 年由图灵量子、沐曦股份、优刻得、脑虎科技四家发起，覆盖量子计算、算力芯片、算力中心建设、脑机接口不同赛道，此前也获得上海市及市经信委的认可。
金贤敏坦言，今年图灵量子担任轮值主席，联盟内部要做一次方向抉择，最终选择了扩容，傅利叶智能这类具身智能企业被纳入进来，成员从最初四家扩展到数十家。金贤敏的判断是，仅靠少数几家机构抱团，很难撬动产业规模，更多不同领域主体参与，新型算力芯片迭代、智算中心落地、算力赋能行业应用，才有规模化发展的基础。
另一边粤港澳量超智融合算力中心，瞄准的是量子算力实际部署与调用的现实难题。图灵量子联合亚洲算力、智城算网共同推进该项目，对标海外已经批量落地的量子‑经典混合算力中心。
金贤敏提到，欧美已经建成几十到上百个同类算力节点，国内还没有成型的标杆。这个项目不是停留在纸面的框架意向，建设计划已经敲定，核心要实现 QPU、CPU、GPU 之间的联调，真正把量子算力纳入平台调度体系。英伟达此前已经推出 GPU 对接量子计算机的量超融合方案，这也是整个行业已经显现的趋势。
把这一系列动作放在一起，我们就能清晰的看到图灵量子的产业逻辑。光量子计算不能停留在硬件能力演示阶段。
量子算力需要接入智算中心，成为可被调度的标准算力单元，供给行业客户使用。联盟和算力中心承担的实际作用，是抹平不同技术主体之间的适配门槛，推动量子算力脱离实验室演示属性，转化成可以采购、能够实际投入业务的产业资源。
剩下的，还是工程化的事
外界总爱用 “狼来了” 看待光量子计算，本质上是混淆了科学突破与产业成熟的时间差。如今光量子已经跨过单纯原理验证阶段：它有足以震撼行业的量子优越性成果，也出现了常温机柜化整机、中试工艺闭环、付费产业客户，甚至开始布局量超智融合算力中心，尝试把量子算力变成智算体系中可调度的标准单元。
但亮眼参数不等于产业胜利。赛道依然被现实枷锁束缚：高性能光子材料和关键器件的稳定供应、晶圆级制造良率、复杂系统中的损耗控制，以及大规模量子纠错与容错计算能力，都还需要持续突破。行业的主战场，已经从发表论文、刷新光子数纪录，转移到产线良率、系统长期稳定性、软件生态与客户付费意愿。
这并不意味着物理层面的挑战已经结束。恰恰相反，大规模光量子计算还需要在光源、损耗、探测、量子纠错和系统架构等方面持续攻关。科学突破与工程化能力，需要同步向前。
量子计算未必会很快颠覆现有算力，但也绝非虚妄的故事。
技术的狼没有立刻扑到产业面前，但它确实已经走出了实验室，只是还要翻越制造、工程和应用的高山，才会真正抵达商用的旷野。
