articles.title: 正面硬刚DeepSeek！MiniMax M3.1 Flash发布，输出卷到200+TPS，价格砍到1/2
articles.text:
智东西
作者 | 王涵
编辑 | 漠影
火爆AI圈的匿名模型Space Bunny，终于被认领了！
智东西10月19日报道，刚刚，MiniMax 正式发布M3.1 Flash，定位为Coding/Agent优化轻量级模型，拥有100万token上下文。
几乎前后脚，10月17日，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017上线。（梁圣又掀桌了！DeepSeek新模型斩杀GPT-6，许愿式编程时代降临）
根据M3.1 Flash的基准测试成绩，该模型在Agentic任务、编程、Computer Use及网络安全能力等方面实现了大幅提升，与DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017基本追平。
价格上也进一步打穿了“斩杀线”。M3.1 Flash的输入价格为每百万Token 1元，输出价格为每百万Token 4元，缓存读取价格为每百万Token 0.1元。据MiniMax团队发布信息，在Agentic类任务中，该模型的综合使用成本较前代模型降低了70%。
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017定价为闲时输入（缓存命中）每百万Token 0.02元、未命中每百万Token 1.0元、输出每百万Token 4.0元，高峰时段输入（缓存命中）每百万Token 0.04元，未命中每百万Token 2.0元，输出每百万Token 8.0元。
能力上你追我赶，价格上更是不甘示弱，这两款“Flash”模型接连落地，国产模型在Flash段位第一次有了“双强”的格局。
一、拆解硬核成绩单：性价比之王，多项成绩超过Kimi K3和GLM-5.3
Space Bunny匿名期积累的社区口碑，让正式版的M3.1 Flash承载了极高的期待，那它成绩究竟如何呢？
在复杂任务与自动化上，M3.1 Flash实现反超。 在评估智能体长程、多步骤真实任务的Agents’ Last Exam中，M3.1 Flash跑出了29.6%的通过率和739元的成本，处在“低成本-高通过率”的最前沿区间，性能远超同价位模型。
而在考察真实业务流程跨应用自动化的Automation-Bench v1.0.6中，M3.1 Flash拿下62.2分，反超了DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017的60.5分，更是将Opus 5甩在身后。
在编程领域，M3.1 Flash与DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017各有侧重。 在DeepSWE v1.1测试上，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017得分为77.0分，排名第一。M3.1 Flash取得73.7分，距离Opus 5仅差0.3分。
在代码修复测试SWE Refore Bench中，M3.1 Flash拿到23.0分，直接是DeepSeek成绩的两倍以上。
在专业与安全领域，M3.1 Flash也稳居第一梯队。 在金融工具调用的BankerToolBench中，它以76.2分与Opus 5并列第一；网络安全CyberGym测试中，其以82.2分与GLM-5.3同处第一梯队；无工具学术推理测试HLE w/o tools中，M3.1 Flash取得43.4分，略高于DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017。
从榜单可以看出，M3.1 Flash绝不是一个“偏科”的模型，它在Agent和自动化上的成绩，甚至已经超越了行业旗舰大模型。
完整榜单如下：
二、发布相隔48小时，DeepSeek和MiniMax打出“双强”格局
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017与M3.1 Flash，同样定位Flash，在两天内接连发布，且基准测试成绩如此接近，让人自然而然地看到了一个全新的格局：双强并立。
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash采用稀疏MoE架构，总参数量552B，但推理时输入仅激活8B 参数、输出激活16B。它在性能与速度上都超过了上一代Pro版本，但定价压得很低。这款模型的发布，直接让开发者们看到了Flash模型的“旗舰能力”。
顺着DeepSeek撕开的口子，M3.1 Flash往前更近了一步。
在M3.1 Flash还处于匿名期时，上线短短几天内，它便在OpenCode的调用量榜单稳居第二，在OpenRouter上一度排名第一。
有网友用Claude Opus 5、GPT-6 Sol和Gemini 3.8 Flash与Space Bunny进行比较，用最高思考级别构建火箭发射场景。该网友称Space Bunny仅花了三分钟，最终呈现的效果能和Opus 5相比，速度也很快。
智东西也第一时间进行了实测，认为该模型效果直逼GPT-6 Astra（神秘模型“太空兔”火了，效果直逼GPT-6 Astra，10万人围观）
Space Bunny匿名期间让开发者惊艳的响应速度在正式版中也得到完整保留。据MiniMax团队透露，他们进一步优化了M3.1 Flash的推理效率，使用了更激进的稀疏注意力架构，日常使用场景下的输出速度可达200+TPS （Tokens per Second），中位数（P50）稳定达到170+TPS。
定价上，M3.1 Flash的输入输出价格约为DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017高峰期价格的一半，与空闲时期价格持平。
▲M3.1 Flash与DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017价格对比（智东西制表）
可以说，这两个模型就像开发者工具箱里两套各有侧重的工具，开发者能根据任务需求灵活调度。
例如，需要代码生成效率和缓存成本控制时，开发者们可以选择DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017；面对长程Agent任务、跨应用自动化或多模态驱动的开发流程时，M3.1 Flash则可以作为第一选项。
此前外界对MiniMax的印象，或许多集中在多模态领域。但无论是Space Bunny匿名期间的调用量霸榜，还是M3.1 Flash正式发布的基准测试成绩单，都证明了MiniMax在Agent与自动化方向的竞争力，也让用户对其后续Pro模型的发布充满期待。
结语：Flash模型上桌，不再是“平替”
DeepSeek和MiniMax的两款Flash模型接替上场，让业内看到了Flash模型的实力。
Flash模型正在撕掉 “预算不足才退而求其次” 的旧标签。从基准测试结果来看，它已能在部分核心指标上，跻身旗舰模型的同台对比序列，同时保留自身在推理速度与成本上的固有优势。
从性价比上看，Flash模型或许最接近真实使用场景的模型类型，国产模型首次形成DeepSeek和MiniMax“双强并立”的竞争格局。
对开发者和企业来说，模型工具箱中，自此新增了一个可以按需调度的优质选择。

articles.title: 曝苹果首款“消费级机器人”，定价1000美元
articles.text:
智东西
编译 | 栗子
编辑 | 云鹏
智东西10月20日消息，苹果上周发布了售价299美元的智能家居屏HomeView，外界普遍将其视为苹果补齐智能家居短板的第一步。但彭博社马克·古尔曼在最新一期《Power On》通讯中披露了一个更值得关注的信号：
苹果已经在开发HomeView的高端版本，内部代号J595，配备电动机械臂，屏幕可360度旋转，并能通过语音识别自动转向正在说话的人。这款产品计划2027年或2028年发布，定位高于HomeView，而非替代品。
换句话说，HomeView是苹果先摆上桌的“降级版”，J595才是它真正想讲的故事。
一、J595的由来：从造车项目遗产到桌面机械臂
苹果开发J595并非临时起意。从已披露的信息看，苹果的家庭机器人计划最早可追溯至2022年，当年公司批准了代号J595的桌面机器人项目。该项目的设想是把一块类似iPad的显示屏安装在机械臂上，让设备能根据用户位置调整朝向，同时兼顾视频通话、语音交互和智能家居控制。由于外形让人联想到皮克斯动画中的跳跳灯，这款产品后来被外界称为“皮克斯跳跳灯”。
▲“皮克斯跳跳灯”概念图（图源：AI生成）
但J595在早期并未获得最高优先级。真正的转折发生在2024年：苹果终止了持续近十年的造车项目“泰坦”（Titan），部分工程师转向机器人业务，计算机视觉、自主导航和运动控制等技术积累也被重新调配到J595上。该项目由苹果技术副总裁凯文·林奇（Kevin Lynch）牵头，他曾负责Apple Watch和自动驾驶汽车项目，团队规模达到数百人。
供应链方面，富士康旗下鸿准（Hongzhun）被指为J595的早期供应商，负责电子组件和外壳；组装测试则可能集中在越南，由比亚迪承接。定价方面，早期传闻指向约1000美元（约合人民币6721元），远高于HomeView的299美元，符合其“高端型号”的定位。
二、为什么非要加一条机械臂：HomeView自己暴露了答案
HomeView的硬件并不差：7英寸屏幕、A18芯片、8GB内存，支持FaceTime、Siri语音控制和智能家居中枢功能。但它有一个被苹果自己的广告“放大”了的缺陷：屏幕不会动。古尔曼在通讯中描述了一则HomeView广告——一家人把设备传来传去，每个人都要亲手把屏幕转向自己。对一个号称让家庭科技交互更自然的设备来说，这个动作本身就说明问题。
▲苹果HomeView概念图（图源：AI生成）
J595的机械臂解决的正是这件事。9英寸屏幕、360度旋转、语音识别定位说话人——用户在厨房走动时屏幕跟着转，一家人围坐时屏幕自动朝向发言者。古尔曼对此的评价是：这可能让J595更像一个“共享的家庭伙伴”，而不是一块固定在台面上的显示屏。
更深一层的原因是数据。苹果在机器人领域并非没有尝试过合作，但造车项目终止后，苹果选择把机器人团队从AI部门转入硬件工程高级副总裁约翰·特努斯（John Patrick Ternus，其是一位在苹果工作了25年的“老兵”，于2026年9月1日正式接替库克，成为苹果历史上第八任CEO）麾下，战略地位明显提升。
桌面机械臂不需要解决家庭环境中的自主导航难题，避开了移动机器人最棘手的技术障碍，同时又能产生传统智能屏无法提供的物理交互数据——屏幕朝向、用户位置、语音指令与动作的对应关系。这些数据，正是苹果训练下一代家庭AI交互的基础。
三、旋转屏早有先例，但苹果真正的考验在生态与Siri
J595在形态上并非首创。亚马逊早在2021年就推出了Echo Show 10，同样配备可旋转屏幕和语音追踪能力，售价约200美元。谷歌Nest Hub虽然不支持旋转，但以约100美元的价格长期占据智能屏市场的入门位置。
HomeView 299美元的定价，已经接近Nest Hub的三倍。J595如果落在1000美元区间，将进入一个几乎没有直接竞品的价位——但这也意味着苹果需要自己说服消费者，一条机械臂值这个差价。
市场数据也不站在苹果这边。Parks Associates（其成立于1986年，在国际上被广泛认可，专注于新兴消费科技产品与服务的市场研究和咨询）2026年的数据显示，在美国拥有智能家居设备的家庭中，37%使用亚马逊Alexa或Ring，12%使用谷歌平台，苹果仅占8%。
HomeView的应用生态同样受限：没有独立应用商店，依赖iPhone传输应用，主流视频服务中仅支持Apple TV，Netflix和YouTube均无专属应用。古尔曼直言，说服已经深度使用亚马逊或谷歌设备的用户切换，并不容易。
但真正的变量不在机械臂，而在Siri。J595的硬件路径已经相对清晰，但它的核心体验，如语音识别、用户定位、个性化回应，却高度依赖苹果的AI能力。而苹果AI的交付节奏，恰恰是HomeView延期近两年的直接原因：硬件早已就绪，成品在仓库里等了大约一年，等的是新版Siri。
在中国市场，这个变量更加复杂。据多家媒体报道，Apple Intelligence计划于2026年12月随iOS 27.3进入中国大陆，但首批功能中升级版Siri AI预计缺席，图像生成和文本生成能力也将受限。苹果已与阿里巴巴合作，引入通义千问模型以满足本地监管要求，并于2026年9月获得相关许可。
这意味着，如果J595在中国上市，其最核心的语音转向和智能交互功能在初期可能无法完整可用。对于一款以“跟着说话的人转”为卖点的设备来说，这不是一个小问题。
隐私则是另一条隐线。J595的摄像头和麦克风需要持续待命，以识别说话人和环境变化。尽管苹果一贯强调端侧处理和隐私保护，但一个始终“在线”、带机械运动能力的家庭设备，仍然会引发比固定屏幕更直接的隐私顾虑。
四、苹果在赌“家庭AI入口”的下一种形态
摩根士丹利2025年曾预测，到2040年苹果机器人业务的年收入可能达到1330亿美元。这个数字是否成立，取决于一个更根本的判断：家庭是否需要一台会动的屏幕。
苹果的答案显然是肯定的。J595的立项逻辑，是把造车项目积累的运动控制、计算机视觉和AI能力，迁移到一个比汽车简单得多、但比智能屏复杂得多的品类上。它不需要在家庭里自主导航，只需要在一个桌面尺度上完成“感知—判断—转向”的闭环，技术风险可控，但体验差异也足够明显。
如果J595按计划在2027至2028年落地，它将成为苹果第一个真正意义上的“消费级机器人”产品，而非智能音箱的附属屏幕。这条路能否走通，不取决于机械臂转得是否顺滑，而取决于Siri AI能否在J595上市时，兑现HomeView已经等了两年仍未完全兑现的承诺。
结语：机械臂不是答案，Siri才是
J595用一条机械臂解决了HomeView“屏幕不会动”的尴尬，但这只是苹果家庭AI故事的开头。真正决定它成败的，不是电机和关节，而是Siri能否在2027年兑现HomeView已经等了两年仍未完全兑现的承诺。
亚马逊Echo Show 10已经把旋转屏做到200美元价位，苹果想用1000美元的J595说服消费者，靠的不能只是苹果标和更顺滑的转动。
机械臂虽然能让屏幕转向人，但只有足够聪明的AI，才能让人愿意转向苹果。
来源：苹果官网、彭博社、9to5mac、Fiance.Biggo、Appleinsider、Ascendants

articles.title: Trajectory-Guided Steering: Mitigating Spurious Feature Bias in Clinical Classification
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22618v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Existing inference-time corrections either need counterfactual data built around the specific spurious feature or behave unpredictably. We observe that how a model's preference between answers evolves across layers, its prediction trajectory, indicates for each document whether a correction is likely to help. We propose Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS), which decides from the trajectory alone whether to correct each prediction and in which direction, with no counterfactual data and no knowledge of the spurious feature. On 16 clinical classification tasks from i2b2, TGS fixes 17.7% of errors while breaking only 1.3% of correct predictions and stays net-positive across all tested hyperparameter settings; all baselines are net-negative or near zero. The same corrections reduce reliance on the spurious feature: on the most affected diseases, gender-swap inconsistency falls sharply (hypertension 53.5% -> 38.0%, diabetes 35.1% -> 21.5%). Applying the correction to every document instead raises breaks on correct positive predictions from 0.1% to 6.4%, so per-document selection is essential. TGS also transfers to three model families and three other clinical and biomedical datasets.

articles.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22721v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.

articles.title: Causal Edit Serialization
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22820v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

articles.title: 蓝厂最强旗舰！vivo X500 Ultra关键参数出炉：2K屏+骁龙8EE6
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，在此前vivo X500系列新品发布会的媒体专访环节中，vivo产品副总裁黄韬透露，vivo X500 Ultra会正常迭代，新品将在明年三四月份正式亮相，主要面向专业创作者。
今天下午，博主数码闲聊站曝光了vivo X500 Ultra的关键参数。该机将采用6.85英寸2K 144Hz LTPO直屏，屏幕由京东方提供，搭载高通第六代骁龙8超级至尊版旗舰平台（快科技注：以下简称骁龙8EE6），并支持3D超声波屏幕指纹。
对比Pro Max，vivo X500 Ultra最大升级点之一是芯片平台由天玑升级为高通骁龙8EE6。这是高通旗下首款2nm芯片，也是安卓阵营最强悍的手机芯片。
CPU方面，骁龙8EE6搭载定制Oryon架构，采用2+3+3八核设计，超大核主频突破5GHz。这是行业首个突破5GHz的移动CPU，CPU性能较上代提升13%，能效提升37%，任务调度与数据访问效率也进一步优化。
除了搭载最强悍的骁龙平台，vivo X500 Ultra还将拥有堪称“灭霸级”的影像实力。不过，具体细节目前暂时不得而知。
作为参考，在今年3月份，vivo X300 Ultra搭载了一套专业影像系统，配备85mm蔡司超级长焦，采用的是vivo与三星联合研发的HP0传感器，并首次在长焦端实现了3度微云台级光学防抖，达到了CIPA 7.0专业级防抖标准。
配合其3+2蔡司大师镜头群，vivo X300 Ultra覆盖了从14mm超广角到400mm超长焦的全焦段，并支持全焦段直出超清照片。作为迭代旗舰，X500 Ultra的影像实力值得期待。

articles.title: v0.5.22

# Highlights

*950 PRs from 245 contributors.*

## New models

| Model | Type | Cookbook |
|---|---|---|
| Clef / Clef Flash | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Cloudflare/clef) |
| PPLX-Decider v1 / v1.1 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Perplexity/PPLX-Decider-v1.1-27B) |
| EmbeddingGemma 2 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma2) |
| LLaDA2.2 | LLM / VLM | |
| HunyuanImage-3.0-Instruct | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Tencent/HunyuanImage3) |
| Kandinsky 6 / Kandinsky 6 SR | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Kandinsky/Kandinsky6) |
| Wan-Animate-2 | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2) |
| SANA-Video 2.0 | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/SANA-Video/SANA-Video) |
| LLaDA-Image / LLaDA-Image-Turbo | Diffusion | |

## What's new

* DeepSeek-V4.1 gets up to 2.3x more throughput per GPU on H200, and now runs on AMD MI350X / MI355X with up to 1.9x throughput from DSpark ([#41251](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41251), [#41308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41308)).
* Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decodes 12% faster on B200, and GLM-5.3-Flash with DFlash 10% faster on B300 ([#42175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42175), [#42489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42489)).
* MiMo-V2.6-Pro gets 1.85x decode throughput with DFlash on B300 ([#41886](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41886)).
* Models load 10x faster with the new InstantTensor loader ([#40453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40453)).
* PD disaggregation gets up to 27% more throughput and half the p95 TTFT on long-prompt workloads ([#40703](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40703)).
* HiSparse now supports EAGLE and MTP for long-context serving with the KV cache in CPU memory ([#37771](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37771)).
* GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 can now combine decode context parallelism with MTP, with up to 2.1x faster decoding on GLM-5.3 ([#43735](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43735)).
* SGLang now runs on Apple Silicon Macs with the standard PyTorch backend, alongside MLX ([#36780](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36780)).
* MiniMax-H3 and Qwen-Image 2.1 now run in ComfyUI with SGLang Diffusion, which also loads community GGUF checkpoints and LoRAs ([#43504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43504), [#43581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43581), [#42556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42556), [#39523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39523), [#42174](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42174)).
* Important fix: Hybrid linear models could resume from wrong mamba states when speculative decoding and structured output were used together. Thanks to [@Wirick](https://github.com/Wirick) and Baseten for finding it ([#43029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43029)).

## To upgrade

SGLang now requires Python 3.11 or newer.

```bash
uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang==0.5.22
```

| Platform | Docker |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA (CUDA 13) | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22` |
| AMD MI35x | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x` |
| AMD MI30x | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi30x` |
| Intel GPU | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-xpu` |
| Intel CPU | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-xeon` |

articles.title: Anthropic Readies Model That Reads Users' Intentions Better
articles.text:
In the last month, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have released more than a dozen new models. If you thought that pace was crazy, don’t expect things to slow down anytime soon.
Anthropic is preparing to release a new model that is better in its reasoning and intuition than the Anthropic models that are currently available commercially, according to a person who has used it. The unreleased model is especially good at discerning a person’s underlying intentions and goals even if they don’t give the model much information, such as explicitly stating those goals, the person said.
For instance, a person might ask the model to fix a single bug, and the model might go off and instead identify the underlying class of problems that caused the bug and ask whether it should fix the whole class of problems, said the person who has used it.
The Anthropic model is also better at thinking outside of the box rather than regurgitating common sense advice or solutions, the person said. For instance, if a user asks for advice on how to invest in stocks, rather than providing generic advice like looking at price-to-earnings ratios, the model might come up with its own creative algorithms to predict future stock performance, the person said.

articles.title: 8488元起！微软新Surface开启预售：换芯骁龙X2 Plus+16GB起步
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，微软13英寸Surface Laptop与12英寸Surface Pro近日在电商平台及官方商城开启预售，两款新品均换装高通骁龙X2 Plus平台，预售定金100元。
核心配置上，骁龙X2 Plus采用第三代Qualcomm Oryon CPU与台积电3nm工艺，集成Hexagon NPU，AI算力达80 TOPS，显卡部分为高通Adreno。
两款Surface均延续无风扇设计，微软公布的数据显示，电池续航提升18%，图形速度提升超过60%，设备内AI性能提升95%。
屏幕与机身是两款机型差异最大的地方。12英寸Surface Pro采用2196×1464分辨率触摸屏，最高90Hz刷新率，机身厚7.8毫米，重686克，后置1000万像素摄像头。
13英寸Surface Laptop则为1920×1280分辨率、60Hz刷新率，重1225克，屏幕面积更大但便携性稍弱。
值得注意的是，产品页与规格表在处理器标注上存在并列口径。13英寸Surface Laptop规格表写的是骁龙X Plus（6核心），而12英寸Surface Pro才标注骁龙X2 Plus（6核心），官方未给出统一说明，下单前建议对照具体型号页面确认。
价格按尺寸和渠道形成多档结构。在京东等电商渠道，12英寸Surface Pro仅有16GB+512GB一个配置，售价8488元；13英寸Surface Laptop提供16GB+256GB（9788元）和16GB+512GB（10588元）两个配置。
需要注意的是，24GB+512GB的大内存版本仅在微软官方商城自营销售，不参与第三方电商渠道。其中12英寸Surface Pro售价11588元，13英寸Surface Laptop售价12188元，与电商渠道同容量版本存在1300元至1600元的价差。

articles.title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22894v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.

articles.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
articles.text:
Since its earliest days, the video game industry has been built on developers creating clones of competing games, with varying levels of originality and varying levels of enforcement from game platforms. Now, though, AI coding tools are making that cloning process so efficient that many developers are getting extremely cautious about sharing their early work too widely.
Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflux, which had been set to go live with today's launch of Steam Next Fest.
In a post on social media Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, "we're concerned that the demo's content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game's presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch."

articles.title: You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project
articles.text:
Panchovix on GitHub recently released a VBIOS configurator for RTX 30-to 50-series cards that doesn’t require flashing. The loader provides a UI for easy configuration and lowers the risk of bricking your GPU by avoiding a risky flash process, and it's available for Linux, too.
Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs
(Image credit: Noctua)
Desktop GPU Roadmap
Nvidia's Enterprise GPU Roadmap
Testing DirectStorage with GPU decompression
The GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?
Rubin in-depth
The Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PC
Software like MSI Afterburner or ASUS GPU Tweak is often the go-to tool for quickly changing your graphics card’s settings; however, those tools have hard limits to how much you can push the graphics card. If you want to tweak your GPU beyond the firmware’s set limits, you can change it by tweaking the parameters in the VBIOS. Configuring VBIOS is similar to changing BIOS settings in the BOOT menu. With the VBIOS loader, you can change settings beyond the firmware’s hard limits.
The way it works is by storing the modified VBIOS image in the GPU’s register key; as the Nvidia driver looks for a VBIOS override on startup, it finds the VBIOS image and restarts, applying the override settings. The flash chip on the graphics card is not overwritten, reducing the risk of bricking your GPU. However, this does not protect the card from any extreme settings that could destroy electrical components; it merely provides a safer and more convenient way to adjust and apply VBIOS settings, including a way to roll back to the default VBIOS settings should you face any instability.
Bricking a flash chip isn’t as catastrophic as it seems, however. As long as you have a backed-up version of the VBIOS, you can easily buy an SPI flash chip programmer or even build your own using a cheap Raspberry Pi Pico and its many clones; sometimes programming the flash chip may not even require desoldering. Programming a flash chip is very tedious and inconvenient, though, which is why avoiding the risk of a botched flash process altogether is so appealing.
Unless you’re familiar with power delivery, voltage tables, and the patience required to test for hours, we wouldn’t recommend jumping into this unless you’re prepared to risk your GPU. However, you can still safely take advantage of this software by tweaking the fan curves and other settings you’ve applied and tested in software like MSI Afterburner if, for some reason, the startup settings don’t stick. This software will give your GPU new default settings that override at every startup, so long as Nvidia doesn’t remove the registry key that allows the VBIOS override.

articles.title: AI 引爆 BAT「薪酬倒挂」潮，老员工：人麻了
articles.text:
大厂正在收紧招聘，但对 AI 人才的争夺并没有停止。
“所有大厂目前都处于 HC（招聘名额）收缩状态，人才招聘是优中选优”。
猎头 Mia 对雷峰网表示，另一个现实局面是：各家依然缺人、抢人，遇到真正想要的人，通常不会卡预算。
“有牛的竞品（比如 OpenAI）的人来，立马腾坑。”
这种抢人逻辑，引发公司的另一种内部矛盾。
一位互联网从业者表示，“现在内部做基础模型的员工即便职级不高，薪酬已经吊打职级更高的同事。”他还提到，公司近期传出可能取消职级的消息。
尽管这一说法尚未得到证实，但当薪资与职级差距越大，薪酬体系的尴尬也由此显现。
这也让企业陷入两难之地：不开出天价，抢不来人；给出高薪，又搅乱了原有的薪酬体系。
事实上，十年之前，就已经出现薪酬倒挂的迹象。
01 老员工忆当年，辛酸泪一把
一位在大厂工作多年的工程师回忆，2017 年前后，“我离开的时候，薪资还没有校招新人拿得多。”他说。
他解释，此前一年，薪资涨幅还有 20% 多，自从核心领导有所调整后，却降到了 5%，导致内部出现严重的薪资倒挂。
当时旁边工位坐着一位晚一年入职的海归应届生，职级比他低一级，月薪却高出一万。那两年，他所在的三十多人团队，“一个月流失 10%，都是成群结队地走”。
他回忆道。据一位资深猎头透露，十年前的阿里、腾讯就已经抢人很猛了，腾讯甚至会给简历上有百度实习经历的学生直接发校招 offer。
当时百度给顶尖校招人才开出的年薪约 20 万到 25 万元，已经不算便宜；同一时期，阿里星的年薪 60 万封顶，已是当时的天花板。
猎头 Mia 告诉雷峰网，今年做基模的应届生，年包“200 万元起步”，小红书、字节 Seed 的顶档可以达到 400 万 — 500 万元，百度去年给基模人才的年包在 200 万 — 300 万元，今年“只多不少”（有关大厂 AI 人才流动的更多内幕消息可加微信 Whho123start 了解更多）
从 25 万到 200 万，“顶尖人才”四个字，十年间贵了近十倍。
这样的说法也得到了其他资深互联网从业者的肯定，那时百度作为互联网大厂的“老前辈”，用人思路是只招最牛的学生，也舍得给钱，而且因为地处北京，招聘可以比硅谷成本低三分之一。之后受到 2008 年金融危机影响，一大批顶尖人才转而留在国内，百度也因此招到了一批优秀的学生，比如戴文渊、张博等。
高薪抢人的另一面，也引发了新老员工的不满情绪。
雷峰网此前了解到，一位华为“天才少年”计划的入选者回忆，当时天才少年的薪酬在内网公开之后，不少老员工觉得自己的学术成果和贡献未必更小，“凭什么工资就比他们少”，甚至有人在工作中给这些天才少年使绊子。
当时华为还有员工在内网实名发帖，逐一质疑“天才少年”的履历，称他们都是“水货”。
不过十年之后，面对薪酬倒挂这样的问题，许多大厂老员工已经非常平和。
“旁边坐个新来的工资比我高，无所谓。”某大厂资深算法师说道。
在他看来，这本身就是正常的市场薪酬机制：老员工觉得该涨没涨、资源没给够，到了时间节点自然会走，“这也符合当前的市场行情”。
Mia 给雷峰网讲了一个好玩的事情，她曾与 Meta 推荐系统 AI 部门的一位员工交流过（该部门与 Meta MSL —— Meta 超级智能实验室属于平行组织）。
该部门薪资偏低，尽管同样做生成式 AI 后训练，薪资却偏低，工作五六年职级薪酬几乎没变，且对方属于早期参与 Meta 基础模型研发的资深成员。
与心态同步发生变化的，还有普通 AI 人才的市场行情。
02 大厂舍得撒钱，但也得看对方办多大事
多位猎头告诉雷峰网，互联网大厂挖人的标准也出奇一致：其一在大厂头部公司上手做过；其二有知名创业公司经验。
他们的解释是：训一两百亿参数的模型，和训千亿、几万亿参数的模型“完全不是一个量级”——后者极其烧钱，必须有经验的人才能少踩坑。如果只是小公司的履历，在这套标准里几乎不算数。
他们的解释是：训一两百亿参数的模型，和训千亿、几万亿参数的模型“完全不是一个量级”——后者极其烧钱，必须有经验的人才能少踩坑。如果只是小公司的履历，在这套标准里几乎不算数。
这就导致普通 AI 求职者的处境并不像看上去那么乐观。首先是人才太多。
不止一次有猎头表示，现在基本各大厂的 HC 基本冻结，除了 DeepSeek 和千问相对招人多一点。
但冻结并不均匀。有负责基模的猎头透露，目前各家的基模团队，只要是好的人才，照单全收；真正收缩的是应用侧，岗位确实在减少。
Mia 分析了供需关系的逻辑：人才像商品一样受市场供需影响。
前两年 AI 人才供不应求，候选人掌握议价权，通过校招开高薪和各家互相抬价，造成了今天薪资倒挂的局面。但今年市场供给已经足够（大厂也有裁员人员流出），供需趋于平衡，溢价空间在缩小，薪资终将回归理性。
当然，薪资也不会立刻降下来。
毕竟，前几年入职的校招生拿到的高薪，如果现在突然压低新人的报价，内部又可能出现新的不满，薪酬调整只能是一个动态过程。
其次是，人才的割裂程度会不断加深。
“优秀的人永远不愁工作，中间层的人会非常难找工作。”另外一位互联网大厂的高级招聘章玉表示，接下来的人才市场还会进一步分层：真正稀缺的人依然有议价空间，能力和经验没那么突出的候选人，就会面临更激烈的竞争。
他举例说，像姚顺雨、田永龙这样的顶尖人才，企业往往愿意投入很高的成本争取，但对于其他人才，关注度就没这么强。
对大厂来说，他们更想要的是已经在头部团队里做过大模型、知道怎么把模型真正训出来的人。
最后，AI 市场变化太快。
这就导致人才行情的更替，也像模型更新一样快，抢手和失宠就在朝夕之间。
“目前仍处于风口上的是 Agent，尤其是面向协作场景的 Co-worker Agent。”一个月前，猎头 Mia 对雷峰网表示。
Coding Agent 则是持续存在的人才缺口，“国内各家都在挖”，与此同时，Evals（模型评测）和预训练数据（Pre-training Data）相关人才也开始受到重视。
赛道之间的冷热分化，同样明显。
比如 AI 搜索（AI Search）的热度大不如前一年，还有推理（reasoning），随着 OpenAI o1 和 DeepSeek-R1 相继出现，技术趋于成熟，留给人才的发挥空间在收窄。
以及猎头们都提到的一个尴尬赛道：AI for Math。这一赛道的处境比较特殊，各家模型的能力差距尚不足以支撑国内公司大规模、独立地投入资源，除非手握充足的算力、资金和研究资源，否则很难长期押注。
大厂撒钱，撒的是“确定性”，但一群年轻公司，正在用另一套招人逻辑，瓦解旧的职级体系。
03 年轻公司的抢人逻辑
今年首轮外部融资已完成的 DeepSeek，正在密集扩招。
据雷峰网了解，DeepSeek 近期扩招明显偏工程侧：一类是服务端/后端开发，一类是做 Agent 运行底座的 Agent 弹性计算/Agent Infra；在 Agent 产品化上，他们把模型以外的编排与运行时称为 Agent Harness，对标 Claude Code/Codex 一类代码智能体。
也就是说，做 Agent 不能只有算法，必须有人做开发，infra 同样重要。
而在扩张之前，DeepSeek 的招人画像极为鲜明：最早偏好北大系学生，典型特征是极客精神、高度技术化、超级相信 AGI、硅谷派研究员风格。
简单来说，“年纪小，没有受过大厂的‘污染’”，章玉总结道。
相比之下，Kimi 则是另一种答卷。团队大约 400 余人，人才密度保持得不错，决策链路极短，有业内人士告知，就连招一个实习生都要考虑很久。
另一家模型厂商智谱则走向了另一极端。“他们大量使用实习生，实习生比正式员工还多。
一个团队 10 个正式员工配 20 个实习生。不过这在模型厂商来看很正常。”章玉对雷峰网解释道。（有关大厂 AI 人才流动的更多内幕消息可加微信 Whho123start 了解更多）
这些年轻企业对人才的吸引力是显而易见的。雷峰网从多处了解到，年轻人之所以愿意去这些公司，是因为大厂分工太细、发挥空间有限，一些追求技术探索和更大自主权的人，反而会倾向于后者。尤其对今天的 AI 人才来说，钱也不是唯一的答案。
负责互联网大厂高级招聘的章玉对雷峰网解释，AI 圈子习惯把这些 30 岁以下，又有模型成功经验的人才称之为“小天才”，除了薪资之外，他们还会看公司是否有足够的算力和资源、能否支持自己真正训出模型，以及公司是否有成功训出模型的经验。
总结起来就是“画饼没用”。
具体怎么抢人，校招和社招是两套话术：校招生更在意薪酬和职级是否匹配，社招则更看重 scope——职责范围、具体做什么事。
而对于真正想要的人，话术和规则都不存在了。
Mia透露，目前各家大模型公司针对优秀的 AI 人才，薪酬和 scope 全部 case by case，非常灵活。
有趣的是，这场抢人已经不完全发生在国内。一位互联网猎头观察到，海外公司反向挖角中国大模型人才的现象，在 2025 年尤为明显。过去更多是国内公司去美国抢人，如今中国模型能力被海外看到，这条人才通道的方向开始倒转。
03 结尾
薪酬倒挂的现象并非中国独有。
PwC 连续两年的《全球AI就业晴雨表》显示，AI 技能在全球劳动力市场的薪资溢价已从 25%一路涨到 62%，六大洲的招聘市场都在给同一种稀缺性重新定价。
至于最极端的案例，还是 Meta：开出四年约 2.5 亿美元的薪酬方案，只为抢到一位 24 岁的研究员。一边是新人身价不断抬高，一边是老员工涨薪乏力。
但类似的剧本并不新鲜。每一轮技术浪潮里，企业都会为抢人打破薪酬秩序，新人贵过老人；再往后，行业供需重新平衡，溢价也随之退潮。看起来，这场人才战还远未到终局。而所有天价 offer 最终会证明同一件事：给得再多，不如招对一个。

articles.title: 36氪首发丨覆盖半导体产业链多环节，这家国产碳化硅材料企业完成超亿元C轮融资
articles.text:
作者 | 乔钰杰
编辑 | 袁斯来
本文约1500字，建议阅读4分钟
硬氪获悉，浙江六方半导体有限公司（以下简称“六方半导体”）近日完成超亿元C1轮股权融资，本轮由北京仓廪资本与诸暨产业投资集团有限公司联合出资。
六方半导体成立于2018年，专注于半导体新材料的研发与生产，业务覆盖半导体长晶、外延、刻蚀等关键工艺环节，为下游客户提供核心材料及精密零部件解决方案。
公司掌握CVD‑SiC碳化硅材料合成核心技术，依托该技术推出导流桶、单晶硅外延托盘、LED芯片外延托盘、SiC聚焦环等产品，覆盖半导体产业链多个环节。
在碳化硅长晶原料制备方面，六方半导体采用气相法制备高纯碳化硅粉料，具备高纯度、高密度、低氮含量等特性。目前公司产品性能可对标海外同类产品，已逐步导入国内主流长晶厂商。同时，基于CVD-SiC核心技术，公司不断拓展高纯SiC材料的应用领域，包括高纯SiC原料及薄膜在光学，芯片散热，异构集成等领域的应用。
六方半导体成立之初聚焦碳化硅涂层芯片外延托盘的国产替代。经过持续研发，公司掌握了CVD-SiC涂层的量产设备及工艺的核心技术，实现了碳化硅涂层芯片外延托盘的国产替代。
在此基础上，公司进一步突破整体SiC生长制备及加工技术。整体SiC材料是半导体领域众多核心零部件基础材料，包括刻蚀工艺所需要聚焦环，RTP设备所需的边缘环等。
（图源/企业）
随着3D NAND向300层以上推进，刻蚀工艺所需步骤数从50步向100步以上增加。AI算力芯片扩产则进一步拉动了刻蚀设备装机数量，作为刻蚀设备的核心耗材，CVD-SiC刻蚀环的需求量随之大增。目前国内CVD-SiC聚焦环国产化率不足15%，7nm以下的先进制程所需的聚焦环国产化率不足5%。
六方半导体创始人何少龙博士牵头承担了“大尺寸超高纯碳化硅制备关键技术”国家重点研发计划，针对CVD-SiC快速沉积的科学问题以及高硬脆材料的高效加工技术难题展开科学攻关，最终实现国产替代和产业化。
公司创始人何少龙博士毕业于浙江大学物理系，曾先后在日本广岛大学、国立材料研究所开展研究，回国后任职于中科院物理所、宁波材料所，从事凝聚态物理研究，已在《Nature Materials》《Nature Communications》《Phys. Rev. Lett.》《PNAS》等国际期刊发表30余篇学术论文，多次受邀在美国March Meeting、日本半导体年会、香山会议等国内外顶级学术会议做特邀报告；现任国家重点研发计划首席科学家、浙江省级领军人才。
公司本轮融资资金将重点用于前沿新品研发及产能扩建，占地100亩的新厂房预计2026年12月正式投产。
（图源/企业）
以下为创始人问答：
硬氪：接下来公司的前沿产品研发主要会投向哪些方向？
何少龙：目前我们已经在拓展的方向，包括碳化硅材料在光学及芯片散热领域的应用。
碳化硅具有较高的折射率，在AR眼镜以及Meta lens等领域均有很高的应用价值。我们希望拓展碳化硅薄膜沉积技术，进一步延伸到光学领域的应用。
另一方面，碳化硅的热导率理论值最高可以到500W/(m·K)，是非常理想的散热材料，我们将拓展SiC材料在芯片散热领域的应用。
投资方观点
仓廪资本：半导体核心材料与关键工艺零部件是国内半导体产业链实现自主可控的核心基石，也是硬科技领域长期具备高成长价值的黄金赛道。六方半导体团队多年来在材料领域的深度技术积累和扎实的产业化落地能力，具备突出的行业稀缺性。未来投资方将充分调动自身的产业资源网络，在客户对接、技术协同等方面为企业提供全方位赋能，助力企业快速成长为赛道内的核心领军企业。
诸暨产投：本次投资是地方国有产业投资平台围绕半导体先进材料赛道的关键战略布局。后续将充分依托诸暨本地的产业配套优势与政策支持体系，为六方半导体新厂区落地建设、区域产业链生态对接提供全流程保障，推动企业在诸暨扎根发展，共同带动区域半导体新材料产业集群的成型与壮大。

articles.title: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22688v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e.g., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution. When several candidates could satisfy the same need, execution may be required to identify the relevant one. Investigating candidates in a shared trajectory can leave alternatives unexplored or allow failed attempts to influence subsequent reasoning. To address this, we present BRIA (BRanch-Inspect-Adopt), a simple yet effective agent that temporarily isolates candidate investigations in separate branches. Each branch retrieves and executes tools to investigate its candidate; a task agent inspects the resulting execution evidence and adopts only useful results into its continuing trajectory. BRIA retrieves additional tools as new capability needs arise during task execution. We evaluate BRIA on PlanBench-XL and MCP-Atlas using a shared pool of 1897 tools, three language models, and static and adaptive retrieval baselines. Across all settings, BRIA matches or exceeds the strongest retrieval baseline. On MCP-Atlas, it achieves an average claim score of 89.77, compared with 75.40 for MCP-Zero, a gain of 14.37 percentage points. BRIA also lies on the Pareto frontier for task performance and input-token cost.

articles.title: Watermarkability: Measuring and Improving Language-Model Compatibility with Logit-Based Watermarks
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22810v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Language-model watermarks can help identify model-generated text, encode provenance information, and detect post-generation edits. A broad class of logit-based watermarks increases the logits of a designated token set at each decoding step. Because a base model's native probability mass on this set varies across contexts, models, and watermark rules, the same logit bias can yield different adherence rates and increases in perplexity (PPL). We introduce watermarkability to characterize the compatibility between a model and the token sets requested by a watermark. At a target mass $\tau$, we quantify this property through a watermarkability cost: the expected minimum KL divergence from the base-model distribution required to assign probability at least $\tau$ to the requested set. A lower cost means that the model is more watermarkable for that request distribution. To reduce this cost, we propose a two-stage method. In the first stage, we train a target-set-conditioned low-rank adapter on unions drawn from a 16-way vocabulary partition to increase the requested set's probability mass. In the second stage, a closed-form controller applies the smallest remaining uniform logit bias needed to reach the target mass. We evaluate the method on six watermark schedules using OPT-125M and Qwen3-8B. Across the 12 model-schedule pairs, the pre-adaptation watermarkability cost correlates with the log-PPL increase under a near-hard fixed-bias baseline (pooled Pearson $r=0.929$). For every schedule, at least 99.80% of sampled tokens fall in the target set requested at their decoding step. At this reliability, the adapter and controller reduce average per-schedule prompt-conditional PPL by 46.3% on OPT-125M and 5.2% on Qwen3-8B relative to the fixed-bias baseline.

articles.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. In Qwen3-30B-A3B this loss is made at the two chat-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek-V2-Lite at the first 8-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage. Reduction changes the first token's attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full. On real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts, placing them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while placing them at random in the documents is about 3 points worse (two of five prespecified primary comparisons; the others were undecided or not run). Because the answer boundary always ends a single-turn prompt, and DeepSeek's loss was no longer detectable once its instruction moved away from the start, the sensitive tokens lay at the prompt ends in every sensitive layout we found, so rules that keep the ends are not distinguished from rules that read application marks. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts and not at 2K tokens.

articles.title: 性价比斩杀DS V4.1 Flash 国模MiniMax M3.1 Flash发布
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，一如下午预告的那样，稀宇科技刚刚发布了MiniMax M3.1 Flash大模型，在性价比斩杀线中把才夺冠没多久的DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017给超了。
据官方所说，此前以匿名身份处理了超过 200T Token 的 Space Bunny，正是 MiniMax M3.1 Flash的早期版本，今晚是正式发布。
官方表示，作为新一代Flash 模型，M3.1 Flash在Agentic任务、编程、Computer Use及网络安全能力等方面实现了代际的提升，同时线上推理速度提升了近3倍，使用成本降低了70%。
M3.1 Flash在多项基准测试中取得了全面进步，在复杂Agent任务 (Cowork)、Computer Use、软件开发 (Coding) 及网络安全方面，达到了领先模型水平。
价格方面，Agentic类任务中，模型的综合使用成本较前代模型降低了70%。输入价格为每百万Token 1元，输出价格为每百万Token 4元，缓存读取价格为每百万Token 0.1 元——这个定价跟V4.1 Flash的闲时价格是一样的，但缓存0.1元的价格比后者的0.02元高不少，所以实际费用还得看Token效率。
在官方公布的对比测试中，加入了与V4.1 Flash-1017版的评测，但不是所有项目都有对比，M3.1 Flash也不是每个项目都赢了，总体上跟V4.1 Flash互有胜负，水平相当。
但在每任务的对比中，M3.1 Flash的帕累托曲线是赢了V4.1 Flash的，性价比更高。
编程为主的DeepSWE评测中，M3.1 Flash比V4.1 Flash略逊一筹，写代码应该还是后者更强。
目前M3.1 Flash 现已正式上线MiniMaxAPI、MPlan以及 MiniMax Code中，并将于稍后开放权重。
不过也有网友反馈称MiniMax方面又改了旧套餐的规则，建议购买之前再看看其他人的反馈再做决定。

articles.title: 逆势大增！华为手机重夺中国第一
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，根据Counterpoint Research市场监测服务初步数据，2026年第三季度中国智能手机出货量同比下降10%，创下自2012年以来第三季度的最低水平。
但华为和苹果两家反而实现逆势上涨，合计占据40%的市场份额，进一步拉开了与竞争对手的差距。
市场整体下滑，一部分原因是存储元器件涨价，手机制造成本抬升，不少新机售价跟着往上走。现在手机硬件升级感知不强，很多用户觉得没必要频繁换机，换机周期被拉长，大家更愿意等到大促再考虑换新。
大盘走低的同时，市场格局发生明显变化。华为凭借折叠屏、阔直板等多款新品，覆盖高端、中端多个价位段，出货量拿到19%的同比增长，以21.3%的份额冲到国内市场第一位。
中国前六大智能手机品牌出货量占比
报告指出，然而，华为自9月1日起正式上调了产品价格，这可能会给未来的销售带来进一步压力。
苹果方面，以19.5%的市场份额位居第二，iPhone 18 Pro系列市场反响不错，上市前三周的销量较iPhone 17 Pro系列同比增长了 23.5%。
基础款iPhone 18的发布推迟，促使部分消费者转而购买Pro系列机型，从而助推了Pro系列初期的销售势头。
简单来说，现在国内手机市场两极分化越来越明显。愿意花钱买高端机的用户，更多流向华为、苹果。普通消费群体，面对涨价的新机，选择继续用旧手机，不着急更新。
机构也提到，9月份安卓旗舰集中发布，会给第四季度带来一定拉动。但存储成本居高不下，很难指望市场马上迎来大幅反弹。
后续各大厂商会更多靠AI功能、特殊屏幕形态，来刺激用户换新意愿。

articles.title: Adobe惊爆10.0满分极危漏洞！无需登录即可控制服务器：官方竟冷处理
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，Adobe旗下电子商务网站建设平台Magento和Adobe Commerce近日爆出CVSS 10.0满分漏洞，代号BlockStrap（CVE-2026-103849）。
远程攻击者无需任何身份验证，也不需要管理员介入，就能在网店服务器上执行任意代码并全面接管主机。Adobe却把这个补丁列为第2级优先，建议商户30天内完成更新，引发安全行业强烈质疑。
漏洞由安全研究员vozec发现，根源在于Magento的邮件模板引擎存在架构缺陷，官方安全公告APSB26-153发布不到24小时，Sansec研究团队就成功复现了4条不同的远程代码执行（RCE）路径。
这已经是Magento邮件模板引擎6周内第二个CVSS 10.0满分漏洞，上一个漏洞CVE-2026-756509月初遭大规模零日攻击后，Adobe才紧急发布热修复。
Sansec分析称，虽然攻击链路径相对复杂，但在现代自动化和AI辅助逆向工具普及的当下，把更新补丁反向解析成可用攻击脚本的门槛已大幅降低。
针对Adobe给出的30天宽限期评级，Sansec批评风险评估过于乐观，强烈呼吁所有电商“立刻召回团队，今天就着手修补”，防止服务器被植入后门或窃取消费者信用卡交易数据。
Sansec的技术解析还显示，本次BlockStrap本质上是对9月防护机制的绕过，Adobe之前的防御逻辑是给可信模板指令加数字签名供验证，但攻击者发现，只要把恶意指令包在子模板里，这条数据照样会被系统连带签名，随后在上一层处理时被触发执行，整套防御架构形同虚设。
Sansec特别提醒，别信Adobe所谓第2级优先和30天内修补的建议，9月的StyleSmuggler热修复和10月的BlockStrap更新彼此独立，商户必须确保两个安全更新都已部署，只打一个无法覆盖全部威胁，而且必须立刻处理，绝不能拖。

articles.title: Google named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Agentic AI Platforms
articles.text:
As organizations work to leverage AI to transform their businesses, it is clear that the raw model intelligence is not the key challenge.
Consistently, we hear that the challenges lie in how the agents can be deployed across the company while meeting key requirements for quality, integration, security, and governance.
Gemini provides that connected foundation across the enterprise, and it’s why we believe Google was named a Leader in the inaugural IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic AI Platforms 2026 Vendor Assessment1.
IDC MarketScape vendor analysis model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and suppliers in a given market. The research methodology utilizes a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria that results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier’s position within a given market. The Capabilities score measures supplier product, go-to-market and business execution in the short-term. The Strategy score measures alignment of supplier strategies with customer requirements in a 3-5 year timeframe. Supplier market share is represented by the size of the icons.
Gemini meets work where it already happens
A viable agentic platform has to meet work where it already happens – and run under production-grade controls. Gemini is engineered to deliver developer velocity without compromising governance, built around four core differentiators:
1. Surfaces that connect builders and business teams
Gemini makes it so that every surface connects back to one universal foundation.
Where teams already work: Employees collaborate with Gemini directly inside Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or team chats – the agent carries the same persistent memory, skills, and enterprise permissions across desktop and mobile without needing to switch tools.
Builder tools centered on choice: Gemini platform supports how developers want to work, spanning no-code and low-code builders in the studio to code-first workflows with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Antigravity.
Workflows that compound across the organization: When a team solves a complex workflow, they can package it into a shared skill published to a central Agent Registry. Gemini calls on these skills directly to execute tasks, turning proven procedures into reusable assets across the entire company.
2. Radical openness across models, enterprise data, and tools
Gemini adapts to the software you already run, not the other way around.
Model choice: Through Model Garden in Gemini platform, teams have direct access to over 200 models – including all of the breakthroughs from Google DeepMind like Gemini 4 Argon, day one access to the latest Anthropic models, and third-party and open models.
Grounding on your enterprise data: Gemini connects directly to live enterprise data across Google Cloud in BigQuery and Cloud Storage, as well as Salesforce, SAP, and others. Because Gemini inherits each employee's existing credentials, sensitive information stays governed at the source.
Open standards: Built on open protocols like MCP and A2A, Gemini can easily plug into your existing toolchains and communicate across multi-vendor environments.
3. Smarter token economics
Gemini optimizes cost, latency, and performance directly at the execution layer.
Matching tasks to the right model: By default, Gemini uses Auto mode for users, letting the platform match each step of a task to the right model dynamically. It defaults to a fast workhorse model like Gemini Flash, and escalates to a high-capacity frontier reasoning model only when task complexity requires it.
Reusable skills: Teams can package proven processes into shared skills. Your agents can execute against these established procedures, improving consistency and reducing repetitive token consumption across the company.
Budget guardrails: Administrators can set spending limits by project, department, or individual agent in the billing console. When a budget threshold is reached, new requests pause while active tasks are allowed to complete, giving finance and engineering predictable cost controls without abruptly interrupting in-progress work.
4. Built-in governance and security
Gemini incorporates enterprise governance natively, and at no additional cost.
Dedicated agent identity: Every agent receives its own distinct, authenticated identity governed by least-privilege permissions. When an agent takes action, every event is recorded in an audit trail tied directly to that identity and the identity of which user was using the agent for the task.
Isolated sandboxes: A sandboxed boundary keeps dynamic tasks strictly contained, protecting your underlying infrastructure, core network, and sensitive corporate data from being exposed or compromised.
Policy enforcement: Rather than relying on a model to self-police, Agent Gateway automatically applies corporate security policies, blocks data leakage, and ensures agents only access what they are explicitly authorized to touch.
Looking forward
At its core, Gemini is all about giving your organization an open, reliable platform where builders have choice and teams work with complete confidence.
We are honored by IDC MarketScape’s recognition of Google as a Leader, and we look forward to continuing this work alongside our customers.
Download the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic AI Platforms 2026 Vendor Assessment excerpt to learn why Google is named a Leader.
1. SOURCE: “Worldwide Agentic AI Platforms 2026 Vendor Assessment”, October 2026, IDC # US54140926.

articles.title: 1米7人形机器人难进家门：压迫感太强 很多人不敢用
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，奥维云网一份报告提出观点，人形机器人想要走进普通家庭，小尺寸会是核心突破口，1米7左右的大型人形机器人，对居家环境来说压迫感太强，很难落地。
先说说安全层面。家里环境不像工厂，老人、小孩、宠物来回走动，物品摆放杂乱。一台几十公斤、1米7高的机器人，站在客厅很容易让人觉得紧张。一旦摔倒或者误撞，会带来不小的安全隐患。
换成小尺寸机型就不一样，就算碰到人，基本不会造成伤害，这是机器人入户最基础的前提。
心理学上也有讲究。小机器人圆润小巧，个头只有几十厘米，会唤起人的保护欲，更容易放下心理防备。
搭配类肤外壳、恒温设计，小机器人更像陪伴伙伴，而不是冰冷的工业设备。
研发测试也更省心。小尺寸机器人整体重量更轻，摔倒产生的冲击力比大机器人低很多，更耐摔耐造。
工程师调试动作算法的时候，不用小心翼翼保护机器，可以反复测试各种动作。试错成本低，迭代速度更快，收集的数据越多，机器人的智能策略进步就越快。
目前小尺寸人形机器人已经落地不少家庭场景。最成熟的是陪伴交互，接入各大音频应用，可以对话答疑、辅导功课、练习口语。
不少产品还做成青少年编程开发平台，支持Python、C++代码编写，爱好者能自己修改外壳，动手二次开发。
简单家务也开始尝试，分拣衣物、拿取餐具这类轻量任务已经可以完成。还有产品支持形态切换，室内用轮足模式，到户外自动变成四足形态，能走台阶、砂石路，还可以抬手拍照。
当然小尺寸机器人还有不少难题。在仿真环境里任务成功率很高，放到真实家庭环境，表现会大幅下滑。
缺少海量真实居家场景数据，硬件微型化带来高昂成本，万元级产品能不能让用户买单，还需要市场验证。
行业普遍判断，一老一小会是小尺寸机器人优先发力的赛道。政策层面也在推动养老陪护、儿童教育类机器人落地。
短期来看，家用机器人不会直接包揽繁重家务，情感陪伴、教育、轻量帮手，才是现阶段更现实的方向。

articles.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
articles.text:
Today, I’m talking with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, who has a lot of thoughts about AI, tech, and privacy.
If you’ve been listening to the show, you know that one of my running theories is that those issues are driving a big and maybe kind of unexpected political realignment — and with the midterms coming up next month, and early voting already underway in a lot of places, the stakes are pretty high right now.
So I asked Gov. Pritzker about all that, and he was surprisingly willing to dive right into the absolute existential weeds of what government is even for. You’ll hear him say — and it’s hard to disagree — that some problems are just collective action problems that require the government to do a lot of work. We can’t solve all these problems one at a time, or even one state at a time. It’s a pretty deep conversation, and we really got into it on a lot of issues.
And of course, I had to ask him: Are the Bears gonna stay in Illinois?
Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday.
Okay: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. Here we go.
Gov. JB Pritzker, you’re the governor of Illinois. Welcome to Decoder.
Thanks, Nilay. Great to be with you.
I am very excited to talk to you. We’re in the heart of midterm season. You are running for reelection. I have to tell you. I have to be very honest with you. I personally feel a lot of pressure in this interview, not only because I’m speaking to a governor, but because I went to school in Chicago. My sister still lives in Chicago. My wife grew up in Illinois. Her entire family is farmers in North Central Illinois. Boy, do I have a list of questions for you. I have to do a good job here.
Well, we’re claiming you. Now that I know all that, we’re claiming you. You’re an Illinoisan.
Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here.
I don’t know about that. I grew up in Wisconsin. Here’s my first question for you. I’m a die-hard Packers fan. Are you going to let the Bears move to Indiana?
That is not our intention. We are, in fact, in discussions with the Bears and the NFL about keeping the Bears either in Chicago or in Arlington Heights, but in Illinois.
I’m saying, as a Packers fan, nothing is funnier than the outcome of the Bears moving to Indiana. I just want to put that out there. Openly biased in this case — I own two shares of that stock — but I’m going to make the comparison here. And the reason I started there is not only because I think that’s a funny outcome, although I do, but it feels like we are in the middle of a generational political realignment.
I’m sure you feel that, in this election campaign, the idea of big business and how that should interact with the government, and how the government should be able to push back on big business and not give in to big business. All of that feels up for grabs.
And the comparison I will make in this specific case is your fellow governor, Gavin Newsom, in California. They sued the Ellison family, Paramount, over the Warner Brothers merger. Paramount threatened to leave. They made a lot of noise about Nashville, Texas, Miami, or wherever you make noise about these days, and it feels like Newsom caved. It feels like he pressured his Attorney General, Rob Bonta, to settle that lawsuit and keep them there.
They settled the lawsuit. The next day, the Ellison family is like, “We never… We’re from California. We would never leave.” I see a parallel here with the Bears that is connected to that larger realignment, how government and business should interact. Do you see that parallel? Do you feel that realignment?
Well, what I can tell you is we’re pretty tough negotiators in Chicago and Illinois, and that’s really what we’re in the midst of now with the Bears. But I understand your point about realignment. I mean, there is a generational change, and I think it’s also an attitudinal change about protecting taxpayers, protecting people who frankly are among the most vulnerable to all the technology that’s overtaking people’s lives and invading people’s homes.
And so I do believe that the government has to be more active now and become a fighter for our people and not just a collaborator with business on everything. I’m a businessman, as you know, before I became governor. But I also know that, for the people of Illinois anyway, my job is to protect the working people of this state who often don’t have anybody protecting them except a government that will stand up for them. So that’s kind of the realignment that I see.
And that generational shift, I agree with you. It’s partly a Democratic Party generational shift. Generationally, we’re a little more aggressive. And I’m probably older than the next generation that’s already possibly taking office this November. I’m 61 years old, but I think of myself as having come out of the tech world and as somebody who has been a fighter for progressive values that, yeah, we’ve got to become more aggressive and make sure we’re standing up for our people.
There are two places where I see the realignment in particular. One is data centers, one is privacy, and you just see that as a bipartisan backlash to those things. I would actually add a third, which is antitrust broadly. It’s weird if you go into Silicon Valley. David Sacks is retweeting Lina Khan from the Biden administration talking about whether the AI industry needs an antitrust exemption to manage safety.
They both agree that these companies don’t need antitrust exemptions. They actually should be more competitive. Again, putting that in the context of regulating these companies, thinking about the dynamic between the government and the biggest companies in the world. I’ll just ask the question, I guess, more directly. Do you think Newsom was right to give in to Paramount, or do you think he should have forced them to make good on that threat to leave?
I can’t speak to the Paramount situation well enough to give you an answer, so it would be unfair for me to do so. I can say once again that our orientation today — and I think about the big AI companies and the big social media companies as well — has to be like, wait a minute, too much power in too few hands.
Particularly when we talk about AI, where it’s potentially existential, but certainly transformative, which is probably a kind way to say it about the economy, that we’re going to have to get very engaged. Guardrails, of course, on both parts, but also addressing what I think on the AI front is potentially a significant change in employment in the United States. I’m not somebody who is necessarily convinced that we have to see a whole bunch of job loss, but that does feel like that’s the direction this is going.
What I’m suggesting is we better be prepared, and we better be protecting people who are going to lose their jobs, or at least it appears they’re going to lose their jobs. And I’ll just give you this thought. If these days 4 percent unemployment is kind of the acceptable near full employment number, I think the problem we’re going to see is — if that’s sort of the level that we’re going to hopefully aim for and stay at — that in very short order, we could end up at 7 percent and have that be the baseline, or maybe 10 percent.
And if you think about what’s happened, the upheavals of economies and of governments when you get to 10 percent unemployment in any country. We better be focused on how we’re going to give people the dignity of work and enough income so that they can make a life for themselves when you’re going to put people out of work by virtue of this technology. By the way, much of the benefit of that is going to go to a very, very few people. So we’ve got to wrestle with that and come to a conclusion.
I wanted to start with some of the brinksmanship we have seen in the negotiations between, particularly, states and the big companies, because that brinksmanship is real. The threat is we will leave. We just covered, I don’t know, Kevin O’Leary in Utah talking about data centers, and the people of Utah really pushed back against Kevin O’Leary building that data center. But his argument was, “Well, I’m just going to shop around.”
This is what states do. They compete with tax incentives and benefits, maybe for data centers, which will put everyone out of a job. They compete for land use rights. You’ve got a rural state with a lot of farms in it. How are you thinking about that dynamic? Do you feel like you’re in competition with the other states, or is this bipartisan realignment creating more of a level playing field where these companies are going to have to actually give something?
We are in competition. We just are because it isn’t bipartisan, at least if you ask me. Unless there is a change in the government. I’ll pick on Texas for a second, and there is a chance that you’ll see a new governor in Texas as of November 3rd. In fact, a good chance. But if you look at Texas as it’s run today by a three-term, hoping to be a four-term, Republican governor and a Republican legislature, they have no intention of changing their alignment about incentives.
In the state of Illinois, we don’t want to have to do that. I mean, we obviously want to protect the revenue that we’ve got for the state to pay for the things we think are valuable to our people, but we also want to make sure that we’re attracting jobs and not losing jobs. And in a world where South Carolina, Michigan, Texas, Florida — pick your poison. Michigan may be slightly different just because it’s got democratic control, but these are our competitors. When I’m competing to have a company move to Illinois, I’ve got to make sure, first of all, that I’m somewhere in the ballpark when it comes to the incentives, because otherwise we don’t even get considered.
And then when I say somewhere in the ballpark, I mean, I want to give away less than more, and then I want to provide whatever other advantages I can that aren’t financial so that I can protect the resources that we have. An example of that is, we like to talk about a kind of white-glove service that we offer to companies. If you’re going to bring a factory here, let’s say, just to give an example, we want to make sure that we’ve got somebody who’s kind of a concierge for your company that’s walking you through each of our departments where you need a permit. It doesn’t mean we’re lowering the standards. It just means, a lot of times, the bureaucracy eats up so much time that it makes it impossible for a company to actually do what they want to do in your state.
We try to make sure that if we’re going to attract a large company, with 1,000, 2,000, 3,000 jobs, that we’re at least making it a little easier for them to go through without having to give them massive tax incentives. So that’s the way I think about it. We are in competition. There’s just no doubt about it. Should we be? There’s a lot of discussion about whether we shouldn’t, and maybe at the federal level we should do something about leveling the playing field, but this is the world we’re living in right now.
I wanted to ask those questions just to set the baseline. I really do think something is happening. A lot of young people are dissatisfied with the status quo. A lot of people in general are dissatisfied with what big tech companies are trying to do with AI, with the potential for job loss.
And the relationship between the people, the government, and those companies seems more fraught than ever, especially as they’re trying to expand their physical infrastructure with data centers, as they all become defense contractors, literally taking our tax dollars to sell weapon systems and collect data for the government. That’s a big swirl.
I wanted to start there, but I just want to take one second here and ask you the Decoder questions because I personally think the operation of government is so opaque. It’s very easy to figure out how big companies are run. The CEOs won’t shut up. They’re on podcasts all day long. I think most people have no idea how your job works.
So you were elected governor. How is your office set up, and how have you structured the state government of Illinois?
Just starting from where I sit, and then, of course, we look at it from a customer service perspective. But starting just at the top, I actually did something that no governor of Illinois has ever done — which is that I created not just one deputy governor. We obviously have a lieutenant governor who’s elected also, but a deputy governor is somebody getting appointed by me to serve under me, to help manage the government with me. What I did was put four deputy governors in place, a general counsel, and my chief of staff.
Why is that important? Because what I’ve tried to do is to break down the silos of government. I took all of the health and human services-related departments — that’s the Department of Public Health, the Department of Human Services, the Department of Healthcare and Family Services, everything from health insurance, Medicaid, and public health during the pandemic — and put it all under one deputy governor working directly for me. The idea is that instead of my having, let’s say, 26 direct reports, I’ve got four or five direct reports plus my chief of staff, who each have, let’s say, six or seven departments underneath them.
From my perspective, what I wanted to do was make sure that I’m breaking down the silos of government, making these departments that are often building walls, and they don’t want to talk to one another because they’re afraid they might lose jobs in one department to another department, or lose control of a program if they’re talking to one another. That’s the way it used to be. Now we’re like the deputy governor is there to either beat the heads together or at least bring them together so that they will be operating the government more efficiently. Okay, so that’s from the top.
From the bottom, which is: how do people who live in Illinois interact with the state government? And obviously, technology is one of the upgrades that’s occurred and made it easier. Illinois, frankly, had not significantly invested in those processes before I became governor, or in the technology that was necessary. And I’ll just give you one example of this: We created something called BEACON, which is designed to address the problem that parents and families have with mental health for children. It turns out that there were seven different ways in which people approached the government to get help, and we weren’t coordinating those, and we weren’t helping to provide all of the resources.
I’m talking about outside resources. How do you find a therapist? How do you find a psychiatrist? And how do you pay for those things? Medicaid, if you can’t afford it on your own. But the point is, there’s one door to enter through BEACON that allows you to get access to all of those resources, even if they’re in multiple departments. So that’s just one example. We’re trying to think of this as a customer service operation. It’s one thing to say this is how the org chart looks and another thing to say, this is how you access all the resources of the government that you need.
We provide programs that really matter to people. We have a birth equity initiative to reduce maternal mortality, particularly in Black and Brown communities. And free diapers for some people. The problem is, people don’t even know that the programs exist, and how would you ever figure out that the programs exist, especially if you’re a working person who’s working two minimum-wage jobs? You don’t have any time, and you don’t have any money, and you don’t even know how to talk to the government. And so we’re trying to fix all of those problems of the government with the way that we interact with people.
