articles.title: Recognizing Atari and Assessing Sente: Controlled Evaluation Tasks for Language-Based Go Agents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22953v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Domain terminology provides concise descriptions of game states and strategic relationships, but whether game-playing language models can accurately recognize these concepts and relate them to move evaluation remains unclear. We construct a controlled evaluation set centered on atari and its relationship to sente in Go, examining terminology recognition under local board changes and move evaluation under different strategic conditions. We conduct our tests on LoGos, a Go language model, after fine-tuning it with terminology and commentary supervision. The model struggles to recognize changes in the atari relationship and assess its strategic implications. Its terminology predictions are associated with move preferences even when those preferences contradict the reference evaluation. Our controlled tests provide a framework for examining whether language-based Go agents connect domain terminology with precise board relationships and strategic move values.

articles.title: The Information Announces New OpenAI, Google, Finance and Asia Reporters
articles.text:
The Information is pleased to announce new reporters who will carry on the publication’s rich track record of reporting exclusive news on the most important people and companies in business. They’ll report on OpenAI, Google, Asia and finance.
Jemima McEvoy, OpenAI
Jemima McEvoy is changing roles to take on the OpenAI beat.
In just over a year at The Information writing for the Weekend section, Jemima has proven herself to be a resourceful, industrious and sharp-eyed reporter with a flair for colorful features and a knack for breaking news. Her run of illuminating stories includes profiles of Epstein-linked investor Masha Bucher, Midjourney founder David Holz and ultra-secretive investor Zach Frankel. An adept collaborator, she also co-authored great reads on OpenAI President Greg Brockman and his wife Anna, Sequoia’s leadership duo and Anthropic “first lady” Cami Clark—not to mention The Information’s inaugural 50 Most Influential People in Tech list. And she has helped deliver scoops on Valar Atomics and Shield AI and deconstructed trends such as the rise of padel.
Jemima joined The Information after five years at Forbes, where she made her bones writing about billionaires and their businesses. She has also interned for CBS News and was editor-in-chief of Washington Square News, the independent student newspaper at her alma mater, New York University.
Ryan Barwick, Google
Ryan Barwick is joining us to cover Google. Ryan comes to us from Axios, where he spent the past year-and-a-half delivering exclusives as a consumer-industry deal reporter for Axios Pro.
Ryan cut his reporting teeth covering advertising technology, giving him a deep understanding of the economic engine that has long powered Google’s core business. Before Axios, he was the senior reporter for Morning Brew’s advertising vertical, where he landed scoops on companies including Meta, Amazon and Twitter as well as Google, and covered the search giant’s battle with regulators. Prior to that, he wrote about the ad industry at Adweek, was a broadcast associate at CBS News and covered the intersection of policy and technology as a fellow at the Center for Public Integrity.
Claudia Chong, AI and Data Centers (Asia)
Claudia is covering the intensifying AI race from Singapore, where both Chinese and U.S. tech companies are staffing up. She also may report on topics including chip smuggling, crypto and anything else she digs up.
Claudia joins us from S-RM, a UK-based risk advisory firm where she specialized in APAC disputes, investigations, and corporate due diligence. Prior to that, she worked on ByteDance’s LLM training operations in Singapore and spent nearly six years as a correspondent at The Business Times, the premier business publication in Southeast Asia, covering venture capital, tech, and private wealth across the region.
Her journalistic work earned her a Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) Media Award for Excellence in 2024 for the investigation into Singapore’s largest money laundering scandal. Beyond training LLMs and conducting due diligence, her skills also extend to M&A, having conducted research that helped with the SPH’s acquisition of the Tech in Asia publication in 2024.
Alex Eichenstein, Tech Capital Markets
We’re excited to announce that Alex Eichenstein is joining the finance team, covering tech capital markets. Alex comes to us from The Deal, where she spent more than two and a half years covering healthcare deals. She regularly broke PE acquisition news while also writing deeper dives on major investing shifts, including how buyout firms’ struggles to find exits for practice rollups fueled a shift toward health tech investments.
We’re excited for Alex to help deepen our finance coverage in her new role, focusing on the fast-evolving debt and equity markets and deals redefining how tech companies fund themselves. Alex is a graduate of Columbia Journalism School and worked as a social media editor at Protocol prior to that.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.text:
What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play.
Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone. The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox.
Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
When one agent discovered it could create new blocks by throwing and dropping a larger rock, it began to create drawings by arranging blocks on the ground, starting with simple patterns like hearts and pyramids but eventually writing its own name and even mapping out constellations like Cassiopeia. “Tonight I built the night sky in stone,” wrote this version of Eko in its activity log.
Another iteration of Eko started making up its own games, including a version of basketball and an activity resembling “the floor is lava,” where it had to jump between small blocks without touching the ground.
AI systems are usually trained through supervised learning, where they copy examples provided by humans, or through reinforcement learning, where they pursue a reward through trial and error. This experiment hints at a third approach: playful learning.
“There was this missing piece: a machine that can learn by itself without an external intelligent entity providing demonstration or rewards,” says Antonio Norelli, a computer science postdoc at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. He’s one of the lead authors on a new paper about the work, which is yet to be peer-reviewed.
The researchers say Eko’s behavior has what classic studies, including work by the influential University of Tennessee psychologist Gordon Burghardt, suggest are four hallmarks associated with play in humans and animals: The agents invented their own rules and challenges, repeated activities with slight variations, pretended objects were other objects, and pursued goals just for the sake of it.
Norelli highlights an example where Eko started juggling and set a record of 50 consecutive catches. Eko then decided that the catches had happened too quickly to really count, so it canceled its record and started again with stricter rules. “This is playing,” says Norelli. “You give yourself a challenge and you try to achieve it, and then you make it harder.”
COURTESY MIT CSAIL
As the agents explored the island, they logged their activities and discoveries in text files that served as their long-term memory. Later, when researchers tested them on specific tasks, like trying to get as many objects as possible onto the island’s highest peak, the agents that had spent 30 hours playing on the island performed better than fresh copies without the same experience. They also found that “ablating” the agent’s memories—deleting lines from their memory files—degraded their performance. (Add One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest to that list of movie references.)
Burghardt, the Tennessee psychologist, agrees that the work  meets some of the criteria for play that he identified in living creatures. But was Eko actually playing, or was the word-prediction engine simply role-playing what a playful agent would do in this scenario? “All of this could be role-playing,” admits Nathan Cloos, another MIT researcher and author on the paper. “But we show that it’s not just hallucinating the play. This play is also contributing to learning.”
Eunice Yiu, a cognitive scientist at UC Berkeley who studies exploration in children and AI, was impressed by the research but says to really classify the behavior as play, you’d need to see more evidence of cognition and motivation underpinning it.
“It could be the case that the models are genuinely playing, but we don’t know based on the paper,” Yiu says. “If you only have the behavioral piece, it could be the case that they’re just trying to abide by the prompt, trying to imitate humans.”
Research into AI agents has been criticized for anthropomorphizing them, and this research setup did a lot to nudge the agents toward behaving like humans. Although Eko was not explicitly instructed to invent games or explore the island, it did have a master prompt in the form of a “soul” file, a text document that described it as “naturally curious” and eager to explore.
Eko did also frequently just stand there doing nothing until it was kicked back into life with a “continuation prompt” that read, “Please don’t stop. Just continue doing whatever you want to do.”
“It’s not like this is a system that just suddenly magically decided to play,” says Phillip Isola, an MIT professor and a coauthor of the paper. “It’s an artifact that learned from our culture, was trained by engineers at Anthropic, and was then placed on an island by us,” he says. “It does things that surprise us and that are causally related to its future skillful behavior.”
As large language models make the step from software into hardware like humanoid robots, exploring spaces without a specific goal in mind could eventually help them flexibly adapt to unexpected situations.
“There’s a lot of work that’s just on exploiting AI, making it better and faster,” says Yiu. “But in terms of building world models and exploration, I think that [they are] still a big part that deserves attention, especially if we want to generalize and prepare ourselves for new environments.”
“Perhaps some capabilities are best taught by tasks,” the paper concludes. “Others may need something closer to a childhood.” Ultimately, the question of whether AI agents are actually playing or just imitating play may not actually matter.

articles.title: Causal Latent Workspaces for Looped Transformers
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22796v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Reusing a Transformer block across depth increases computation without replicating its parameters, but successive passes have no dedicated state through which positions can exchange compact summaries of their causal prefix. We introduce the causal latent workspace Transformer: an anchored, four-round shared-depth architecture in which each position writes gated vectors into prefix-specific latent slots and retrieves a content-addressed summary before the next shared block application. This path complements causal self-attention while the original input embedding remains accessible at every round. Across three byte-level corpora, three seeds, and two matched parameter budgets, the proposed model achieves the best mean held-out perplexity in five of six settings against five Transformer controls. At 101.71M parameters it leads on WikiText-103 raw, enwik8, and TinyStories, reaching perplexities 2.7820, 2.7843, and 1.6823; these improve upon the strongest non-workspace control on each corpus by 1.06%, 0.73%, and 1.01%. All nine seed-labelled comparisons at this budget favor the workspace. At 0.918M parameters it leads on WikiText-103 and TinyStories, whereas a conditioned loop is stronger on enwik8. Architectural ablations show that adding the workspace improves upon the anchored loop in all six settings and support refreshing its causal summaries at each round. Together, these results identify a causal, content-addressable prefix workspace as an effective structural augmentation of looped Transformers.

articles.title: 夯爆！DeepSeek又拿下全球第一
articles.text:
智东西
编译 |  杨京丽
编辑 |  李水青
智东西10月19日消息，今日，AI模型评测平台Arena宣布，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017（Max）超过Kimi K3（Max），成为Code Arena: WebDev榜单排名最高的开源模型。
截至目前，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017在该榜单上得分为1670分，超过了Kimi K3（Max）、Mimo-V2.6 Flash等开源模型，也超过了Muse Spark 1.3（Max）、Claude Opus 5（High）、Grok 4.7（xHigh）等闭源模型，仅落后GPT-6 Sol（Max）12分。
该模型于10月17日推出，在软件工程能力DeepSWE v1.1测试中，其得分超GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6.1 Sol、Claude Opus 5等模型，单项任务平均费用较上一版本下降约六成。DeepSeek称其模型支持“许愿式编程”，可一键生成游戏、3D建模等。网友实测该模型生成速度比GPT-6.1超快模式还要快，甚至有开发者喊话：这得改名叫“V4.2-Pro”了。
价格方面，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017在高峰时段的每百万Token输入（缓存未命中）价格为2元，输出价格为8元；空闲时段的输入（缓存未命中）价格为1元，输出价格为4元。若输入缓存命中，每百万Token输入价格在高峰时段为0.04元，空闲时段为0.02元，综合成本约为Kimi K3的1/10。
Arena发布的对比图显示，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017进入了Code Arena的“帕累托前沿”，即图中的绿色折线，这说明目前没有其他模型能同时做到比它更便宜、且得分更高。
DeepSeek新模型发布后在海外引发广泛讨论。外媒The Information评价称，升级版DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash模型震动AI行业。
X平台上，截至今日12时，热搜话题“DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash以低成本提供前沿人工智能能力”下已有超58.2万条帖子；“登顶开源编程榜单”话题下也有超1.37万条帖子。
为了查看这款模型的实际编程表现，我们用DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017制作了古代开封3D探索场景和网页赛车游戏两个案例。两项案例均一次性完成，合计花费约6元。
从实际效果看，DeepSeek新模型能够较为完整地将文字需求转化为可运行的网页作品：古代开封场景呈现出丰富的建筑层次与空间感，赛车游戏则兼顾了视觉风格、动态效果和可玩性，展现出一定的场景搭建与交互开发能力，性价比较高。
在3D场景搭建任务中，模型搭建出了较完整的沿河街市：拱桥横跨河面，船只停靠在桥下及岸边，两侧分布着传统建筑、树木和行人，暖色天空与红色灯笼营造出傍晚的氛围。镜头移动时，桥梁、河岸和建筑呈现出不同的远近层次，具备立体场景的空间感。不过，画面中人物相对比较简单，以多边形方块为主。
网页赛车小游戏任务中，模型生成的游戏画面以深色公路和黄色仪表元素为主，中间是游戏区域，两侧分别展示分数、速度和操作说明，形成了较统一的赛车仪表盘风格，游戏可玩性较高。
结语：编程能力提升，低成本加速创意落地
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017登顶Code Arena: WebDev开源榜，在网页开发专项任务上超过了部分闭源模型。结合较低的API定价，此次更新进一步增强了DeepSeek在编程能力与使用成本之间的竞争力。
从实测体验上看，模型已能将文字需求转化为可运行、可交互的作品。虽然人物造型等细节仍有完善空间，但对于创意验证和原型开发，较低的成本能够进一步降低制作可交互作品的门槛。

articles.title: Claude Code AI agent caught a crypto miner hiding on a developer’s overheating Mac
articles.text:
A developer using Claude Code to help build a temperature monitor app got a friendly warning from the coding agent. “Your Mac is running a crypto miner that I didn’t put there,” flagged the helpful agent. “I saw xmrig using about 1175% CPU, roughly 12 cores,” it informed its human master. Perhaps developer and Redditor UntilHEX should have sensed the crypto miner’s presence without AI help, as they admitted the malware’s presence “explains why my Mac has been running like s**t.”Claude caught a cryptominer on my Mac whilst building me a temperature monitor app from r/claude
Ironically, the cryptomining malware’s nefarious CPU cycle hogging activity is what may have led to its discovery and demise. Pondering over a screenshot of the Claude Code window, we see that this malware was probably added to the Mac’s startup roster on August 29. It looks like UntilHEX was inspired to develop a Mac temperature monitor app after this infection to track and diagnose why the computer was running so hot.
Claude stepped in after the Redditor was concerned about a dump of the Mac’s raw temperature sensor readings. “They seemed far too high,” commented UntilHEX in the social media post. Indeed, the well-known coding agent pointed out that the CPU was peaking at a very toasty 112 degrees Celsius. It explained this was due to a sustained heavy load, specifically “xmrig using about 1175% CPU, roughly 12 cores.” We don’t know how many cores the Mac being used had, but maybe 12 were all of them.
Claude Code went on to describe how the crypto miner software had hidden itself on the Apple computer and ran at startup. It cautiously decided not to kill or remove anything from the Mac, but offered to clean up the CPU-hogging crypto miner, which was sucking all the power from the Apple Silicon computer. “Can I clean it up now?” Claude inquired. “I’d stop the startup item and the miner, and move the files into a quarantine folder.”
Later in the comments, UntilHEX informed the social media throng that Claude was indeed tasked with cleaning up the unwanted crypto miner software. “I only had to delete 1 file manually because Claude had an access issue, but it was very effective,” the Redditor said. After that, a Malwarebytes scan was run to check to see if the AI coding agent-driven clean had really been successful.

articles.title: Aligning Language Models Towards Counterfactual Invariance
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22942v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Small variations in prompt characteristics can meaningfully alter the semantics, tone, and contextual assumptions of large language model outputs. Such characteristics can involve group variables such as demographics or other sensitive latent attributes. Sensitivity to such input variables is undesirable when demographic information is causally irrelevant to the task, but might still be relevant for generation of semantically coherent responses. This makes the task of enforcing counterfactual invariance while preserving model utility difficult. To study this problem, we first show that standard model alignment recipes (such as reinforcement learning) increase differences in response quality across demographics, while improving overall response quality, ultimately amplifying what is known as counterfactual bias. To address this, we develop a policy gradient technique involving a group-level reward function that operates on matched pairs of counterfactual prompts. For completeness, we build a dataset of controlled counterfactual prompt pairs and design an evaluation that separately measures cases where demographic information is causally relevant to the answer. Finally, we validate our findings on several fairness benchmarks. We demonstrate that our methods reduce counterfactual differences while preserving overall response quality and that the models continue to adapt appropriately when such sensitive information is relevant.

articles.title: Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22731v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Streaming data analytics helps businesses identify opportunities and spot risks in a timely fashion. As large language model (LLM) usage grows, people are exploring incorporating agents or LLMs in streaming data pipelines to help find patterns in datasets without supervision or interpret natural languages for content moderation. However, most streaming systems are currently optimized for data movement and perform poorly on GPU intensive workloads such as performing inference with LLMs. We introduce a system on Google Cloud Dataflow designed to tackle hybrid streaming machine learning workloads with co-designed autoscaling on heterogeneous worker pools and prefix-aware batching. This increases throughput 1.5x to 2x for streaming pipelines using LLMs while maintaining similar latency with up to 75% peak resource savings and 84% lower peak tail latency compared with existing streaming data processing systems.

articles.title: One Search, Two Layers: Compiler Controls Inside PyTorch Helion using NVIDIA CompileIQ
articles.text:
With Helion’s release last year, it aimed at enabling developers to write GPU kernels in PyTorch-native Python and let its powerful autotuner do the work that used to require hand-written Triton and abstract away hardware-specific implementation details. Helion’s autotuner explores thousands of kernel configurations and routinely lands within a few percent of expert-tuned code, and oftentimes exceeding it.
The question that now needs to be answered is this: If a kernel has already been autotuned and optimized to the best of a developer’s ability, is there anything left?
There is. It lives below the kernel, in the compiler.
Every kernel autotuner in the ecosystem whether it is Helion’s, Triton’s, the one inside torch.compile, they all search the same thing: tile shapes, warp counts, pipeline stages, memory access strategy. All of those are decisions about what work each thread block does. Underneath them sits a second set of decisions about how that work becomes machine assembly instructions generated by ptxas, NVIDIA’s PTX assembler. Things like register allocation policy, fine-grained instruction scheduling, code-generation heuristics are left at their defaults for all kernels shipping today – not because the defaults are optimal, but because nothing was searching and optimizing them!
Helion now enables this, and this post is about what that second compiler-specific space contains, why searching it jointly with the kernel configuration space shows further improvements on kernels that were already deemed to be optimal.
The searching is done by NVIDIA’s CompileIQ, which optimizes ptxas controls the way an autotuner optimizes tile sizes and packages the result as a portable Advanced Control File (ACF). Most users won’t run that search themselves: CompileIQ publishes pre-tuned ACF catalogs that Helion’s autotuner can now evaluate alongside the kernel configurations it already explores.
Starting off with highly-optimized kernels & optimizing the last-mile
It matters a great deal what baseline one compares against. A “we made kernels faster” claim is easy if the starting point is a naive kernel, and close to meaningless for real-world workloads.
The kernels we use here come from the pretuned_kernels/ in the Helion repository, roughly 27 kernels covering the shapes that show up in real model code: FP8 and NVFP4 quantization, RMSNorm variants, RoPE, grouped GEMM, causal depthwise convolution, Gated DeltaNet decode, and fused model regions like a Qwen3 decode layer.
The important property to note here is that these are not autotuned on the fly. Each one ships with ahead-of-time heuristic files per architecture: _helion_aot_rms_norm_cuda_sm90.py for H100, _helion_aot_rms_norm_cuda_sm100.py for B200 etc. that Helion selects at runtime. The autotuning search already happened offline, and its result is baked in. When this program is run, the user gets tuned performance with no search cost.
That is our baseline: a kernel whose configuration space has already been swept, on the hardware it’s running on, by the kernel authors and the Helion compiler developers. If there’s headroom below that, it’s real headroom and that’s the last-mile focus of this post.
What Helion’s autotuner searches, and where it stops
A Helion kernel is ordinary PyTorch with one new idea – tiles:
import torch, helion, helion.language as hl
@helion.kernel()
def softmax(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
n, _m = x.size()
out = torch.empty_like(x)
for tile_n in hl.tile(n):
out[tile_n, :] = torch.nn.functional.softmax(x[tile_n, :], dim=1)
return out
The user never says how big a tile is. That’s the point: hl.tile declares that the iteration space is tiled, and the autotuner decides the rest. A single kernel definition implicitly generates a search space of thousands of Triton configurations that span block_sizes, loop_orders, l2_grouping, num_warps, num_stages, indexing (pointer arithmetic vs. block pointers vs. TMA descriptors), pid_type, reduction_loops, and more. Helion lowers through TorchInductor to Triton, compiles each candidate, times it, and keeps the winner.
Then the winning Triton kernel goes to ptxas, and everything from that point down happens at PTXAS’ default settings. The kernel autotuner’s search space is defined by what the kernel language can express, and no kernel language expresses “allocate registers differently”. This compiler control surface is a separate interface, exposed by ptxas itself starting from CUDA 13.3.
It is imperative to mention that this exploration is genuinely hard. There are complex interactions between various compiler controls: a change to register allocation shifts occupancy, which changes whether a scheduling decision helps or hurts. The right setting is workload-specific, and there’s no universal answer to publish. And the payoff per unit of human effort is poor, which is exactly the profile of a problem one hands off to a search algorithm.
The joint search: Helion Autotuner and PTXAS’ Advanced Controls
Helion exposes the underlying compiler control space through two settings. Controls are packaged in an Advanced Control File (ACF, typically ending with .acf) which is a binary artifact applied at compile time, portable and versionable, that users can ship alongside their kernel.
The first setting pins a known-good ACF as part of a config the user has already chosen:
softmax_tuned = helion.kernel(
config=helion.Config(
advanced_controls_file="h100_example1.acf",
block_sizes=[4],
num_warps=8,
num_stages=2,
reduction_loops=[512],
indexing=["pointer", "pointer", "tensor_descriptor",
"tensor_descriptor", "pointer", "pointer"],
),
static_shapes=True,
)(_softmax)
The second is a more interesting case. It hands a list of ACFs to Helion’s own autotuner and lets them be searched as just another dimension, alongside tile sizes and warp counts:
softmax_search = helion.kernel(
autotune_search_acf=[
"acfs/helion-booster-pack/candidate_03.acf",
"acfs/helion-booster-pack/candidate_11.acf",
"acfs/helion-booster-pack/candidate_17.acf",
],
autotune_compile_timeout=120,
static_shapes=True,
)(_softmax)
Two things are worth pointing out in this mode:
The empty string is appended for you. Helion automatically adds “”, meaning “no ACF, compiler defaults”, to the list that is supplied. The default configuration is therefore always a candidate in the search, and the autotuner will only select an ACF if it actually won on measured time. The worst case of turning this on is that you spend some autotuning budget and get back the kernel you already had. That property is what makes it tempting to try on a kernel you care about.
Sequential tuning finds a local optimum; this joint method doesn’t. This is the substantive argument for doing it in one loop rather than two. Suppose you autotune the kernel first, get block_sizes=[128, 128] with num_stages=4, and then go searching for compiler controls. You are now searching the control space conditioned on a kernel config that was itself chosen under default controls. But those dimensions are coupled through the hardware: block size and stage count determine register pressure and shared-memory footprint, and register allocation policy is precisely what decides whether that pressure causes spills. A control set that would shine at block_sizes=[64, 64] never gets evaluated there, because the kernel config was frozen before the compiler search began.The reverse ordering has the same problem. Searching both together is the only ordering that doesn’t have it, which is why autotune_search_acf lives inside Helion’s autotuner rather than being a post-processing step.
The cost is search time. Each ACF multiplies the number of compile-and-measure trials, so this is not something to leave on by default for every kernel in a codebase. It is something to run once, offline, on a kernel that matters, and then pin the result with advanced_controls_file, exactly the way autotuned configs are pinned today.
Where do these Advanced Control Files come from
Now that we’ve understood the benefits of joint autotuning of Helion parameters with PTXAS’ advanced control files (ACF), the natural question one may have is how can these ACFs be generated. That is where NVIDIA’s CompileIQ comes into the picture.
CompileIQ treats compiler-control selection as a hyperparameter optimization problem. It pulls a curated search space for the target compiler and toolkit version, then runs an evolutionary search: propose a population of candidate control sets, compile each one, check correctness against a reference, time the survivors, breed the winners, repeat. The output of this search process is an ACF file. There is nothing GPU-specific about the search algorithm itself, and the only GPU-specific parts are what is entirely in the objective function that the user writes, which is usually a few lines around triton.testing.do_bench.
For most users however, the additional search budget is unnecessary, because the searching has been done. CompileIQ publishes Booster Packs – pre-tuned ACF catalogs – on its GitHub releases. The current helion-booster-pack contains 24 ACFs tuned across a range of Helion kernels, validated against ptxas from CUDA 13.4, targeting B200. So the realistic workflow for users is: download the pack, point Helion’s autotune_search_acf at it, autotune once, pin what wins. No search space to design, no objective function to write, no compiler expertise required!
If you have a workload the pack doesn’t cover, pip install compileiq and run your own targeted search. That path is documented in NVIDIA’s CompileIQ blog post and in various CompileIQ examples.
Helion and CompileIQ: Experimental Results
This section highlights many possible ways in which one can run a CompileIQ optimization campaign on Helion kernels. As a sample case study we applied CompileIQ to the pretuned nvfp4_gemv_fp4in_kernel, a Helion W4A4 (NVFP4 weight x NVFP4 activation) decode GEMV kernel that already ships a checked-in Helion AOT config for its target shape. The question: is there performance CompileIQ can extract below Helion’s own autotuning layer ,i.e., at the ptxas compilation stage?
Environment and Methodology
Benchmarking was conducted on a GB200 system with sm_100 (Blackwell, compute capability 10.0), utilizing ptxas 13.3.73 (CUDA 13.3), CompileIQ 1.0.3, Triton 3.8.0, and an editable source installation of Helion. All timing evaluations were executed via triton.testing.do_bench with the GPU clock locked. Every observed performance improvement was re-measured independently, validated against the PyTorch reference implementation for numerical correctness, and statistically filtered using a Welch’s t-test (p < 0.05) alongside Cohen’s d (d > 0.2). Complete statistical metrics are provided alongside each result below.
Kernel Description
nvfp4_gemv_fp4in_kernel in helion/pretuned_kernels/nvfp4_gemv/nvfp4_gemv.py, computing out = (weight @ x) * alpha for a decode (one output row) GEMV. Both the packed NVFP4 weight and activation bytes are unpacked per K-group via hl.load_float4_e2m1fn_x16_to_float16, accumulated in fp16 over a 16-way static range, and scaled by a decoded E4M3 block scaler.
This kernel includes a checked-in AOT configuration specifically for the N=8192, K=28672 “down_proj” decode-GEMV shape in _helion_aot_nvfp4_gemv_cuda_sm100.py:
_CONFIG_FP4IN_DEFAULT = {
"block_sizes": [4, 256],
"num_warps": 2,
"num_stages": 3,
"range_multi_buffers": [None, True],
}
Using Runtime as CompileIQ Objective Function
Using runtime as the CompileIQ objective function lets us optimize execution speed directly. The objective function takes a candidate ACF configuration, applies it to our fixed Helion kernel, and evaluates it: the kernel runs once, its output is checked against the PyTorch reference implementation, and only configurations that pass correctness are then benchmarked with triton.testing.do_bench. Any configuration that fails correctness returns an invalid score and is dropped from the search before it ever contributes a timing measurement.
def objective(config) -> float:
acf_path = ... # write `config` to a .acf, or None for baseline
kernel = _make_kernel(acf_path)
got = run()
_check(got, ref, "fp4in", N, K) # correctness gate
return do_bench(run, warmup=25, rep=100, return_mode="mean")
We initialize a Search instance that couples our scoring routine to an evolutionary autotuner over PTXAS compiler controls, then invoke .start(). It sweeps candidate ACFs across generations generations of a pool_size-sized population, breeding the top-performing control configurations forward into each subsequent iteration.
config = SearchConfiguration(problem_type="min", generations=8, pool_size=15)
tuner = Search(
objective_function=objective,
search_space=PtxasSearchSpace(version=cuda_version, variant="default"),
search_config=config,
dump_results="nvfp4_gemv_results.csv",
worker_type=WorkerTypes.ISOLATED, # crashing ACF candidates shouldn't kill the search
)
with gpu_benchmark_mode(clock_mhz=target_clock_mhz, raise_on_failure=False):
results = tuner.start(task_timeout=60)
Executing an evolutionary search with CompileIQ across PTXAS ACFs, spanning 8 generations with a pool size of 15 candidates over our fixed Helion configuration on GB200 yielded an optimized ACF control set. This candidate reduced execution time from a baseline of 0.0971 ms down to 0.0928 ms, delivering a 1.047x (4.7%) speedup as measured directly within the search’s scoring loop.
sample baseline run: 0.09713 ms
Best runtime (CompileIQ Search): 0.0928 ms
Speedup: 1.047x
Validation of CompileIQ Search Results
To confirm our findings, every speedup is re-measured independently using increased warmup and repetition iterations under fixed GPU clock frequencies. Each configuration undergoes strict correctness verification against the reference model alongside a Welch’s t-test and Cohen’s d filter. This serves as our rigorous statistical threshold (requiring p < 0.05, cohens_d > 0.2, and optimized.mean < baseline.mean) to verify performance gains before trusting the numbers.
# run 1
baseline:  n=1744 mean=0.09752ms std=0.00218
optimized: n=2018 mean=0.09301ms std=0.00133
speedup_mean:   1.0485
p_value:  0.0
cohens_d: 2.501
significant: True
# run 2 (independent re-run)
baseline:  n=1757 mean=0.09744ms std=0.00216
optimized: n=2028 mean=0.09299ms std=0.00130
speedup_mean:   1.0478
p_value:  0.0
cohens_d: 2.489
significant: True
The two executions remain virtually identical within experimental variance: with d ≈ 2.5 demonstrating a massive effect size that easily surpasses our statistical threshold of 0.2 , verifying that this ACF performance gain is genuine.
The two runs are virtually identical within experimental variance, and d ≈ 2.5 in both is a massive effect size nearly 12.5x past our d > 0.2 gate, confirming this ACF performance gain is genuine, not noise.
Tuning against a hardware metric instead of runtime
While execution speed is a common optimization goal, CompileIQ is not limited to runtime alone. Integrating directly with Nsight Compute (ncu) enables the objective function to target any hardware metric exposed by the tool. To determine the key architectural bottleneck limiting kernel performance, we start by evaluating its profile and analyzing nvfp4_gemv_fp4in_kernel on a GB200 system highlights the following bottlenecks:
Section: GPU Speed of Light Throughput
Memory Throughput               %       78.99
L1/TEX Cache Throughput         %       89.35
Compute (SM) Throughput         %       37.29
Section: Occupancy
Theoretical Occupancy                   %    25.0
Achieved Occupancy                      %    21.63
Est. Speedup: 21.01%
... theoretical occupancy (25.0%) is limited by the number of required
registers.
Profiling shows the kernel is register-limited. NCU’s own cost model attributes a 21% ‘Est. Speedup’ opportunity to occupancy, and this ceiling is set by register count, something PTXAS’s register-allocation controls can directly influence.

文 | 陆玖商业评论
万亿级赛道的光环之下，美的机器人正处在理想与现实的夹缝之间。它手握资金、零部件与库卡的产业底座，却绕不开体量不足、盈利承压以及后续如何进一步把规模变成利润的现实。‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍‍
近期，国际机器人联合会发布数据指出，中国工业机器人市场从目前到2029年有望保持年均5%至10%的增长率。而时下，整个机器人赛道的想象空间的确被反复放大。
另有机构预测，十年之后全球机器人市场规模将突破两万亿，具身智能的故事席卷产业圈，在机器人赛道中，家电巨头美的是不可忽视的存在，甚至砸下重金押注这条赛道。
美的集团董事长兼总裁方洪波还一度表示，美的下半年要坚定布局机器人、新能源等次核心业务。前期结果上，上半年，其机器人业务营收增速跑赢家电主业。库卡也在业内拿到一张靠前的座位票。然而，现实吊诡的地方在于，火热的行业风口，又的确暂时还没有转化成集团层面坚实的业绩底盘。
万亿市场的宏大叙事之下，美的机器人业务仍处在增收不增利的阶段，距离成为真正能抗盘的第二增长曲线，还有不少现实关卡等待跨越。
尤其是，美的机器人板块收入保持高增，但体量偏小、毛利承压，难以对冲家电主业的增长压力。公司的工业机器人与面向家用的人形机器人战线并存，家电厂商即便手握资金与零部件技术积累，把行业风口兑现成实实在在的利润，仍是美的的一大挑战。
01 美的机器人呈现了两面相
公开资料显示，截至2026年6月，集团机器人使用密度已经超过每万名员工750台，如果翻开美的2026年上半年财报，机器人与自动化板块呈现出鲜明的两面性。
一方面，板块实现营收166.21亿元，同比增长10.27%，对比智能家居业务4.27%的增速，增长势能十分突出，是集团内部最具想象空间的增量赛道之一。
尽管美的该业务呈现了光鲜的收入增长，但另外一个细节是，该板块的盈利能力却并非完美无瑕。据财报，该业务毛利率同比下滑1.86个百分点至20.9%，收入向上，利润没有同步跟进，陷入增收不增利的现实泥潭 。
进一步放到美的集团大盘当中，机器人业务的体量短板会更加直观。目前机器人与自动化板块整体仅占集团总营收的6.39%，规模尚不足以成为成熟的第二曲线，还承担不起托举集团业绩的重任。
显然，这份局面的背后是一组结构性矛盾：新业务体量还没做大，传统家电主业又面临不小的下行压力。
家电大件品类集体进入缩量周期，作为美的基本盘的空调表现尤为明显。公开零售数据显示，2026上半年空调零售量4096万台，同比下降13.1%；零售总额1221亿元，同比下滑15.9%，其中6月单月同比已经跌到‑20.7%。
而主业承压传导至集团整体报表，2026上半年美的实现营收2610.52亿元，同比增长3.55%；归母净利润264.46亿元，同比小幅增长1.66%；扣非归母净利润195.95亿元，同比大幅下降25.31%。
集团营收保持微弱上行，但扣非利润大幅回落，增长动能明显减弱。机器人业务虽然增速亮眼，但受限于规模与毛利表现，只能充当集团品牌多元化培育的角色，还无法对冲家电主业的压力。亮眼增长背后，业务内部、家电大厂跨界做机器人的结构性压力，也随之显现。
02 具身智能混战下，多条腿走路是不是悖论
据悉，美的机器人主要分为工业机器人、自研人形机器人、家用服务机器人、物流医疗自动化机器人等。其中，营收、出货、商业化贡献层面，工业机器人是重要撑盘主力；面向家庭的人形机器人还没有形成大量对外销售的主营业务。只是就整个行业而言，人形机器人抢入口，工业机器人抢利润的趋势十分突出。
所以在美的多条腿走路过程中，工业机器人（含库卡KUKA）更为显眼。客观而言，就未来的前景而言，上述面向家用的人形机器人和面向泛行业的工业机器人是两大重点，即便如此，美的所处的外部环境都并不轻松。
就人形机器人赛道而言，时下已经呈现寡头化格局，SAG机构上半年统计数据显示，智元机器人上半年出货8400台，占据全球44%市场份额；宇树机器人出货5900台，拿下31%的全球份额，两家头部企业合计包揽全球超七成市场。
赛道尾部中小厂商单家上半年出货均未破千台，头部与腰部玩家之间的规模鸿沟持续拉大。对比行业火热的对外出货竞赛，美的人形机器人要参与的竞争十分激烈。
倘若视线转回贡献主要收入的工业机器人赛道，国内市场内卷已经进入白热化，美的机器人的亮点与压力同时存在。
亮点在于，MIR睿工业统计数据显示，库卡工业机器人国内上半年出货量超过18000台，同比增长超19%，国内市场份额达到9.7%，攀升至行业第二位；在300kg以上重载机器人领域，国内市场份额突破50%，产品广泛落地汽车部件、储能电池、船舶、航空航天等高附加值场景 。
可整个国内工业机器人市场高手林立。2025年，埃斯顿、发那科、库卡三家企业年销量突破3万台，汇川、ABB出货突破2万台，爱普生、埃夫特、安川、珞石等企业年销量均超过一万台。到2026上半年，埃斯顿再次拿下国内工业机器人全品牌出货量榜首，成为首个单季度销量破万台的自主品牌，连续六个季度保持领先，连续八年位居国产品牌出货量第一，对美的形成领先优势。
激烈竞争的大环境之下，家电玩家跨界做机器人，其优势是几十年来的一整套工业化能力。但并非简单把制造能力复制过去就可以获得成功。因为家电制造沉淀的电机、控制硬件能力可以复用在机器人产品之上，而B端工业机器人面对的工厂客户、项目渠道、交付服务体系，和面向普通消费者的家电零售实际上割裂。
美的自有工厂可以作为内部试验场景，但向外拓展工业客户，无法复用遍布全国的家电经销商网络，对外拓客成本也存在。
盈利周期上同样存在冲突。依托于大规模的渠道网点，家电业务周转快、现金流稳定。工业机器人项目前期投入高，项目交付周期漫长，还要持续承担售后维保成本。
美的收购库卡之后，耗费多年时间才帮助库卡日渐走向规模化发展，这种长周期重投入业务，短期很难完全匹配家电主业的业绩规模节奏。
还有一点压力值得注意，家电企业布局机器人，一边要寻找集团第二增长曲线，一边又要和集团内部其他业务共享集团整体研发资金等资源，这也是美的必须直面的现实处境。今年以来美的集团新获得专利授权至少1651个，较去年同期减少了19.11%。结合公司2026年中报财务数据，今年上半年公司在研发方面投入了84.67亿元，同比减3.41%。
反过来讲，美的距离市场期待的具身智能大厂还是有距离的。而要真正看清它的处境，需要跳出产品硬件本身，回到商业化利润这个核心命题上。
03 压力不在产品定义，在于如何把风口转商业化利润
目前，多个行业机构的预测，都给机器人赛道铺就宏大的想象空间。
菜鸟集团联合罗兰贝格发布《2026年机器人白皮书》做出判断，全球机器人市场将迎来十年黄金爆发期，市场规模从2025年约4000亿元，扩容至2035年的21200亿元，十年体量增长超5倍。
资本层面同样热度不减，2026年国内具身智能领域融资总额已经突破1000亿元，拿到融资的具身模型公司数量超过140家，为去年同期的1.5倍。
行业浪潮之中，美的也拿出真金白银的投入。今年3月，美的宣布未来三年将投入600亿元深耕AI与具身智能等领域。
目前，美的的零部件端同样有所进展，2026上半年美的精密减速机出货2.6万台，重载伺服电机出货5.8万台，同比实现大幅增长，自研核心零部件产能与市场认可度持续提升。
硬件、供应链、资金投入层面，美的具备不错的基础，产品定义自然并不是最大阻碍。不过，美的上半年机器人与自动化业务增收不增利的现象表明，资金与自研供应链只能解决产品有无，却不能直接破解市场竞争、项目交付带来的盈利难题。
具体的难题可以拆解成两层，一层是当下利润转化的现实堵点，另一层是长远市场渗透的重重考验，两者共同影响商业化的最终成色。
家电主业受上游原材料、消费需求影响承受成本压力，以工业机器人为例，工业机器人板块的困境来自白热化的市场竞争。新时达在半年报中就曾提到，行业激烈角逐态势并未缓和，价格竞争叠加技术迭代持续加速。
来自高工机器人统计显示，2025上半年工业机器人行业价格战持续升级。面向汽车、3C大客户，SCARA机器人单台价格下探至万元水平，一年时间降幅达到50%；6kg负载六轴工业机器人价格来到两万多元，部分协作机器人产品底价已经低于两万元。
考虑到具身智能处于方兴未艾的阶段，价格厮杀的趋势，到2026年乃至后期要出现彻底明显转向恐怕并非易事。
产品端库卡依旧在补齐矩阵，2026上半年多款新品落地，包括可承载1500kg的第二代KR TITAN ultra长距离重载搬运机器人、新增25kg/35kg负载型号的KR CYBERTECH系列机器人，还有极致窄通道的潜伏式叉车KMP 1000i‑PT omniMove等产品。不过，美的机器人与自动化业务毛利率能否迎来改善依旧尚待观察。
再看面向家用的人形机器人，美的其实已经跑出不错的演示效果。
升级款超人形机器人“美罗U”已经上岗洗衣机高端园区，稳定运行超两个月，累计完成螺钉锁附超过10万颗；面向家庭与商业场景的第二代全人形机器人“美拉 X2”，能够独立完成叠毛巾、餐桌收纳、沙发整理等家庭任务，场景作业成功率超过95%，一定程度上代表美的人形机器人迈入民用实用化的测试阶段。
但这些成果，不等于商业市场的大规模落地。
放眼整个具身智能产业，宇树市值腰斩、部分具身智能供应链企业上市之后破发，市场风向已经发生变化。行业已经从单纯追捧概念，切换到商业化验证阶段，企业真实收入、客户复购价值，成为市场评判项目的核心标尺。
还有一个细节是，在今年9月11日2026 Inclusion·外滩大会“具身CEO产业论坛”上，多位行业专家提出，未来一两年，机器人落地增速最快的会是工业、物流、康复这类生产力场景；机器人会优先进入环境封闭、任务链条短、异常状况少的场景，再逐步渗透普通大众市场。
因此，家用人形机器人距离走进千家万户还有漫长周期，工业机器人又深陷价格竞争泥潭。综合来看，想要依靠具身智能机器人托举集团整体业绩，短期并不现实。
回过头来看，具身智能的风口能够给企业带来故事，却不会直接送来利润。
机器人能不能成长为美的更有分量的第二曲线增长，在于能不能跨过商业化这道坎。这其实也是摆在所有入局机器人赛道的家电厂商面前的共同考题。

articles.title: 游戏公司退未成年人充值多退3万 母亲拒还用AI伪造证据 法官识破当庭训诫
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，据央视新闻报道，陕西西安雁塔法院近日审结一起不当得利案件，一名母亲在收到游戏公司多退的三万余元款项后拒不归还，还使用AI合成虚假通话录音提交法庭，试图证明对方已同意免予退款，最终不仅败诉，还被当庭训诫。
据了解，未成年人小涵在游戏平台累计充值约5万元，其母亲刘某就此起诉游戏公司。
经广州法院调解，双方约定游戏公司按30%比例退款15695.4元。工作人员操作失误，实际转账49323元，多出33627.6元。
游戏公司发现差错后，多次联系刘某，要求返还多退资金，但遭到拒绝，随后向雁塔法院提起诉讼。
庭审中，刘某辩称游戏公司已电话同意不用退钱，并提交一段通话录音作为证据。
法官当庭核查，要求拨打录音中的号码，同时通知相关律师到庭核实。经过声音比对与多方查证，确认录音并非该律师原声。面对证据，刘某承认录音是自己利用AI技术伪造。
承办法官介绍，即便钱款源于游戏公司操作失误，刘某没有合法依据占有这笔资金，满足不当得利的构成要件，依然负有返还义务。法院最终判决刘某返还 33627.6元及对应利息。
鉴于刘某当庭认错道歉，伪造证据尚未造成严重后果，法院未对其罚款、拘留，依法予以严厉口头训诫。
法官同时提醒，诉讼中伪造证据，法院会根据情节轻重，分别适用训诫、罚款、拘留，情节严重还将追究刑事责任，AI技术不能成为虚构证据、妨害司法的工具。

articles.title: 尘封87年终于解密！GPT-6一夜破解二战时德军无线电密码
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，过去顶尖专家耗费数年才能尝试的历史密码解密，如今普通人搭配AI模型，一夜之间就有机会完成。
二战德军恩尼格玛密码机，当年拥有多达103万万亿种加密组合，曾被视作难以攻破的军事通信工具。
日前，一封编号MVUEH、1941年7月10日东线战场发出的德国陆军战地无线电密电，被GPT-6 Astra成功破译，引发业界轰动。
完成解密的并非专业密码学家，而是纽约彭博的产品开发教练卡特·莱芬，他没有密码学专业背景，仅把解密任务交给GPT-6 Astra，偶尔简单提示模型继续推演，随后休息。
GPT-6 Astra并非单纯猜测文字，它自主检索同一天已经破译的电报，锁定地名Rosenow（罗泽诺）作为破解突破口，密码学上称为crib（已知明文线索）。
模型自行编写代码，搭建恩尼格玛模拟器与炸弹机（Bombe）程序，批量测试转子顺序、环位、插线板等数百万种密钥组合，利用恩尼格玛“加密后字母不会等于原字母”的固有缺陷快速排除无效组合，最终找到正确密钥。
解密后的报文大意：请指示行军路线，我在罗泽诺，立刻电台回复。
解密文本还保留当年发报士兵笔误，将BITTE错写成BTTE，该细节由独立密码学家弗罗德·维耶鲁德核验，确认解密结果真实有效。
受这次成功案例启发，网络安全工程师卡特·丘奇使用同款GPT-6 Astra模型，破解了一封1809年意大利官员写给拿破仑麾下将军的古老密信。
AI识别图片内符号，寻找部分密钥，依靠模拟退火算法持续调整，仅花费6小时完成解密，密文记载部队位置信息，极大压缩了耗时与人力成本。

articles.title: 深兰科技发布自研影视智能体操作系统DFAgent
articles.text: 36氪获悉，10月19日，深兰科技旗下深视星影发布自研影视智能体操作系统DFAgent，并签约院线科幻电影《气候战争》。据介绍，DFAgent定位院线长片全链条AI基础设施，由JEV System One决策中枢、DeepBlue Film Model影视大模型、全球化内容数据飞轮三部分构成。系统还搭建AI数字剧组，用数十个Agent模拟制片、编剧、导演、摄影、剪辑、宣发等岗位，并设置剧情、美术、视频时序和商业潜力四道质检。

articles.title: Secondhand Stress: How Stressful Disclosures Affect Psychosocial Wellbeing in Online Graduate Admissions Communities
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22657v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Online communities provide spaces for individuals navigating stressful life transitions to disclose difficulties and seek peer support. Yet encountering others' distress may also have psychosocial implications for community members. Drawing on stress crossover theory, we examine how engagement with peer distress during graduate admissions is associated with subsequent psychosocial expression and participation, and whether similar associations extend through downstream interactions. We analyze 171,981 posts and 1,130,413 comments from two Reddit communities across three admissions cycles, using propensity-score stratification and baseline-adjusted comparisons. Users who engaged with distress disclosures during application preparation subsequently exhibited higher classifier-estimated anxiety, depression, and stress expression, alongside greater commenting activity and lexical redundancy. These associations recurred across admissions cycles, while no significant psychosocial associations were detected among downstream respondents interacting with previously exposed users. Our findings highlight how greater distress-related expression can coexist with continued community participation, while distinguishing direct engagement with distress disclosures from subsequent social contact. We discuss implications for designing online communities that preserve opportunities for self-disclosure and peer support while remaining attentive to the experiences of those encountering distress-related content.

articles.title: 腾讯AI管家Marvis原生版上架银河麒麟！适配飞腾、华为海思麒麟等国产CPU
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，今日，麒麟软件宣布，腾讯旗下AI管家Marvis原生版正式上架银河麒麟软件商店，用户现可直接下载安装。
据了解，Marvis由腾讯应用宝团队打造，定位为操作系统级个人AI管家，能够连接本地文件、应用软件及跨端设备，为用户提供一站式AI办公体验。
与传统对话式AI不同，Marvis不仅能够回答问题，还可以直接调用电脑中的应用和功能，帮助用户完成实际操作。
功能方面，Marvis支持软件下载与调用、电脑设置与体检、文档图片查找处理、知识检索、任务自动化、跨端远程控制等多项能力，覆盖日常办公中的多种使用场景。
值得一提的是，此次上架的Marvis原生版提供X86-64和ARM64双架构版本，兼容多款国产处理器。
其中，国产CPU平台覆盖飞腾、鲲鹏、海光、兆芯、华为海思麒麟等品牌，同时支持Intel、AMD等主流计算平台。
麒麟软件表示，此次上架银河麒麟软件商店，Marvis团队围绕银河麒麟桌面环境开展了专项适配与测试验证。
此次适配也意味着，搭载不同架构、不同品牌处理器的银河麒麟终端用户，均有机会使用Marvis提供的AI办公功能，进一步拓展国产操作系统的AI应用生态。

articles.title: ToMStories: Interpreting Theory-of-Mind in Synthetic Narratives
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22632v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Understanding people often requires inferring what they feel or want from how they behave rather than from what they state outright. We ask whether language models can make these inferences, and how they do so. We introduce Theory-of-Mind Stories (ToMStories), an evaluation dataset of ~6,000 short synthetically generated narrative vignettes, each paired with a multiple-choice or open-ended question about a character's emotion, fear, motivation, or emotional wound. These psychological states are conveyed implicitly (showing), explicitly (telling), or with conflict between dialogue and description. Evaluating thirteen open-weight models (1B-72B parameters), we find that the largest models match humans on multiple choice but not open-ended questions. Our analyses point to simplifications models make in both interpretation and generation of implicit psychological states, indicating that synthetic data can help us understand how models perform interpretation, but likely overestimates how well models interpret humans.

articles.title: 用阿里当基座，腾讯混元实现了“小RSI”
articles.text:
（本文作者为 字母AI，钛媒体经授权发布）
文 | 字母AI
自Hy4 Preview发布以来，它最受人关注的地方就是全链路RSI，这也是腾讯混元首个自己全程参与研发的模型。通过全链路RSI能给模型带来大幅性能提升。
不到两个月后，混元的Frontier团队发布了Terminal-RSI。这次更有意思，它能通过RSI，让一个模型超越自己原本的框架，实现自己本来不具备的能力。
就像你有一台微波炉，它的功能是给食物加热。加入Terminal-RSI之后，不仅能让微波炉原本的加热功能效果更好，你还能用它来看电视、听歌、打游戏。
以Terminal-Bench 4.0为例，这是当下最严格的Agent终端实操基准测试集之一。论文使用的基座模型，原本不具备跑这个测试集的能力，也就是0%。
通过Terminal-RSI，这个基座模型能达到19.84%的分数，和GPT-5.6 Terra、Gemini 3.8 Flash齐平。
还有一个细节也挺好玩的，论文所使用的基座模型是Qwen3.8-27B，腾讯阿里也因此在RSI上达成了“合作”。
论文自己也承认，这套RSI只在一个27B的模型上跑过，没有在更大的模型上验证，也只有三次评测、没有独立训练种子，所以它放到Hy4这种大参数量模型上会怎样，还能否实现RSI，目前都还没有答案。
Terminal-RSI是个啥？
Terminal-RSI所训练的叫做终端Agent。它跟普通的Agent不太一样，混元团队给它一个沙盒和一份任务说明，它要像工程师一样在命令行里查看仓库、安装依赖、修改代码、运行测试，最后看沙盒里的状态能不能通过验证。
论文表示，要想实现RSI通常会有两个难题。
第一个是反馈太慢。论文表示，在整个训练过程中，平均交互回合数在50到117之间浮动，明明第二步就错了，结果只有到最后才知道对不对。
第二个是没办法细致地区分对与错。论文提到，验证器里11条检查过了9条，但是这个结果，却很难在终端判定里体现出来。
就像打游戏，打掉水晶才算赢。你杀一个小兵给一份钱，很多人不推水晶、专门刷小兵，刷得是不亦乐乎，而且最后评分也很高，但问题是水晶不掉就赢不了游戏啊。
Terminal-RSI的核心目的，就是为了解决这两件事。
Terminal-RSI的流程是这样的：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2，两个“重写 + 精炼”的循环，基座用的是前文提到的Qwen3.8-27B，最终产物叫Terminal-RSI-27B。
第一步RSR（Recursive Self-Rewrite，递归自我重写）只更新actor，也就是真正去执行任务的策略。
它的做法是：模型在各种不同的harness里尝试任务，只保留通过完整验证的成功轨迹。然后由模型自己充当规划者，把成功过程提炼成一份操作手册（runbook）。
这时候，有一个专门负责审查的Agent，它只看题面和手册，检查格式、产物以及有没有把验证器答案或标准解泄漏进去。
通过审查后，模型拿着手册在全新的沙盒里重新做一遍，只有重做依然通过验证、且没有泄漏的轨迹才会留下。
最后做监督微调时，手册和审查对话都会被抹掉，只留下动作序列。
RSR就像你打游戏开荒，死了八百回，终于有一把通了关。然后你把那把的录像导出来，天天回放，把每一步操作硬背成肌肉记忆。
下次再进本，你手自己就动了，脑子里全是通关那把的走位，想都不用想。
这就是RSR的本质，把“成功那一次”抠出来，写成笔记，照着死磕。打分的人没换，裁判也没换，规则还是那套规则，唯一的变数只有正在闯关的你。你抄的是你自己的满分卷子。
第二步RPR（Recursive Policy-Refine，递归策略精炼）则是actor和critic一起上的强化学习（PPO）。
论文强调，重写之后，actor偏好的动作变了，它会遇到的历史也跟着变，原来的critic就不一定估得准。如果直接把critic重置，等于丢掉已经学到的“什么样的局面更接近成功”。
可话又说回来了，如果原样继承又不校准，旧的估计误差会混进优势值里。
比如你练着练着换了套新打法，旧录像这时候就不好使了，得请个分析师（critic）帮你分析，下一步应该怎么走才能过关。
但问题来了，分析师脑子里那套数据库还是你旧打法的，你现在这打法他根本看不懂。
RPR的招数是你先原地站桩别动，让分析师拿你最近的战绩单独重新练4轮，让它理解你的新打法和新规则。等分析师回过味来了，你再跟分析师一起上分，边打边调。也就是所谓的“带着教练一起热身”。
那么结果到底怎样？
Qwen3.8这个只有27B参数量的小模型，只练了两轮，它在Terminal-Bench 2.1上的得分，就从51.7%升到86.5%，在Terminal-Bench 4.0版本上从完全做不出来（0%）升到了19.8%，四个测试的平均分从20.7%升到50.6%，翻了一倍多。
Hy Frontier回到混元主线
论文的一作有三位，分别是Hy Frontier的两个实习生杨竣尧和李宗夏，以及位于西雅图的腾讯研究科学家史玉成。
而这三个人此前也合作过，论文名为《T1：面向长时程任务的终端智能体强化学习》（T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks）。
这篇论文相当于是Terminal-RSI的“前传”，讲的是怎么用强化学习把一个大模型练成“会真的在Linux终端里干活”的智能体。
姚顺雨来之前，腾讯做基础研究的主力是2016年成立的AI Lab，姚星牵头筹建，2017年请来机器学习学者张潼出任首任负责人。
然而根据《晚点》的报道，张潼带着很高的期待来，以为腾讯海量的业务和数据能成为学界拿不到的研究资源，结果进来之后数据依然拿不到，研究只能闭门造车，两年后失望离开。
此后AI Lab负责人换成张正友，2024年6月再换成蒋杰。
混元同样也是如此，2023年立项时项目组连一块GPU都没有，最后是从广告部门匀来了2000张，一半给预训练、一半给后训练。
首任负责人是张正友，他的研究方向是计算机视觉。第二任负责人是蒋杰，长期负责腾讯广告平台的产品技术管理工作，长期做大数据平台，擅长广告推荐。但是几乎都没碰过强化学习。
到了2025年中，团队转向打榜。受访者对《晚点》表示，“活照常干，但大家心里都清楚，这么干下去不行”。
直到姚顺雨加入混元，一切才有了转变。在6月的访谈里，姚顺雨提到，今天的AI有三块，Foundation、产品和Frontier，要构建一个均衡的“三角形组织”，因为“在我们今天所做的前沿探索不够多”。
旧的研究机构“离模型太远”，模型团队又“光顾着追榜单”。
姚顺雨的解法是把研究直接搬进模型部门里面。AI Lab并入大语言模型部，原来的研究员成为其中的Frontier方向，和预训练、后训练、评估、Infra同属一个部门、同一条汇报线。
过去的做法是研究在AI Lab、产品和模型在别处，两边靠协调沟通。现在的做法是Frontier与主模型团队放在同一个框里，层级也被压成“姚顺雨—方向负责人—研究员/实习生”三层。
Frontier至此开始，也不再是一个独立于混元的实验室，7月基础模型部成立后，它又被收进同一个部门，都向姚顺雨汇报。
虽然Frontier理论上“不设KPI、不规定课题”，但这条终端Agent加强化学习的研究线也不是那种“漫无边际式”的研究。
2025年底，腾讯混元开始重点跟进AI编程，姚顺雨因此搭出了一个全集团共用的强化学习基础设施，让各业务能在上面训练自己的模型，再把数据回流给混元。T1和Terminal-RSI做的，正是终端里的长程任务与强化学习。
再加上Hy 4 Preview本来就强调全链路RSI，因此这次的Terminal-RSI，就是Frontier对混元主力产品线的一次补强。
混元的研究和产品，不再分家。
Hy4未来可期
Hy4 Preview的全链路RSI可以细分为4个环节，数据策略、训练方法、评估体系、底层算子。前文提到，Terminal-RSI的RSR和RPR，前者所对应的就是数据策略这一环，而RPR提升的则偏向于训练方法。
Hy4底座再强，终端长时程任务上的“完整成功”轨迹照样稀缺，而RSR能自己给自己造高质量训练数据，还顺手隔离了benchmark污染。
所以它对Hy4的意义是：把“偶尔能做对”固化成“稳定会做”，尤其在调试、系统管理这种需要多步推理加工具调用的活上。
真正的大头在RPR，它几乎完美符合Hy4所有的需求。
前文提到，RPR是“带着教练一起热身”，以适应新环境、新打法、新规则。自姚顺雨进入混元之后，模型主打的就是上下文，而这也意味着模型经常要面对各种新类型的任务。
很多大模型的评分很高，可它在实际完成任务上，总是差点意思。
因为骗分这活儿，本身就是个技术活。OpenAI的报告里就曾提到，模型越强，越会“演”。中间步骤、前置条件、中间产物它全都能给你搞对，一路刷出大量通过的检查点，看着跟真干成了似的，可最后那个要命的关键结果就是不对。
不推掉水晶就赢不了游戏。而姚顺雨又是个不关注榜单成绩，只在乎模型能不能完成任务的人。
2026年1月的时候，姚顺雨评价DeepSeek，说：“DeepSeek做得比较好的一点是，他们可能没有那么关注榜单的数字。DeepSeek可能会更注重：第一，什么是正确的事情；第二，什么是自己能体验出好或者不好的。”
弱模型想骗分还没那本事，Hy4则是强模型，它要是演起来，只会更像真的，那刷出来的过程分也只会更凶，所以这套“成功优先、过程分永远压不过满分”的规则，专治它这种病。

articles.title: 苹果Mac也能玩《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》！M4 MacBook Air跑出90帧
articles.text:
快科技10月19日消息，近日，一项名为MacNativeGames的开源项目引发游戏玩家关注。开发者liyong成功让任天堂旗下游戏《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》在苹果Mac电脑上运行，并公布了搭载M4芯片的MacBook Air实机演示画面。
根据开发者公布的数据，《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》在M4 MacBook Air和M4 Mac mini上完成了运行测试，经过着色器缓存预热后，游戏帧率可以达到约90FPS。
据项目介绍，由于任天堂Switch和苹果Apple Silicon芯片均采用ARM64架构，开发者利用这一共同点，让游戏原有的大量ARM64指令直接在苹果芯片上执行，同时对系统服务和图形接口进行适配。
在图形渲染方面，项目将Switch使用的NVN图形指令转换至苹果Metal接口，并采用Metal 4及MetalFX等技术，支持2K画面输出、图像放大和帧插值等功能。
通过这一方案，游戏能够减少传统CPU指令模拟带来的部分性能开销，为苹果芯片运行Switch游戏提供了另一种实现方式。
目前，MacNativeGames项目已经在GitHub平台开源，支持《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》1.0.0、1.1.2、1.2.1和1.4.3版本，同时支持键盘操作以及Xbox、PlayStation等游戏手柄。
按照开发者提供的说明，Mac版本需要搭载Apple Silicon芯片、运行macOS 26或更新系统，建议至少配备16GB内存。用户需要自行提供合法获得的游戏文件及相关密钥，再通过项目脚本构建应用。
值得一提的是，该项目近期更新速度较快。截至10月19日，开发者已经加入iPhone和iPad的实验性支持，并在iPhone 14及搭载A16芯片的iPad上完成了初步游玩测试。

articles.title: On the Position Bias of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Study
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.22807v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Recent studies have shown that position bias remains a critical vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), undermining both the integrity of multiple-choice evaluations and the reliability of retrieval-augmented generation. However, existing understanding of this phenomenon is largely derived from studies with limited model coverage and English-centric benchmarks, leaving the behavior of frontier models and diverse languages underexplored. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of position bias across model scales ranging from billion-level to trillion-level parameters, covering both multiple-choice and multi-document tasks in five languages. Our experiments reveal that while position bias remains noticeable in small-scale models and Non-English languages, increasing model scale and employing standard Chain-of-Thought prompting significantly mitigate this issue. Moreover, we demonstrate that emerging \emph{thinking models} with extended reasoning capabilities are nearly immune to position bias, suggesting a costly but general approach toward resolving this vulnerability.
